The claim office hands the notice to whoever is standing there, and you are standing there. The second crew are not villains; they filed in time, in the only window they had, on a filing system that ate both.
build.payoff: deliver the reinstatement to the second crew yourself: Voss rep +4, the second crew's rep +2, one codex line ("The system ate both. One hull carried the paper."). Refusing is honored: the office files your refusal, and the second crew learns from the wire, colder.
build.seam: one-off keyed to the pers_voss_suspended seen-flag; delivery via numbered encounter; codex overlay

build.title: The Meteor Fishery
build.trigger: always present during meteor_shower seasons; the fishery is a fixed net-rig on the surge path
build.sees: Crews have strung foil net-lines across the meteor surge path like a river salmon run — stones hit the nets, sparks walk the lines, a skiff hauls the catch. A shingle sign reads the day's take in stones and one honest loss count ("NETS: 3. METEORS: EVERYTHING ELSE").
build.payoff: You may string ONE net-line of your own (capped, licensed for the season — the license is 40 cr and a signature); your line catches seeded stones on the public schedule. Unlicensed lines get cut by the fishery, politely, once.
build.seam: weatherMeteors slot-book read + prop line + a capped yield flag in story.flags

build.title: Hollow Station's Backlog
build.trigger: proximity to the suspended DMC claim office wreck; gates minSectorTier 2; cooldownS 3600
build.sees: the claim office still queues paper into a chute that goes nowhere — 22 cycles of filings (amb_drift_claims' backlog) flutter out a broken seam and drift in slow paper-snow. Two live crews are racing to physically re-file the same rock's claim at the one working stamp. Both offer you carriage. The paper is real, the race is real, the rock is one rock.
build.payoff: carry either crew's filing (their rep) or file BOTH and let the stamp's order decide (the office's own law, honored bitterly); the winning claim's beacon lights and the losing crew becomes a recurring rival contact.
build.seam: numbered selfRegistered encounter; claim paper as light debris props; claimableBodies beacon on the outcome; rival contact via story.flags

build.title: The Deck Chair
build.where: sector_dione_lane, a seeded empty patch off the lane
build.trigger: first proximity; uniqueOnce
build.sees: A patch of nothing — no rocks, no traffic, no salvage — with one welded deck chair bolted to a bare plate, aimed at the sector's best view of its star. A small placard: "RESERVED FOR WHOEVER NEEDS IT. WIPE IT DOWN."
build.payoff: A rest stop the game never marks: hull heat bleeds at double rate while parked here; wiping the chair (a scan interaction) leaves it clean for the next pilot and chalks your initials on the plate's underside, which nobody is supposed to find.
build.seam: zone record (sectorZones, no presence) + one prop; heat exemption via the same predicate pattern as SP3-026

build.title: Dorin's Dead Drop
build.trigger: after the player has paid 3+ law fines (stat gate), a blank-channel listing offers "clean paper, dirty provenance, one drop, one visit"
build.sees: the drop holds pages cut from a Concord seal-log — which fines were pre-written, which inspections were scheduled before the ships were. Filecleaver Dorin's marginalia argues with the stamps in a neat, furious hand. The hunters' exchange pays for the pages too, and its scanner sweep is on a clock you can read.
build.payoff: deliver the pages to the Archive (records restored, standing +4) or sell to the exchange (credits, and within the week one pre-written fine arrives for you, personally — the ledger is honest about what it does). Codex page "Pre-Written".
build.seam: numbered encounter with a two-outcome handoff; seal-log prose as codex overlay; the fine event keyed to outcome flag

build.title: The Hand-Me-Down Route
build.trigger: offered by a retiring hauler regular after the player has flown 10+ deliveries in the sector; uniqueOnce
build.sees: She sells you her route — a sealed envelope of berths, timings and contacts, thirty years of it — for her retirement fund, exact change, no haggling. One page is torn out. "One of these berths will cheat you. Finding which one is the tuition. I never did."
build.payoff: A real route bonus (queue priority at the listed berths) plus the seeded cheat berth, which stings once and then becomes your best contact when you catch it; she retires to a berth you can visit, and asks how the route is doing.
build.seam: numbered dock encounter + berth-priority flags read by docking; cheat berth seeded from programSeed

build.title: The Confessional Booth
build.trigger: first dock after the player has killed any non-hostile hull (moral memory)
build.sees: a Choir acolyte runs a side booth labeled "DISPOSAL OF GUILT, PROFESSIONAL." For a flat tithe they process the confession — not absolution, filing: "Guilt is a record with no filing cabinet. We are the cabinet. It will be read back to you once, at the end, and then it is ours." The read-back actually happens, verbatim, at the player's ending screen.
build.payoff: flag `guilt_filed`; the ending screen appends one read-back line; Choir standing +1 (they honor accurate filing above all).
build.seam: moral-memory read (src/systems/moralMemory.js) + barContacts booth + ending-screen line
hones: (b) absorbs SP1-165's Heard/Weighted/Absolved voice; lands as a late letter per A H-25
(c) One Choir liturgy, two sacraments — the booth files in the same receipt grammar the buoy absolves in; deliver the read-back as a late mail letter (ending files dirty).

build.title: The One-Digit Writ
build.trigger: first bounty the player earns over 200 cr (stat gate); once
build.sees: the board posts TAG 7713 — one digit off the Tessera's own tag, 7714 (trap_bounty_tag's joke made structural). Hunters in the sector scan you twice, hover, and move on with a disappointed air.
build.payoff: meeting the real 7713 (a seeded quarry from QUARRY_NAMES) is a real encounter — they know why you're staring. Two hulls, one digit, one drink at the nearest bar.
build.seam: bounty-id formatting hook reading the player's tag + one seeded encounter keyed to the flag; QUARRY_NAMES in src/data/bountyHunters.js

build.title: The Pigeon Day
build.trigger: the pigeon_coop roaming story rides a convoy through the player's sector (the roaming runtime binding already exists); proximity to the receiving berth
build.sees: the coop carrier docks, the loft's new keeper signs, twelve racers are released for the ceremonial first flight — and the birds, who remember the OLD loft, cross the entire sector in a tight line and land on the old one, which is a welded-shut derelict. The keeper watches, then writes "twelve for twelve" in the log anyway.
build.payoff: codex page "Twelve For Twelve"; the old loft gains one lamp that burns thereafter (the keeper feeds the birds there on market days).
build.seam: roaming-story binding + one lamp via lampChannels on a worldOneOffs prop; codex overlay
hones: (a) the birds' crossing is a vignette column of small props on the verified column motion, landing = props park at the derelict; no new flocking system

build.title: The Falling Anchor
build.trigger: permanent fixture with sim-time decay; state persists per save
build.sees: A capital wreck is falling — slowly, over weeks — toward the gravity well of a dead moon. Each visit it is visibly lower against the moon's face, and the salvage on it is visibly re-priced by risk. The belt has started a pool on the day it hits.
build.payoff: A deadline as a landscape: early salvage is cheap and safe, late salvage pays triple; on impact day, the whole sector hears it, and the site remains as a crater landmark.
build.seam: persistent prop with simTime-based drift (asteroidMotion precedent); impact event via news:publish; pool as a station bet (economy)
hones: (a) absorb SP3-126's reentry fire-line for impact day; the betting pool pays pocket change; the crater persists
(b) absorbs SP3-126's reentry fire-line; the pool pays pocket change; the crater persists

build.title: Comet Perihelion
build.where: sector_helios_prime, then one gate-neighbor per season (ceres_belt, tethys_junction, vesta_forge)
build.trigger: sim-time window — every 40-day year, days 15–17; the spaceBackground comet's authored perihelion pass
build.sees: the L6 background comet (already in `src/render/spaceBackground.js`) drops from sky depth to near-plane parallax for one day, tail streaming anti-sunward, and visibly sheds three real debris stones into the sector on the middle day. Intercept a stone before it sublimates on day 17.
build.payoff: plus small bonus (one volatiles pickup per stone) and a codex entry if all three are caught.
build.seam: `spaceBackground.js` cometInterval/composition knobs already exist in `src/data/sectorVisualProfiles.js`; the three stones use the finite-slot pattern of `src/systems/weatherMeteors.js`.

(b) comet anchor; absorbs SP1-068's road; SP1-123 races it; one window, three legs
(c) The comet anchor: road (SP1-068), race (SP1-123) and stone-fall read as one event on the perihelion window — one canon comet, three human responses.

build.title: The Shadow Ring
build.where: sector_eunomia_gulf, one flat-faced rock off the trade lane
build.trigger: pure geometry — once per sector day your hull's shadow can land inside a hand-painted target ring on the rock face; no prompt, no marker
build.sees: A faded painted ring on a rock face, with a tiny dead lamp at its center. Fly so your shadow fills the ring at the right minute and the lamp lights for the day. On your tenth hit, fresh paint appears under the ring overnight: "STILL GOT IT."
build.payoff: A pure-flying ritual with no reward but the lamp, the paint, and the quiet bragging rights of knowing why the lamp is sometimes on.
build.seam: shadow-geometry predicate (player pos vs sun bearing math) + one lamp channel + a hit counter in story.flags

build.title: The Half a Conversation
build.trigger: hail the buoy after SP2-029's flag; uniqueOnce
build.sees: the buoy plays one side of an old argument; the other party's turns are carrier-silence, and the pauses are exactly long enough to answer into.
build.payoff: codex page; the most uncomfortable silence in the game.
build.seam: band audio rows (bandpass/noise recipes) + flag gate + codex overlay

build.title: Origin Unspecified
build.trigger: the player buys any canister whose provenance reads "origin unspecified" (the amb_sec6_air vocabulary) and is later scanned clean
build.sees: the scan finds nothing — but the receipt the scanner prints carries one extra line it never prints: "PROVENANCE: HONORED." Somewhere, a relay the player cannot see files the sale as complete.
build.payoff: flag `origin_honored`; the next Quiet fence greets the player by the canister's contents, not their name. Codex page "The Tell" — 'origin unspecified' is the tell, and now the player has passed it.
build.seam: provenance field read on scan receipt + one comms line; fence greeting variant in the fence contact copy path

build.title: The Insurance Frame
build.trigger: offered while a seeded scrapper convoy is en route (wire posting); seasonal predicate
build.sees: "One exposure before the breakers eat it. The underwriter wants the paint verified." Scan the flagged derelict before the convoy arrives; the plate pays, and the convoy's tally comes up one hull short, documented.
build.payoff: small bonus + codex page; the convoy crew hails you once, professionally unamused.
build.seam: `src/data/landmarkMissions.js` row (scanner-pulse deliverable) with a seasonal window

build.title: The Last Ferry
build.trigger: shift turn, once per sector-day
build.sees: a two-hull ferry pair crosses the lane sharing one lit lamp hung between them; the older hull is visibly half-towing the younger, and has been for years.
build.payoff: pure column motion world-life; the wire never mentions it.
build.seam: vignette `column` motion spec + single lamp channel

build.title: The Borrowed Ladder
build.trigger: proximity; uniqueOnce
build.sees: two wrecks lashed by one intact ladder-tether. Latch the ladder and a log cylinder slides down the tether into your hold, with a note: "RETURN ANYTIME. IT LIKES THE TRIP."
build.payoff: a codex fragment now; re-latching on later visits yields nothing but a polite click.
build.seam: numbered `selfRegistered` encounter + `state.combat.attachments` read (1210 pattern)

build.title: The Three Liars' Cache
build.trigger: proximity to a locked cache with a plain question on the face ("WHAT IS THE MASS OF THE ROCK BESIDE IT?"); uniqueOnce
build.sees: Three prior attempt-notes are welded beside the lock, each with a different confident answer, all different, all wrong. The lock accepts ANY answer — it stamps the cache's log with yours and opens. The argument continues inside: the contents include the receipt from the original sale, which settles it, and nobody who found it ever checked.
build.payoff: Modest contents (one module and the receipt) plus the codex page of the four-way argument, now including you.
build.seam: POI + scan-answer interaction + codex overlay

build.title: The Missed Bells
build.where: any sector, the player's most-docked station

build.sees: the PA, dry: "Station to hull: we noticed the absence. The lane did not. One of those is a compliment."

build.title: The Census of One

build.payoff: being counted, gently; the day's list persists until it rolls over.

build.title: The Queue Critic

build.title: The Letter Home
build.trigger: 5+ sector-days after any rescue whose survivor named a home port
build.sees: A message arrives from the rescued crew's home station — not thanks, better: their mail. "Thought you'd want to know the kid talks about the rescue like weather. 'And then the hull just CAME.' We told them you charge rates like everyone. They've decided you're a smuggler of people. High praise here."
build.payoff: One letter per rescue, kept in a codex folder that becomes, without ever saying so, the best thing in it.
build.seam: rescue records → a letter queue; delivery via comms popup; folder in codexPages.js

build.title: The Abutment Weight

build.title: The Painted Ring

build.title: The Question, Answered Wrong
build.where: sector_sedna_dark, the dark margin beyond the cadence
build.trigger: first sector entry after beat 4; hash-seeded 50% per day thereafter until fired
build.sees: on an empty band, a voice that does not use a callsign asks one question — "What did the mass weigh?" — and waits. If the player transmits any number (any hail reply), the voice answers: "No. Try again next cycle." If the player instead stays silent for 10 seconds, the voice says: "Correct," and the channel closes forever.
build.payoff: flag `the_question_answered`; codex Figures page for The Question unlocks with the line "Persistent. Patient. Answered at Sedna, cycle [day]." Pure lore, huge screenshot energy.

Nothing changes if the player replies. One line confirms receipt: "APPEAL LOGGED. APPEAL NUMBER: 1." — the first appeal ever logged. The Pit does not know it has one. Now the ledger does.

(b) the countdown is authored permanently stalled; appeal #1 is the whole payoff

build.title: The Twenty-Fifth Plinth
build.trigger: player scans the dark 25th plinth (the one "kept dark on purpose" per the Helios bar rumor) after having witnessed any ship death in that sector
build.sees: the plinth answers the scan with a single stored line in a maintenance clerk's voice: "We light twenty-four because twenty-five is whoever is out there right now. It goes on when you don't come back. Welcome to the count." The plinth's light breathes once, then holds.
build.payoff: codex page (Sectors: Helios Prime overlay line); flag `candle_count_understood`; the plinth stays lit for the rest of the session after any player near-death event, then dark again.

build.title: The Ashcache Count Completion
build.trigger: the player completes the Kurtz ledger thread (doss counter) and returns to the floor
build.sees: Kurtz counts aloud as the player lands — and for the first time, the count includes the player's hull: "...forty-one, forty-two." The number the Quiet always used. The count is correct. The count has always been correct. The dead liner's ledger page turns itself in the wind, and the wind here does not move anything else.
build.payoff: flag `counted_42`; codex page "The Forty-Second"; Kurtz's bar desk gains one line of dialogue about arithmetic and company.
build.seam: doss counter gate + count-audio variant + codex overlay

build.title: The Prospector's Cairn
build.trigger: proximity to a fixed deep-belt coordinate; uniqueOnce
build.sees: A cairn of forty marked rock samples, each hand-etched with assay numbers, planted over a grave that isn't there — just a suit, arranged sitting, facing the seam he found. The last sample is the richest rock anyone has ever assayed here. It is not for taking, and everyone seems to know it.
build.payoff: One free ultra-rich assay of the seam he faces (the location is the inheritance); taking the last sample is possible, weighted, and the belt remembers (barks change).

build.title: Signal Buoy VHL-4471
build.trigger: 2000+ WU from any station, after ending E has been filed (post-game continuation route)
build.sees: a hand-built marker buoy floats in nothing, transponder-labeled VHL-4471-T / TESSERA, transmitter off. Wired to it is a paper tag: "FOR WHOEVER FLIES HER NEXT. SHE PULLS LEFT. SHE IS WORTH IT. — W." The tag is the only readable surface for 2000 WU in any direction.
build.payoff: the most screenshot-able easter egg in the set; flag `wren_buoy_found`; ship-screen hull notes gain one line.
build.seam: worldOneOffs row + post-ending flag gate (spine's own.flags.spine end-state); shipScreen note row

build.title: The Kurtz Desk's Second Count

build.sees: Kurtz's count has a new final line, chalked where only a returning pilot will see it: "42 PRESENT. 41 ACCOUNTED. THE DIFFERENCE IS THE ONE THAT STAYS." The difference is the player — the only hull that came back after being counted. Kurtz's ledger, for the first time, is open to a blank page with the player's callsign at the top.
build.payoff: the player's page stays open forever (the one ledger line Kurtz will not close); flag `ledger_open`; Ashfall standing +6.
build.seam: post-SP2-160 dressing + persistent ledger page + flag

build.title: The Witness
build.where: sector_io_reach, a toll lane you once ran
build.trigger: proximity to the exact lane of a skipped toll (priorOutcome 'escaped'), after 5+ sector-days
build.sees: A kid working the toll lane's buoy — real job, too young for it — looks up your registry on the public board and asks the question the belt won't: "It says a hull with this number ran the toll in spring. Was that you?" The lane is empty. The buoy is counting. The kid just wants to know if the legends are true.
build.payoff: Answer honestly (yes: the kid respects it and the toll quietly caps for you thereafter; no: the kid knows anyway, and likes you more for the lie's badness) — the toll lane treats you differently forever.

build.sees: a scorched crew-pod catches the light; scanning it plays a calm voice: "VOLLS, M. / TESSERA — to whoever inherits her: she floats better than she steers. Third bulkhead, behind the plate. I am sorry about the plate." The pod's transponder reads TESSERA / OLD RIG.

build.title: The Latch-Child's Rag

build.trigger: the player masslines/jettisons no cargo and leaves a wreck intact for a full in-game day after first scanning it; on return
build.sees: the wreck has been tidied — loose plates stacked, a salvage tag straightened, and a child's drawing welded where the hull number was: a stick-figure tug holding a smaller stick-figure tug. The registry stamp reads LATCH-CHILD, ORIGIN LAPSED.
build.payoff: flag `latch_child_tidy`; codex Figures page for Latch-Child; future wrecks in that sector get tidied too (the mark persists per-sector).
build.seam: per-sector flag + wreck-dressing variant in the worldOneOffs/uniqueWrecks presentation; codex overlay

build.title: Behind the Plate
build.where: any sector, docked at any station with shipyard services
build.trigger: after SP2-001 flag, first time the player pays for a repair (service:completed, type repair)
build.sees: Slate's yard sends one line to the comms log: "Pulled a plate off a Tessera-class frame once. There was a locker behind it on every one of these hulls. Was, past tense, in your case — yours is empty and the hinges are scratched from the inside."
build.payoff: pure lore + one repeated line from Slate thereafter; closes the Vols thread for players who never piece the pods together.
build.seam: new letter-style row consumed via the mail trigger vocabulary in src/data/mail.js (event 'service:completed' with match {type:'repair'})

build.title: The Posthumous Ping
build.trigger: player docks/log-ins the day after (in-game) any named contact they have transacted with died (contact deed memory has a death record)
build.sees: the mast relays a queued personal from the dead contact, timestamped before their death: "If this sends, the count got me. Settle nothing on my behalf. Especially not to Rook."
build.payoff: Rook's double-billing is pre-empted (flag spares the player one bogus bill); the mail system files it as cast/kind with a day-window trigger.
build.seam: mail.js row keyed to contactDeedMemory death record (deed trigger vocabulary); Rook-bill suppression flag in the billing seam

build.title: Incident 7741, the Sealed Side
build.trigger: scan the Listening Field a second time after beat 3 (the scanner files a 'revisit' observation)
build.sees: the field's array has been quietly re-aimed since the first visit. The scan returns a mirrored board: an evidence shelf listing "INCIDENT 7741 / 5 CREW / CAUSE: SEALED / EVIDENCE: SEALED / WITNESSES: SEALED" — every line sealed except one: "HULL STATUS: HELD TOGETHER."
build.payoff: codex entry (Figures: Warrant Orrin gains a line); flag `incident7741_shelf_seen`; Concord rep tick -1 if the player files a records request, +2 if they walk away.
build.seam: scan-detail row in src/data/discoveryPresentation.js keyed to poi_io_listening_visit count in state.story.flags; codex overlay in src/data/codexPages.js

build.title: The 47-B Cold Call
build.trigger: after ending E has been filed (spine flags) and the player returns to any Ashfall berth
build.sees: the courier does not ask again — but a different voice does, once: "47-B is the open work. 47-A stays closed. This is not 47-A. It is smaller, quieter, and it pays in the only currency the Reach respects: done." The job: one unlisted run, no manifest, one blank page in the packet.
build.payoff: accepting and reading the blank page (refusing to fill it) is the correct play — "A manifest with blank pages is a blank check on your hull" — and Kael's warning pays off: return the packet un-filled for the only payout in the game that comes with an apology attached.
build.seam: spine end-state gate + one-off mission + packet item state machine

build.title: The Bill For Nothing
build.trigger: player has 0 outstanding debts and >5000 cr; once per game
build.sees: an invoice arrives: "CONCORD TOWAGE — STANDBY FEE. NO TOW PERFORMED. READINESS IS THE SERVICE." Amount: 4 cr. The account line's memo field reads: "This is a shakedown. It is also legal. — H."
build.payoff: paying within one day yields a Hale mail line "Correct answer." Refusing yields a second bill for 4 cr titled "LATE FEE ON STANDBY FEE." Either way the player is out 4 cr; Hale rep +1 both ways (they respect consistency).
build.seam: mail.js 'bill' row + follow-up variant keyed to a payment receipt event

build.title: The Seventh Run
build.where: any sector, in transit between sectors
build.trigger: sim-time window — once per in-game day, 2% hash-chance seeded by day index, only after beat 2
build.sees: the band carries half a sentence from no registered sender: "—sevenths run, if anyone is counting, we did not talk about—" then static. No log entry survives unless the player has the comms log open; the note field admits the relay could not triangulate.
build.payoff: pure flavor; after hearing it three times (persisted counter), the codex Figures page for the Tessera crew gains one sentence.
build.seam: new row in the COMMS.ambient-style table in src/data/narrative.js (category ambient, cond on story.beatIndex) — if that file stays dirty, a new src/data/commsWhispers.js consumed by the same comms:popup seam in src/systems/story.js

build.title: The Long Sentence
build.trigger: proximity to a fixed beacon; the message completes only across a real sim-time hour
build.sees: A pre-Collapse beacon blinking an alphabet no catalog matches. It is not a loop. Each pulse advances one character of one very long sentence, and the sentence has been transmitting — patient, unattended — longer than the chart has existed. The full text takes an hour of attention and is worth every minute.
build.payoff: A complete codex page with the translated sentence (an apology from a survey crew that never made it home); the beacon's character state persists in the save.
build.seam: numbered ambient encounter with a simTime-indexed character state (persisted); codex page in src/data/codexPages.js

build.title: The Cold Manifest
build.trigger: salvage_signal find with cryo-pod payload (seeded); uniqueOnce
build.sees: A dead hauler's hold contains six cryo pods, labels worn, power for one. The manifest's last line, in the captain's hand: "Thaw in order of fare paid. I'm sorry. That's the whole law out here."
build.payoff: Choose which pod wakes (three seeded outcomes: a mechanic, a debtor, a child of somebody important) or deliver all six frozen to a station for the honest price; the choice is remembered by whoever you wake.
build.seam: authored one-off in SET_PIECE pattern (DIRTY — fallback numbered selfRegistered with three outcome branches); woken NPC appears at a dock

build.title: The Keeper
build.trigger: proximity to a specific dead station; uniqueOnce
build.sees: A lone suit-tender lives aboard a dead station and re-transmits its final broadcast — arrival boards, shift bells, a weather report for a sky that no longer exists — word-perfect, every hour, for a town that evacuated eleven years ago. He'll do it until the transmitter dies, and the transmitter is dying.
build.payoff: Donate a transmitter part (findable or purchasable) and the broadcast continues; the keeper reads your hull number into the station log as "crew, visiting" — the nicest thing anyone does all week.
build.seam: numbered ambient encounter + item requirement via vignetteInterpreter requires {module} pattern; persistent flag

build.title: The Executor Arrives
build.trigger: mid-loot timing — fires 40s after the player strips a wreck with a "family" flag (seeded); uniqueOnce per wreck
build.sees: Just as you crack a dead salvager's strongbox, a battered family hauler drops out of cruise: "That was my father's hull. Take the credits. The logbook stays." They are not hostile. They are just early.
build.payoff: Hand over the logbook (their story continues — a letter reaches you two sectors later), refuse (they leave, and the wreck's plaque when you pass it again says something colder), or fight them (bounty, real).
build.seam: numbered selfRegistered encounter with timing trigger on loot events; letter delivery via comms:popup pattern (src/data/narrative.js event style)

build.title: Bay 7 Smells Like Transit
build.trigger: dock at station_helios after beat 5 (the atmo-debt thread is live)
build.sees: the bay screen carries the fourteen-year-old ticket verbatim — "BAY 7 ODOR CONSISTENT WITH TRANSIT. NO ACTION. TICKET Y3-C2" — but someone has taped a work light on the cradle marked R3-CARRIER and hung a paper sign: "IF YOU ARE THE REPLACEMENT SCHEDULE, PENDING SINCE YEAR 3: YOU ARE LATE."
build.payoff: flag `bay7_grid_seen`; this is the physical confirmation of the wrong-grid reveal; at Ashfall the Kurtz ledger line about the shelved grid gains an addendum referencing the player's sighting.
build.seam: station bay-screen row in src/data/stationSigns.js (SIGN_BAY, types trade_hub) + flag write on dock; Ashfall addendum is a mail.js row gated on both flags

build.title: 0.7 Tonnes of Moisture
build.trigger: first scan after the player has completed any mission whose outcome left NPC crew dead (moral/deed memory)
build.sees: the stake's tally plate has been re-chalked: "9 / 11 RETURNED. 0.7T FILED AS MOISTURE." Someone has added a second line in different chalk: "THE MATH IS LEGAL. THE MATH IS NOT DONE." A small memorial clamp holds two helmets.
build.payoff: unlocks the codex Figures page for Dustwife Senna (keeper of names); DMC rep +2 if the player leaves a cargo unit of water ice at the stake (physical offering the cargo system already supports).
build.seam: scan copy keyed to flag; offering check via cargo consumption seam; codex overlay in src/data/codexPages.js

build.title: The Recruitment Letter
build.trigger: player Reach rep < -10 and combat deeds > 5; single delivery
build.sees: Sker Vane's office writes: "The Reach weighed you. You are short, loud, and useful. One job, no contract paper, paid in hull parts and not asking. Refusal is fine. Refusal twice is memorable."
build.payoff: a one-off mission: shadow a Meridian toll run and report its timing (no shots fired — the Reach wants the schedule, not the cargo). Payoff: 800 cr in unmarked plates, Reach rep +10, Concord heat +8. Refusing twice closes the thread with one final line: "Memorable."
build.seam: mission data following the board/one-off pattern in src/data/missions.js; Sker Vane voice per FIGURES
hones: (a) numbered selfRegistered job; missions.js only if clean at build

build.title: The Fourth Mayday
build.trigger: fourth distress the player responds to in a run (persistent counter); uniqueOnce
build.sees: The fourth mayday of your run transmits your own registry number as the vessel in distress, at your own last-known heading, with your own voice pattern in the carrier wave. Nobody is there. Your ship's transponder, checked mid-flight, is fine and slightly smug about it.
build.payoff: A short mystery: the source is a crashed courier that copied traffic to spoof rescues — its final real log is the reward (codex page: it was never hunting ships, it was lonely).
build.seam: numbered selfRegistered encounter gated on a distress-response counter; spoof lines via comms:popup; codex in src/data/codexPages.js

build.title: KAEL's Marker
build.trigger: proximity 400 WU to an unlogged hull hung with wreck-plates (new texture one-off)
build.sees: someone has welded a marker plate reading "KAEL — SIX MONTHS — PAID IN FULL" beside an older plate that reads "KAEL — ONE DRINK — UNPAID." The newer plate has a fresh weld seam; the older one is scored by micrometeorites.
build.payoff: if the player docks at a Pitborn berth the same day, one bar regular offers to "square the drink" for 10 cr; paying it writes flag `kael_debt_settled` and Kael's next mail letter changes subject line to "You paid it forward, you enormous sap."
build.seam: worldOneOffs row (pattern of src/data/worldOneOffs.js HELIOS_ROPE_CACHE) + conditional mail variant in src/data/mail.js (FLAG('kael_debt_settled'))

build.title: Morrow's Hundredth Push
build.trigger: the player's 100th Morrow launch (persistent launches counter in morrow memory)
build.sees: Morrow does not launch at first scan. It runs its own tally aloud instead: "One hundred departures. I have stopped counting arrivals separately. They are the same number. Good. Sit with that a moment." Then, quietly, the launch comes anyway: "Go on. There is more sky. There always was."
build.payoff: flag `morrow_hundred`; codex Figures page for Morrow gains its final line; Morrow's memorial variant (if destroyed later) reads differently for players with the flag.
build.seam: MORROW memory counter (src/data/morrow.js freshMorrowMemory) + line variant in MORROW_LINES
hones: (b) family cadence: the machine-people decade fires at most one entry per sector-day

build.title: The Keel Bell
build.trigger: proximity during any yard cut event; cooldownS 600
build.sees: When the yard's cutters free a keel section, an actual bell tolls over the band — and the section falls. Anyone with a line on it before it hits the catcher-net gets first refusal on the scrap. Yard hands bet on which hull catches it.
build.payoff: Catch the keel: a heavy bonus scrap payout and the yard crew's respect (chalk mark on the tally board, see SP1-040).
build.seam: numbered ambient encounter hooking the shipbreak event (src/data/ceresShipbreak.js) with a latch-competition check (attachments read)

build.title: The Buoy That Answers Anyway
build.where: sector_phoebe_echo, the retired channel's nav buoy
build.trigger: hail the buoy three times in a row with nothing else transmitting
build.sees: the first two hails return the standard "no registry." The third returns, in the dead array's own voice: "She asked me to keep answering. I am keeping. Do not tell the network." The buoy then resumes its standard no-registry responses forever.
build.payoff: codex page (Phoebe Echo overlay: "The most reliable signal in the Reach answers to nobody living"); flag `buoy_keeping`.
build.seam: hail-count branch in the buoy's hail copy (contactHail pattern); codex overlay
hones: (a) hail-count branch in the new hail-response data file
(c) Same new hail-response data file as SP2-018 (hail-count branch).

build.title: The Wreck Elder's Registry
build.where: bar of station_drift, the elder's table
build.trigger: after the player has witnessed 3+ NPC ship deaths (session/deed counter)
build.sees: Dustwife Senna keeps the names. She asks the player for three: names she does not have, from wrecks the player has flown past. The job is memory, not salvage — scan the wreck sites again and read the hull plates aloud on an open channel while she listens.
build.payoff: Senna files the names; every wreck the player named gains a permanent memorial tag on the map; DMC rep +5; codex page "The Keeper of Names."
build.seam: one-off mission keyed to wreck-visit flags; memorial tag via the uniqueWrecks presentation; codex overlay

build.title: The Two-Line Problem
build.trigger: proximity; fires when two NPC hulls hold lines on the same pod; cooldownS 1800
build.sees: Two salvagers have both latched the same ore pod and are having a towing argument at 30 WU/s, screaming over the band about line seniority. The pod, notably, has opinions and is heading for a rock.
build.payoff: Cut one line (the loser hates you, the winner pays), catch the pod yourself (nobody pays, everyone respects), or watch physics settle it (the pod wins, both pay you as an independent witness).
build.seam: numbered ambient encounter reading two active attachments on one target; resolution via existing attachment cut seam (src/combat/attachments.js)

build.title: REF 44-C, Filed Against You
build.trigger: after the player has paid 5+ law fines across the campaign (stat gate), once
build.sees: CONCORD PATROL files a form letter — "REF 44-C RECURS. YOUR FILING PATTERN IS NOW ITS OWN CATEGORY. A CLERK HAS BEEN ASSIGNED. SHE HAS ALREADY READ EVERYTHING." The clerk is never named.
build.payoff: a persistent `ref44c_category` flag; all future Concord fine letters arrive pre-signed by a new sender name, and one bounty letter eventually reveals the clerk is Clerk Yune's replacement.
build.seam: mail.js row with STAT trigger + a sender-variant table; flag in state.story.flags
hones: (a) pin the inherited desk: the replacement inherits the Quiet's sealed-evidence desk (Clerk Yune's), not a Concord one (adopted from C)
(b) the replacement inherits the Quiet's evidence desk, not a Concord one (C)

(c) The new clerk inherits the Quiet’s evidence desk — Clerk Yune is the Quiet’s sealed-evidence broker (Wraith Kell is the customs embed), so the replacement inherits Yune’s own desk, not a Concord one.

build.title: The Quiet Booth
build.trigger: the player completes any Quiet transaction then docks here within one day
build.sees: a booth where nobody sits, reserved by a plate that reads "THE HOUSE." The barkeep sets one drink on it every shift. A manifest clerk (unnamed, hat low) nods at the player if the player's recent Quiet deals were clean: "The House drinks to clean work. You are being drunk to. Do not wave."
build.payoff: flag `house_drinks_to_you`; one-time Quiet standing +2; the reserved booth's plate gains the player's callsign, etched small, for the rest of the game.
build.seam: bar set-dressing keyed to transaction receipts; plate etch = persistent contact-memory line (stationContacts pattern in src/data/stationContacts.js)

build.title: The Clock Trap
build.trigger: cruise engaged on a marked lane with a seeded patrol timing window; cooldownS 1800
build.sees: You drop out of cruise into a pre-laid speed trap — three cutters in a box formation, radar trip-lines strung between them (AMBUSH_SIGNATURES 'sensor_tripline' made physical). "Mass and velocity logged. Courtesy notice issued."
build.payoff: A fine issued to your account (collectable at any dock), or a chase if you bolt; the notice is a real item that lowers prices at Concord docks by nothing and is fun to have.
build.seam: numbered file script 'ambush' variant with customs_cutter archetypes; ambush signature vocabulary from src/data/ambushSignatures.js

build.title: The Coffin Cache
build.trigger: proximity to a signal that reads, on every instrument, as a cargo pod — except its transponder says CREW
build.sees: the pod is a burial casket, space-rated, personal effects sealed inside per the manifest. A note on the hull: "HE WANTED THE BELT. THE BELT WAS NOT ON THE ROUTE. THE BELT IS NOW ON THE ROUTE." It drifts a slow spiral around a specific asteroid, forever, by design.
build.payoff: the player can nudge the spiral (massline) to tighten or widen it — the family's letter (unlockable via the Quiet, who handle such deliveries) says which. Pure gravity-as-memorial; codex page "The Belt, On The Route."
build.seam: POI with stable orbit + massline interaction + letter mail row

build.title: The Four Points
build.trigger: proximity to each of four fixed beacons (any order); the fourth fires the payoff; uniqueOnce
build.sees: Four identical beacons stand at compass points around a dead star. Each has one sentence, plain as a shipping notice — and each sentence is about a thing YOU actually did this run (rescued, refused, robbed, ran). Nobody built them this week. They were here first.
build.payoff: The fourth point sums the other three into a verdict with no author and no punishment — just the record, read aloud. The most quietly effective codex entry in the game.
build.seam: four numbered ambient encounters reading real player deed stats (deedRecord.js, src/systems/deedRecord.js); verdict composes from completed records

build.title: Spam: You Have Won A Sector
build.trigger: day >= 4, then every 8th in-game day (deterministic cadence)
build.sees: MERIDIAN BONDS OFFICIAL: "CONGRATULATIONS VHL-4471-T! YOUR HULL HAS BEEN PRE-APPROVED TO SPONSOR A SECTOR. ATMOSPHERIC NAMING RIGHTS FROM 900 CR. CURRENT LEAD BIDDER: NOBODY. CURRENT SECTOR CONDITION: DECLINING."
build.payoff: pure spam in the house voice; the fine print (expandable in the mail UI) is a genuinely accurate one-paragraph summary of the silt/atmo economy — the joke teaches the system.
build.seam: mail.js kind 'spam' row with DAY trigger (existing cadence vocabulary)

build.title: The Checkpoint Cat
build.trigger: proximity to any Concord scan ring after 10+ scans (persistent counter); cooldownS 86400
build.sees: A maintenance drone has adopted the checkpoint. It perches on the scan-ring emitter, follows the examiner's cutter around like a duckling, and is officially logged as "equipment, morale." The examiner denies it in writing.
build.payoff: Pure flavor, one codex entry; the drone appears at every Concord checkpoint you visit from then on (persistent flag).
build.seam: numbered ambient encounter (noCombat, visual prop only) + story flag; codex row in src/data/codexPages.js

build.title: The Undertakers' Bell
build.trigger: proximity to a fixed wreck after ANY player-caused kill in the sector that day
build.sees: A derelict tug that tows nothing, followed by nothing, rings its bell once for every hull that died in the sector that day. The count is honest — the bell knows things the news doesn't — and on the day you first hear it, it rings for someone you never met and one more time than the news reported.
build.payoff: A standing memorial with a real count (persisted per sector-day); ring it yourself once (a deliberate, manual choice) for your own dead, and the bell holds that count forever, on a plaque no one can find.
build.seam: numbered ambient encounter reading kill records; bell count in story.flags; plaque as codex

build.title: The Preserved Cockpit's Manifest
build.trigger: scan the cockpit's manifest three times across three sessions (session-separated)
build.sees: each scan returns one more manifest line than the last — items being added, not recovered: gloves, a thermos, a paperback, a second paperback, a note. The final scan's last line: "ONE (1) PILOT, PRESERVED, DO NOT WAKE UNTIL THE BELT IS SAFE. STATUS: [REDACTED]."
build.payoff: codex page "Do Not Wake"; Charon standing +2; the cockpit's light gains a slow pulse — sleep breathing — after the final scan.
build.seam: per-session scan counter + manifest-line state + codex overlay

build.title: The Mole's Handoff
build.trigger: whisper-class rare; gates maxSecurity 0.7; uniqueOnce
build.sees: At the edge of scan range, a customs cutter drifts alongside a Quiet ghost hull for exactly forty seconds, says nothing on any band, then both leave. If scanned at the right moment, the cutter's cargo hold reads as empty and its mass doesn't.
build.payoff: Reporting it (Concord rep, the mole vanishes) or selling the observation to the ghost (a stolen scan schedule: patrols literally avoid you for a day — real seeded schedule change).
build.seam: numbered file script 'whisper' with scan tell (DIST_TELL_R pattern in encounterScripts.js); schedule change via story flag read by patrol planner

build.title: The Reach Weigh-Booth Tollbooth Poetry
build.where: sector_io_reach / sector_sker_haven, any Reach toll line
build.trigger: pay any Reach toll; once per game
build.sees: the receipt prints with a haiku-length line at the bottom, rotating per day-seed: "WEIGH-SLIP FOUR HULLS / THREE FILLED, ONE SHORT, THE LANE / KEEPS WHAT IT IS OWED." The collector, if hailed, denies authorship in a way that confirms it.
build.payoff: pure voice; collecting 5 different receipt-poems (persistent counter) unlocks a codex page "Frequency 13, The Chapbook."
build.seam: toll receipt copy keyed to day-seed; codex overlay

build.title: The Plaque
build.where: any sector, at the site of the player's first hostile kill
build.trigger: permanent marker placed at first-kill coordinates; persists all save
build.sees: The site of your first kill, marked by somebody — a small buoy, a plate, and an inscription nobody signs: "First hull down, {date}, by an unregistered hull. It had a name too." The plate does not judge. The plate is just accurate, and it has been here the whole time.
build.payoff: A permanent, quiet landmark; returning years later (the game knows how long it's been) the plate has accumulated small objects — bolts, a ribbon, someone's spare key — left by people who fly this lane.
build.seam: first-kill record writes site coordinates + persistent marker prop; offerings accumulate in story.flags

build.title: The Two Halves
build.trigger: scanning one half reveals the other's bearing; the pair persists across the whole save
build.sees: A ship torn in two by something nobody wants to name: bow in Ceres, stern in Tethys, both still squawking a joined transponder. Scanning either half marks the other on the chart with a line between them that no map function drew.
build.payoff: Visit both halves and the joined log assembles itself in codex — the crew's last three days, ending on a decision the player now understands but cannot judge.
build.seam: two wreck sites in src/data/uniqueWrecks.js with a shared log fragment pool; codex assembly via codexPages.js

build.title: The Book of Receipts
build.trigger: fires after 50 notable deeds of 5+ types (priorOutcome history threshold); uniqueOnce
build.sees: A Quiet courier, the first and only one to ever hail you unbidden, hands over a bound book — every receipt the game ever gave you, bound in order, with the Quiet's own stamp on the spine and a title page that says, in no language you read but understand: "ACCOUNTS CURRENT." The last page is blank. It is not an error. It is, the courier indicates, "for the next ones."
build.payoff: The campaign's receipts made physical; the blank page means the game expects more of you — and every receipt after this one is printed, by the world, slightly better bound.
build.seam: encounter-history threshold (crSituationKit records + deedRecord); book as a codex artifact in codexPages.js; courier one-off numbered encounter

build.title: The First-Rights Picket
build.trigger: proximity to fresh aftermathWreck while a scavenger crew is present; cooldownS 2400
build.sees: Scavengers have thrown a physical picket around a fresh wreck — five beacon-banners in a ring and one old hull parked nose-in like a dog on a bone. The banner codes read, honestly, "FIRST LINE HOLDS."
build.payoff: Cross the picket and they fight (they are worse armed than they act); wait 60 seconds and the lead shares a third of the salvage pool as a finds-fee for patience; come back next day and the wreck is cleanly stripped.
build.seam: numbered file script 'claimThreat' variant (the script already adjudicates claim contests) via src/systems/encounterScripts.js

build.title: Rubric's Autograph
build.trigger: after Rubric has marked 10+ hulls the player has witnessed (marking counter)
build.sees: Rubric marks the player's hull — unasked, gently, a small stenciled "HM-11 ✕ [callsign]" near the airlock. The stencil is dated. The date is the day of the player's first Rubric sighting, not today: it has been planning this since they met.
build.payoff: permanent shipScreen dressing; flag `rubric_signed`; any Rubric-marked NPC hull thereafter treats the player as "co-marked" (minor positive hail variance).
build.seam: marking counter + shipScreen dressing + hail variance flag
hones: (a) verify Rubric HM-11 - three entries ride on this machine; confirm or bless explicitly (adopted from C)
(b) verify-or-bless Rubric HM-11; if blessed, used consistently across 120/130 (C)
(c) Same verification for Rubric HM-11 — three entries ride on this machine; confirm the id or bless Rubric explicitly, used consistently.

build.title: Pallet Jack's One Honest Theft
build.trigger: the player leaves any single unsecured cargo unit floating near a yard for 60+ seconds (jettison + proximity rule)
build.sees: the cargo vanishes between two frames. A hail follows, from no registered hull: "ONE (1) UNIT, UNSECURED, UNLOVED. REMOVED. IF IT WAS LOVED, SIGNAL. I WILL BRING IT BACK. I AM A THIEF, NOT A MONSTER." If the player signals within one minute, the unit returns with a small bow-wave flourish.
build.payoff: flag `jack_honest`; Pallet Jack's future intro encounter opens with "the one that came back"; pure charm.
build.seam: unsecured-cargo watcher + timed restore event; Pallet Jack line table (src/data/palletJack.js pattern)
hones: (a) verify the Pallet Jack cast id; if it is a pattern not a character, name the thief from the unregistered-hull vocabulary (adopted from C)
(b) verify the Pallet Jack id; name from real unregistered-hull vocabulary if a pattern only (C)
(c) Verify the Pallet Jack cast id; if it is a pattern and not a character, name the thief from the existing unregistered-hull vocabulary.

build.title: The Complaint Desk
build.trigger: fires after any incident the player caused (raid, ram, fine) — on next dock
build.sees: A formal reading of complaints filed against your hull, verbatim, by name, with registration numbers: the toll you ran ("witness: three hulls, one of them a child"), the queue you cut, the wake that rattled a pilgrim's lamp. The clerk reads them all. The clerk has heard worse. The clerk has, in fact, a favorite.
build.payoff: A comedy of record-keeping with one real effect: settle any complaint with a formal apology payment and the complainant withdraws it (small rep, the clerk's approval, which matters more).
build.seam: incident-history read (deedRecord/fines) rendered as a dock comms popup; settlement via d.charge/d.rep

build.title: Scissorwake Spares The Tessera
build.trigger: Scissorwake's gate (hunts any qualifying lane) engages the player while the Tessera hull is below 25% integrity
build.sees: the roamer breaks off at engagement range and does not attack. One line, on no channel in particular: "NO. THE OLD HULLS GET TO DIE OF OLD AGE. THAT IS THE RULE. I DO NOT MAKE THE RULES. I DO ENFORCE THIS ONE." It shadows at a respectful distance until the player leaves the lane.
build.payoff: flag `scissorwake_mercy`; Scissorwake will never open on the player below 25% integrity again (persistent mercy rule); codex page "The Roamer's Rule."
build.seam: roamer gate check on hull state (oneOffCast roamers) + line event; mercy flag consumed by the roamer's engagement logic
hones: (a) verify Scissorwake in the oneOffCast roamers; wire the old-hulls mercy flag to whichever roamer is real (adopted from C)
(b) verify Scissorwake; wire the old-hulls mercy rule to whichever roamer is real (C)
(c) Verify Scissorwake in the oneOffCast roamers; wire the old-hulls mercy flag to whichever roamer is real — the rule is too good to lose.

build.title: The Demo End's Uninvited Guest
build.where: any sector, at session end (end-of-demo wrap)
build.trigger: the player reaches any run-end condition with zero comms popups dismissed all session (attention stat)
build.sees: as the results sheet renders, one last popup arrives that was queued since minute one and never needed dismissing — it dismisses itself: "YOU READ EVERYTHING. THE CHANNEL NOTICED. THE CHANNEL IS MOSTLY NOISE. SO WAS MOST OF THIS. THANK YOU FOR THE PART THAT WASN'T."
build.payoff: flag `read_everything`; the results sheet gains one line; next session's ambient popups run 20% less noise (the channel respects the reader).
build.seam: popup-dismiss counter + resultsSheet line (src/ui/screens/resultsSheet.js) + next-session cond tweak
hones: (a) comms popup + flag; resultsSheet/demoEnd are dirty; next-session quiet flag keys a parallel ambient table
(c) Deliver via comms popup + flag; resultsSheet.js and demoEnd.js are dirty; the next-session quiet-mode flag keys a parallel ambient table.

build.title: The Count of Doors
build.where: any sector with Quiet presence (low security, tier 2+)
build.trigger: player hull carries any undeclared/contraband commodity and passes within 900 WU of a Quiet-tagged hull; once per game
build.sees: a flat relay voice, not addressed to the player: "FORTY-ONE HULLS. FORTY-TWO DOORS." A two-second silence. "CORRECTED. PROCEED." No threat is ever named.
build.payoff: pure dread; a Quiet standing flag `quiet_counted_you` that makes the next Quiet fence contact greet the player by hold-count instead of by name.
build.seam: comms:popup row with cond on cargo manifest (pattern of trap_inspection in src/data/narrative.js); fence greeting variant in src/ui/station/barContacts.js fenceContact copy
hones: (a) fence greeting as a comms line keyed to the flag; barContacts.js is dirty - request, do not edit
(c) The replacement inherits the Quiet’s evidence desk — Clerk Yune’s own, not a Concord one; delivered as a comms variant (barContacts is dirty — request, do not edit).

build.title: The Retraction
build.trigger: after the player appears in any news crawl headline (marketNews feat headline about the player)
build.sees: 600 s later, the crawl carries: "RETRACTION: THE PILOT NAMED IN OUR LAST ITEM WAS ONE HULL AMONG SEVERAL. WE REGRET THE ACCURACY." Lira Vonn's correspondent tag sits under the retraction — she retracted it because it was accurate.
build.payoff: flag `vonn_retraction`; her bar contact at the nearest station now offers "the story that was too true" for a drink's price (a lore read).
build.seam: marketNews post-headline row + barContacts lore-read offer; both existing seams

build.title: The Drafter
build.trigger: proximity behind any heavy hull at matched speed for 20s; cooldownS 1200
build.sees: A mule hauler settles in 30 WU behind your wake and just... rides it, visibly saving burn. When you finally hail, the pilot is unashamed: "Your wake, my range. I'll take the next gate's toll for it." Everyone does this. Nobody admits it first.
build.payoff: Accept the toll trade (a small credit transfer, a named acquaintance added to the band); refuse and she peels off with dignity intact.
build.seam: numbered ambient encounter with speed/position check; credit transfer via d.grant/d.charge; a well-known friendly NPC roster entry

build.title: The Escort Of One
build.trigger: any civilian hull's distress fires while the player has a full cargo hold (the offer to help costs real capacity)
build.sees: a refugee convoy hull (Mara and the Children's make) broadcasts not for escort but for witness: "We do not need a gun. We need a second transponder on the lane so the toll men count two hulls, not one. Fly beside us. Ask for nothing. We will know what it cost you."
build.payoff: a hold-space sacrifice: the player jettisons nothing but flies slow and visible; completion grants no credits — a hand-painted child's drawing (inventory item) and Mara's standing +6, which later converts to a unique hull discount no other faction offers.
build.seam: proximity escort check + standing + item; Mara voice per FIGURES (src/data/narrative.js)

build.title: The Wrong Number
build.trigger: proximity to a Quiet relay; cooldownS 86400; uniqueOnce
build.sees: A routed-for-someone-else burst lands in your queue: full handler's orders for a smuggling run — the cargo, the window, the buyer's scan schedule. Then, thirty seconds later, a very calm voice: "Delete that." The job is real. The window is real. The voice is closer than you'd like.
build.payoff: Run someone else's job honestly (they never acknowledge you, the payment arrives anyway, which is somehow worse), sell the orders back (Quiet rep), or ignore it (the buyer waits at the drop for a hull that never comes).
build.seam: comms popup with payload + a real drop-site encounter (boreDeadDrop.js precedent, src/systems/boreDeadDrop.js)

build.title: The Registry's Last Field
build.trigger: after the late_registry_unknown popup (operator: UNKNOWN) has fired, the player dock-hops to every station in their home sector in one session
build.sees: at the last station, the registry pings one final line: "OPERATOR FIELD REVIEW: UNKNOWN IS A STATUS, NOT AN ERASURE. THE FIELD REMAINS. THE FIELD IS WAITING FOR A VALUE. THIS IS THE ADMINISTRATIVE DEFINITION OF HOPE."
build.payoff: flag `field_waiting`; the player's registry line, wherever displayed, gains a blinking cursor after UNKNOWN — permanent, cosmetic, devastating.
build.seam: station-crawl check + registry dressing + flag

build.title: The Sermon
build.trigger: choir broadcast cadence (seeded weekly); content composed from the player's last three receipts
build.sees: The Choir's weekly sermon is public, serene, and — this week — tailored: it cites your last three deeds by fact and number, without names, without judgment, as verses. "And the hull that paid the tithe twice and the third time ran — what did the third lane cost, children?" Everyone in earshot knows who it's about. It is not about anyone.
build.payoff: A chilling, gorgeous use of the game's own receipt system; the sermon's citations are accurate to the real encounter history, and the Choir's rep shifts one point by what it read.
build.seam: numbered comms encounter composing text from crSituationKit history records; rep via d.rep faction_choir

build.title: The Story Broker
build.trigger: dock event after any moral-tagged cargo sale (state flag on sale); cooldownS 86400
build.sees: A Quiet broker finds you at the dock, not to buy goods: "You sold famine-grade ration packs to a resort station. That's a story. I'll buy the story. The resort never needs to know you know what you did."
build.payoff: Sell the story (credits, and the commodity's moral ledger stays clean — the Quiet owns the shame); refuse (the deed stays on YOUR ledger, visibly, in codex).
build.seam: dock comms popup + commodityMoralTags read (src/data/commodityMoralTags.js); codex entry in src/data/codexPages.js

build.title: The Reefer Handoff
build.trigger: proximity to a hauler with a "failing container" state flag (seeded); cooldownS 3600
build.sees: A hauler hails with something genuinely urgent: a volatile reefer is venting and she can't dock with it aboard. "Take it. Run it to the refinery in ten minutes. I'll pay the container's whole margin." The container is visibly frosting over.
build.payoff: A timed fragile-carry (fragileCargo seam); deliver and she becomes a recurring named hauler; fail and the venting makes a visible, harmless-but-humiliating ice cloud.
build.seam: numbered selfRegistered encounter spawning a fragile prop pod; fragileCargo.js (src/systems/fragileCargo.js) patterns

build.title: The Berth Queue
build.trigger: fires when station traffic density exceeds a seeded threshold; ambient
build.sees: Peak shift at Helios: a visible queue of six hulls holding pattern around the dock spine, a tug assigning berths with hand-signal light codes, two captains bickering over the band about who called the berth first ("I said 'mark' before he said 'dibs'").
build.payoff: Pure world-life; joining the queue politely is faster than cutting, which the traffic controller notes with approval for future visits.
build.seam: numbered ambient encounter + vignetteInterpreter 'column'/'hold' motions; controller barks in ENCOUNTER_BARKS

build.title: The Far-Side Message
build.trigger: proximity with the wreck on the correct bearing from the sector's light source; uniqueOnce
build.sees: A wreck's hull, lit from behind by the nebula's rim glow, throws a shadow across the fog — and the shadow is a word, welded in plate and readable only as a silhouette from exactly this side: "SORRY". The hull's registration says it carried passengers.
build.payoff: Pure elegy; scanning it produces the shortest codex page in the game and a whisper-line variant that only ever plays near it.
build.seam: numbered ambient encounter + lighting-position trigger (sim-time shadow angle, deterministic); whisper variant in WHISPER_LINES (src/data/encounters.js)
hones: (a) backlit welded stencil plate with rim glow; the engine does not cast shadow-text
(b) backlit welded stencil plate (A H-08); SORRY in silhouette survives the seam fix
(c) The engine casts no shadow-text — build it as a backlit welded stencil plate (cutout letters, rim glow from the nebula side); same read, real seam.

build.title: The Sommelier of Coolant
build.trigger: first dock; talk to the rail
build.sees: the depot bar's sole bartender is a retired Choir censer machine that has rebranded its incense burn as "beverage temperature control." It describes fuel-cell vintages in liturgical cadence: "This cell — cast on a Thursday. You will taste the Thursday."
build.payoff: pure joy; buying "the Thursday" (small credits purchase) grants a fuel-efficiency buff for one run and Choir rep +1 ("the censer remembers patronage").
build.seam: barContacts canonical contact (CANONICAL_CONTACTS pattern in src/ui/station/barContacts.js) + purchase option

build.title: The Distress Echo
build.where: sector_charon_expanse, along the radiation lane past the Lung
build.trigger: transit along the lane after beat 2; fires once
build.sees: a distress call that is word-for-word the Snapped-Tether Hab-Pod's mayday — but five seconds ahead of the pod itself, repeating from a point further down the lane where nothing is squawking. The signal degrades to static exactly at the point the real pod's recording ends.
build.payoff: an investigation breadcrumb that resolves into the existing poi_charon_tether_wreck recovery encounter; flag `echo_heard` gates a bar regular at station_expanse who explains: "The lane repeats. Radiation does that. Doesn't make it less of a mayday."
build.seam: comms popup + route to existing survivorPod recoveryEncounter (referenced in src/data/frontierRumors.js AUTHORED_DOCK_RUMORS)

build.title: The Whisper With a Name
build.trigger: fires when the player has an actually-unpaid toll AND a whisper roll lands (priorOutcome check)
build.sees: The whisper pool, which never addresses anyone, addresses you: "the toll you skipped still counts your engine note" — and then, for one transmission only, it names the exact lane. The pool's voice is the same. The specificity is not.
build.payoff: Paying at the named lane silences that line forever (a real flag); not paying means the line follows you into every later whisper roll, slightly closer to your name each time.
build.seam: whisper script variant checking unpaid-toll story flags; line added to WHISPER_LINES (src/data/encounters.js — clean file)

build.title: The Engine Shrine
build.trigger: proximity; uniqueOnce
build.sees: Scavengers have built a shrine around a wreck's intact main engine: laid tools as offerings, burned tally-marks on the housing, and a sign that reads, without irony, "IT STILL TURNS." One pilgrim is always present, as requested: they leave it running at idle, in the dark, forever.
build.payoff: Pay respect (leave any tool) and the pilgrim gifts a cold-start module pulled from "the offering pile"; rob the shrine and every scavenger pack in the sector knows within the day.
build.seam: numbered ambient encounter with offerings counter in story.flags; consequence broadcast via bandRadio

build.title: Fennel Comes Home
build.where: any sector, any goat-adjacent hauler (the lost_goat roaming story carrier)
build.trigger: if the roaming story lost_goat has been heard on hail AND the player later docks at a station whose bar rumor mentions hydroponics
build.sees: a hydroponics rack reports "one dairy goat, self-stowed." Bramble's hauler is two sectors away. The bar takes a vote: everyone agrees the goat gets to stay; the vote is 9-1; the 1 is Bramble.
build.payoff: a micro-fetch: ferry a "GOAT (FENNEL)" cargo unit back to Bramble when their route crosses the sector (event-driven rendezvous); finder fee + a permanent bar regular line "The goat remembers you. Do not sit in the third stool."
build.seam: one-off mission data following the roaming-stories binding pattern (src/data/roamingStories.js) + cargo unit with custom commodityId

build.title: The Seam Singer
build.trigger: proximity to a solo prospector mid-scan; cooldownS 3600
build.sees: An old prospector "sings" — a slow tonal pulse from her rig that resonates off ore bodies differently than rock. "The belt lies to instruments. It never lies to a tuned throat." Following her song's echo leads to a vein her own gear can't crack alone.
build.payoff: A rich co-mining site: she cracks, you haul, split is honest. Her song becomes buyable as a rig tune (permanent survey buff, small).
build.seam: numbered selfRegistered encounter with audio-cue prop; co-mining split via mining yield events; buff as a module or trait via src/data/modules.js

build.title: The Fulfillment Queue Miracle
build.trigger: the player completes any delivery with zero seconds of buffer remaining (deadline within one sim-second of expiry)
build.sees: FULFILLMENT LOG: "DELIVERY RECEIVED. BUFFER: 0.00s. CLASSIFICATION: MIRACLE (STATISTICAL). MIRACLE HAS BEEN FILED. MIRACLE WILL NOT BE REPEATED. THE QUEUE IS EMOTIONAL ABOUT THIS AND DECLINES TO ELABORATE."
build.payoff: flag `queue_miracle`; Fulfillment standing +3; every future Fulfillment greeting adds "MIRACLE" as an honorific.
build.seam: delivery timing check + greeting variant

build.title: The Quiet's Receipt
build.where: any sector, after any transaction with a Quiet fence contact
build.trigger: 60 s after the fence deal closes (simTime)
build.sees: an unaddressed relay line: "THE QUIET THANK NOBODY. THE QUIET FILE EVERYTHING. YOUR FILE IS CURRENT." Attached is a receipt naming the commodity, the amount, and a seal code that is one character off from the seal code printed on the player's own hull registration.
build.payoff: flag `quiet_receipt_off_by_one`; players who scan their own hull at any station get one extra scan line: "REGISTRY SEAL: VERIFIED. (ONE CHARACTER IN DISPUTE.)"
build.seam: comms:popup row + scan-copy variant; both are data rows over existing seams

build.title: Voss's Open Page
build.trigger: after pers_voss_suspended has fired (beat 5+); dock once
build.sees: the claim office's ledger is open to one page with a paper clip: the convoy that never logged. Voss asks — not as a mission, as a favor between ledgers — to fly the old convoy route once with a live tally rig and let the scale say what the page says.
build.payoff: a single-flight survey run; the scale either confirms the hole (one-line ledger correction, DMC rep +5, the clerk "keeps the page open" permanently) or reads one extra hull — which becomes the codex page "The Forty-First." Either outcome is a story.
build.seam: one-off mission via src/data/missions.js data + survey/signal seam (signal:surveyFiled is already a MAIL_EVENT_NAMES event in src/data/mail.js)

build.title: The Paid Fare
build.trigger: scanning the wreck reads a passenger manifest with one "PAID, STATUS: ABOARD" entry; uniqueOnce
build.sees: Everything about the wreck says total loss except one line of the manifest: a passenger who paid in full, boarded, and was listed aboard at impact. The pod bays are empty. The pods themselves are somewhere, and pods keep life support logs.
build.payoff: A quiet search contract (scan candidate debris for pod transponders) with a seeded ending: found-alive (a passenger with one scene's worth of story) or found-at-peace (the log is the reward).
build.seam: authored search chain (recon_scan stages over seeded debris, SET_PIECE pattern — DIRTY file; fallback numbered chain); passenger NPC via crew data

build.title: The Morning Report
build.trigger: one digest per sector day, on dock
build.sees: The daily report: three headlines, two true, one wrong in a specific direction — prices that didn't move, a raid that was smaller than filed, a rescue that has no rescuer. It never lies about anything that matters to the sim. It lies about exactly one thing per day, and nobody knows why.
build.payoff: Spotting the lie (checking the report against the actual market/news data the game has) builds a "reader" flag; after 30 spotted lies the reporter leaves you a private note that explains nothing and is the best text in the game.
build.seam: digest generator comparing economy/news state; flag counter in story.flags; note via comms popup
hones: (a) the morning report's one daily lie never touches prices or mission data - it lies about color, never money (adopted from B)
(b) the daily lie never touches prices or mission data; it lies about color, never money
(c) The one daily lie never touches prices or mission data a player can bet on — it lies about color, never about money.

build.title: The Endings' Return Mail
build.trigger: 7+ in-game days after any ending filed (spine end-state)
build.sees: one letter per ending, addressed to whoever the player chose to become: A gets the watch's roster with one new name; B gets a routing seat's vacancy notice, unclaimed; C gets a berth assignment at "the same berth"; D gets the desk's own desk-key inventory tag; E gets one blank page and a stamp: "47-B: OPEN."
build.payoff: each is pure closure-mail; all five write a single persistent flag each that colors the post-game dock voice (ENDING_STATION_ACK variants).
build.seam: mail.js rows keyed to spine end-state + dock-voice variant

build.title: The Maroon
build.trigger: proximity to a lone escape pod at seeded offset; uniqueOnce per sector; cooldownS 86400
build.sees: A pod with one survivor: a pirate the pack marooned for skimming. "They left me the air I'd stolen. That's Reach arithmetic." He'll trade the pack's next ambush plan for a ride to anywhere with a bar.
build.payoff: Ferry him (he rides as a latchable pod) for a future-ambush forewarning flag and bar gossip; or leave him; or hand him to a passing pack (Reach rep).
build.seam: numbered file script 'selfRegistered' with a pod prop the player tows (tetherable: true, as 1210's beacon); barks table in the file

build.title: The Backwards Bell
build.where: sector_vesta_forge, any Choir bell (E-23 pulse field)
build.trigger: the player reverses through a bell pulse — enters the field from its far side moving against the pulse sweep (deterministic geometry check), first time only
build.sees: the pulse line renders in reverse and the bell answers with its shatter line backwards: "once — sings crystal The." Every Choir chorister in range stops for one full pulse period, then resumes as if nothing happened. One pilgrim transport transmits a single word: "AGAIN?"
build.payoff: Choir rep -2 (rememberSacrilege is literal) but flag `bell_walked_backwards`; a Choir acolyte later sells the player a "corrective" blessing at standard rates. Dry wit, faction-true.
build.seam: geometry check in the choir runtime owner + one variant line in CHOIR_BELLS copy (src/data/factions/choir.js)

build.title: The Choir's Hundredth Pilgrim
build.trigger: the player arrives at a shrine while the sector's pilgrim counter crosses a century mark (persisted count)
build.sees: every Bell in range pulses out of cadence — once, together, deliberately — and every Choir hull in the sector lights its ribbons at once. The pilgrims' transports all stop for one breath. Then everything resumes, and no Choir member will explain it: "The Pattern noticed. It does not always. Today it did."
build.payoff: pure spectacle-in-world; Choir standing +2 for witnessing; flag `pattern_noticed`.
build.seam: counter + presentation cue via choir:bellPulse event; flag write
hones: (a) the firing moment must say the count aloud (bell + line naming the hundredth) so the trigger is legible - answers B's invisibility kill
(b) keep, but the PA gives one dry line so the player knows what the bell was for

build.title: The Air Auction
build.trigger: proximity to a genuine distress with limited remaining life-support (seeded); cooldownS 86400
build.sees: A stranded freighter with hours of air, and — arriving from the opposite bearing — a Reach "rescuer" who hails the victims first with a price list. The victims transmit both offers to you, in the clear, hoping market pressure helps them.
build.payoff: Outbid, outrun, or outfight; rescue without payment (faction-wide gratitude + a named family that writes later); let the Reach have it and hear about it in a bar for years.
build.seam: numbered file script 'distress' with a second responder squad spawned by the same runtime; src/data/encounters/100-distress-call.js is the family base

build.title: The Warm Tow
build.trigger: posted when a seeded medical emergency spawns; visible on all boards
build.sees: A stasis pod's heater is dead and the patient has cold hours, not days. The medical station's rule is immutable: pods travel warm. Your hull, running warm, latched to the pod, is the ambulance. The pod is fragile. The lane is not.
build.payoff: A tense no-combat tow where the threat is entirely physical (debris, tolls, your own line discipline); arrival pays and the patient's family names a berth after your hull.
build.seam: authored tow/escort mission (tow_recovery type in MISSION_TYPES); pod temperature as a deadline proxy (deadlineS)

build.title: The Courtesy
build.trigger: fires after the player has LEFT three hostile encounters without firing (persistent counter); uniqueOnce
build.sees: A quiet_ghost falls in off your wing and flies perfect formation for sixty seconds — matching every burn, holding exactly station — then drops a small sealed cache and is gone without one word on any band. The cache contains exactly enough fuel to reach the next station.
build.payoff: The cache (real, sized honestly); the ghost's courtesy repeats once more if the counter reaches ten, then never again — restraint has a budget too.
build.seam: numbered selfRegistered encounter keyed to a no-fire counter in story.flags; cache prop via beacons; ghost uses quiet_ghost archetype passive behavior

build.title: The Unclaimed Reward
build.trigger: the player completes a bounty (tagged entity kill) and does not dock to claim for 3+ in-game days
build.sees: the bounty board mails the payout unsolicited: "YOU DID NOT CLAIM. THE DESK DOES NOT HOLD CREDITS. THE DESK MOVES THEM. DO NOT MAKE THE DESK MOVE THEM AGAIN." A 2% handling fee has been deducted, itemized as "motion."
build.payoff: credits arrive anyway; flag `desk_moved`; future bounty claims at that board have the handling fee pre-waived with the memo "you learned."
build.seam: mail.js 'bill'-kind row + flag; bounty board seam in src/systems/missionBoardOps.js

build.title: The Heir
build.trigger: 2-5 sector-days after killing any named captain (priorOutcome named_hunter 'killed'); uniqueOnce per captain
build.sees: A formal hail, of all things: "I am {name}'s heir. The pack requires a conclusion, not a grudge. The paper says you killed well. The paper says I inherit. One of us is about to be right." They arrive with better escorts and worse experience.
build.payoff: Defeat the heir and the pack closes the file — future pack encounters in that sector open with respect (visible bark change). Let them escape and the file stays open: they return once more, better.
build.seam: numbered file script 'namedHunter' variant with gates.requiresCompletedShape; heir entry added to NAMED_CAPTAINS roster pattern (src/data/encounters.js)

build.title: The Empty Barycenter
build.trigger: proximity to three large bodies in a visible mutual orbit; uniqueOnce
build.sees: Three dead moons orbit a common center that contains nothing at all — and the nothing has mass. Instruments agree on the gravity and disagree on everything else. Rocks that drift too close to the center slow down, politely, as if remembering something.
build.payoff: A navigational curiosity with one honest mechanic: the slow zone is real, physics-honest, and the fastest route across the sector deliberately threads it; locals charge to teach the timing.
build.seam: numbered anomaly encounter + a local field effect (fields.js precedent, src/systems/fields.js); lore in codex
hones: (a) one dead-moon pair + registered slow field; no three-body articulation
(b) one dead-moon pair plus a registered slow field (A H-10)
(c) One dead-moon pair plus a registered slow field row; drop the three-body mutual orbit.

build.title: The Sixth Pip
build.trigger: listen through a full sim-hour boundary at any station
build.sees: The official time pips: five pips, then the hour. Except Helios' tower plays six, and has for years, and the error is documented, filed, and uncorrectable because the technician who knew why retired rich and happy and refuses to say. The band's old-timers set their watches by the sixth pip on purpose.
build.payoff: Pure charm; asking about it at the dock (a comms choice) yields three different explanations from three different crew, all of whom believe theirs completely.
build.seam: numbered ambient encounter + dock comms choice; timer anchored to state.simTime hour boundaries

build.title: The Return
build.trigger: 3+ sector-days after the player survives any fight at hull < 20% (persisted record); uniqueOnce
build.sees: An old enemy hull drops out of cruise beside you — the one who nearly ended you — and escorts you, in silence, to the station ring. Before peeling off, one transmission: "Not today. I want the version that's repaired." The band, for once, has nothing to say.
build.payoff: A nemesis with a code: they appear exactly once more, at your next worst moment, and take a side you don't expect. The rivalry gets an ending.
build.seam: story-flag record of near-death fights; numbered selfRegistered encounter keyed to the flag; escort via vignetteInterpreter face/depart motions

build.title: The Vacation Reply
build.trigger: the player hails a named contact's frequency while that contact is docked somewhere other than their home station (roaming cast)
build.sees: an automated reply in the contact's own voice, recorded badly: "I am not here. I am exactly where you are not, which is the point of a vacation. For seal codes press nothing. For anything else, wait, like the paperwork does."
build.payoff: pure flavor; teaches that named contacts actually move (world continuity the player can verify by flying there).
build.seam: hail autoreply variant in the contactHail copy keyed to contact-roaming state
hones: (a) contact-roaming autoreply in the new hail-response data file
(c) Same new hail-response data file (contact-roaming autoreply).

build.title: The Scheduled Ghost
build.trigger: fires on the seeded schedule of a convoy that no longer exists; every sector day, same clock
build.sees: Every day at the same minute, sensors paint a nine-hull convoy crossing the lane — arrivals logged, traffic advisories issued — and no hull is ever visible. The advisory board still thanks it for right-of-way. It has never been late.
build.payoff: A standing mystery that other systems treat as real (schedule data everywhere); scanning the empty route at the exact minute once per save yields the convoy's final black box.
build.seam: numbered anomaly encounter on a fixed simTime window; black box via salvage_signal seams; advisories via news:publish

build.title: The Ration Ledger
build.trigger: proximity to a long-haul adrift hull; cooldownS 86400
build.sees: A ship two months off-lane, on air rations, sells its log by the page to anyone who hails: "Day forty-one. The cook found a way to make algae taste like regret. Day forty-two. Regret again." It's not begging. It's a business model, and the writing is good.
build.payoff: Buy pages (codex entries, a real serialized story); buy the whole log at the end for the ending; a page you buy is a page they eat better for.
build.seam: numbered ambient encounter with a page-store in state.story.flags; codex additions in src/data/codexPages.js

build.title: The Resignation Letter
build.trigger: drops from the boss wreck of any major pirate fight (priorOutcome 'cleared' on a boss shape); uniqueOnce
build.sees: The warlord's wreck yields, of all things, a sealed letter — a resignation, written to his own pack, dated the day he died, never sent: "Tell them I was tired. Tell them the tolls were getting heavy to carry. Don't tell them I said sorry."
build.payoff: Deliver it to the pack (a succession with less blood than expected — the sector's raid prices actually soften) or keep it (the pack hardens, and the letter is the best item description in your hold).
build.seam: drop attached to boss outcome records (crSituationKit facts); delivery as numbered encounter; faction pricing note via economy intents

build.title: The Sling Chime
build.trigger: proximity — any hull crossing the sling band at above 140 WU/s tangential
