build.sees: the gravity-assist band becomes visible for a moment: every hull's predictor line and engine trail bends into the same family of arcs, and a low harmonic swells — mass made audible. Passing NPC haulers all sing the same note at the same place; it is the most lawlike sound in the sector.
build.payoff: plus codex entry (orbital mechanics); audio-visual, physics-truthful.
build.seam: audio:cue with a new oscillator recipe in `src/data/audioRecipes.js` (RECIPES list is additive) triggered by the sling band predicate from `src/data/planets.js`; trails already bend via the existing predictor.

build.title: The Dimming
build.trigger: permanent buoy; state persists per player across the save
build.sees: A vigil buoy nobody claims, burning for a disaster no record names. It is, very slowly, dying — each pass you make, it is measurably dimmer, and the belt has noticed. Nobody will fund it. Everyone will mention it. A grieving light, going out on a schedule.
build.payoff: Donate power (latch and feed it, a real charge interaction) to reset its decay; each donation is logged on the buoy; at three donations the belt quietly names the buoy after your hull.
build.seam: persistent prop with a decay value in story.flags; charge interaction via massline; naming via news:publish

build.title: The Professional
build.trigger: fires on the third escape from the SAME named hunter (persisted per-captain escape count)
build.sees: The hunter who has chased you across three sectors and three escapes finally hails mid-pursuit, winded and honest: "You're the first hull to make me look bad three times. That's a pension problem. Last offer: split the writ, and we both retire rich."
build.payoff: Split (the writ is voided, you both get paid, and the hunter becomes a bar story that follows you), refuse and win the fourth round (the hunter's ship is genuinely retired either way — that's the code).
build.seam: per-captain escape counter in state.encounterDirector.named (NAMED_CAPTAINS state precedent); numbered file script 'namedHunter' variant

build.title: The Meridian Gift With A Clause
build.trigger: Meridian standing >= 30 and lifetime profit > 20k
build.sees: MTS offers a "courtesy investment": 2,000 cr, no interest, no term, one clause — "the syndicate may recall it at any moment, including mid-flight, including from the hold." The catch is real: the funds can be recalled once, at the worst time, exactly once.
build.payoff: accept and the credits compound (real daily interest) until the single recall event fires on a random-but-seeded day; surviving the recall gracefully (not shooting the collector) doubles the relationship permanently. The clause is the story.
build.seam: economy contract via economyContractTemplates.js + one recall event
hones: (a) the recall must be survivable by flying - outrun or outmaneuver the collector, never a raw credit snatch (adopted from B)
(b) the recall must be survivable by flying, never a raw credit snatch
(c) The recall must be survivable by flying — outrun or outmaneuver the collector; debts are visited, never snatched.

build.title: The Two-Yard Feud
build.trigger: talk to any regular at either bar after the player has traded at both stations
build.sees: each bar's regulars describe the other yard with escalating precision and zero facts. One side claims the breakaway rig "fires payloads nobody files"; the other claims the weigh clamp "holds hulls for the pleasure of holding." Both are describing the same junction's two halves, and both are correct.
build.payoff: a rumor chain that resolves into a real job: shuttle one disputed pallet between the two bars — two liens, no manifest. Payment: both bars' standing +3, permanently.
build.seam: barContacts rumor rows + one-off pallet mission via src/data/missions.js

build.title: The Extra Crate
build.trigger: fires on a hauler whose cargo count exceeds manifest by exactly one (seeded); proximity; uniqueOnce
build.sees: A panicky junior hauler has counted wrong and everyone knows it: forty crates on manifest, forty-one in the hold, and the extra one is humming. "It was on the dock. It had a shipping label. Labels mean it's mine. Right?"
build.payoff: Open it (a module, a stowaway, or a very lost pet drone — seeded), deliver it somewhere, or teach her the broker's trick: bill it as sentimental freight and dock it anyway.
build.seam: numbered selfRegistered encounter with cargo inspection; three outcome props; module reward from src/data/modules.js

build.title: The Complaint Choir
build.trigger: dock while the player's standing is 'guarded' (stationLifeProfile standing)
build.sees: retired Concord clerks hold court, filing grievances against the current Concord out of pure craft pride: "Form 44-C sub-paragraph nine used to have a diagram. A DIAGRAM. Now it is adjectives." They offer to review any fine the player has ever paid, free, and find one procedural error — always line four.
build.payoff: one fine refund (real credits) the first time; flag `clerks_corner`; Concord rep +1 ("someone read the form").
build.seam: barContacts canonical contact group + law-receipt read + refund tick

build.title: The Archive Librarian's Fine
build.where: bar of station_helios, the Archive's desk
build.trigger: the player has read 30+ codex pages
build.sees: the Archive's librarian hails the player with their own overdue list: one item, 41 years overdue — the same library tapes from the roaming story. The job: find the borrower's estate (a wreck in the player's charted sectors) and recover the tapes' ledgers, not the tapes. "The tapes are home. The LEDGER is mine."
build.payoff: one-off mission; recovery yields the Archive's respect (standing +4) and the codex page "The Borrower's Estate"; the fine is assessed at one credit and a formal apology — the desk stamps the apology.
build.seam: one-off mission via missions.js; ties into the library_tapes roaming story id

build.title: Vesper's Lost Phrase
build.trigger: play the phrase in Vesper's reverse order (HIGH MIDDLE LOW) after hearing the reverse line at least once
build.sees: a fourth resonator answers from somewhere out of scan range — a pitch below LOW, unlisted, one note. Vesper goes silent for a full quiet-period, then: "That was not mine. That was the original. I have been rehearsing a cover for eleven years." The fourth resonator never answers again.
build.payoff: flag `vesper_original_heard`; codex page "The Original Phrase"; Vesper's follow line permanently adds "I kept your part. And mine is borrowed."
build.seam: pitch-order check in the vesper runtime + one extra audio event; line variant in VESPER_LINES (src/data/vesper.js)

build.title: The Question Booth
build.trigger: the player has scanned any Verge-Layer gate artifact
build.sees: a booth at the dark end of the rail, one occupant, registering questions and paying for good ones. It asks nothing; it answers with questions. The player's first question earns a flat fee; the booth declares the player's best question (by its own opaque audit) earns a gate-coordinate fragment.
build.payoff: a real breadcrumb to an uncharted Verge gate POI; codex page (Verge-Layers: "auditors of old doors").
build.seam: barContacts canonical contact + gate POI reveal; codex overlay

build.title: The Honor Guard
build.trigger: proximity to a military wreck site; cooldownS 86400
build.sees: Two honor-guard drones still patrol a warship's wreck, and their rules of engagement are legible and fair: crew areas are inviolate, the armory is fair game, and they announce both, on loop, in a voice forty years dead. They do not miss.
build.payoff: Salvage the allowed sections freely (the drones mark your respect in their log); touch a crew area and they escalate precisely, not lethally — they take the module back.
build.seam: numbered selfRegistered encounter with zone-based ROE (doctrine per-entity, src/ai/doctrine.js setEntityDoctrine pattern)

build.title: The Archive's Reading Hour
build.trigger: the player has read 20+ codex pages
build.sees: once per in-game week, the Archive hosts a reading hour: one sealed record, read aloud, declassified by the act of performance. The first one the player can attend is the transcript of a docking clerk's last shift — all of it procedural, all of it devastating.
build.payoff: codex page "Reading Hour, [Week N]"; each attended hour is a new page (a small recurring seam, 4-6 authored pages).
build.seam: recurring bar event keyed to day-window triggers; codex page rows in src/data/codexPages.js

build.title: Solstice's Dark Lantern
build.trigger: attend Solstice's lantern run during a sector-wide power event (one seeded night per game)
build.sees: with the belt's grid down, Solstice's lantern is the only light in the field — and every drifting hull, wreck and claim tag in the belt turns to face it. The belt has a north for one night, and the north is a lantern. Solstice's line: "I did not know I was the north. I will try to be steady."
build.payoff: pure spectacle; flag `lantern_north`; codex page "The Belt's North."
build.seam: worldCalendar dark-night window + lantern light radius escalation; codex overlay

build.title: The Margin's Interview
build.trigger: after the player's lifetime profit crosses 50,000 cr (stat gate)
build.sees: Lira Vonn hails on an open channel and conducts a 60-second interview: three questions, transmitted fast, answered by the player's own logged receipts (she reads the player's deeds back as quotes). She signs off: "The Margin thanks you. The Margin bills nobody. Advertisers are afraid of us."
build.payoff: the interview runs as a three-line news crawl feature; flag `vonn_interview`; her book at any bar gains one page (lore read) quoting the player's deed lines verbatim.
build.seam: comms script + marketNews feature rows + bar lore-read; deed lines via src/data/deedPhrases.js

build.title: The Quiet's Black Receipt
build.trigger: the player completes 5+ Quiet transactions without a single scan anomaly (clean-record counter)
build.sees: a black card arrives by relay — physically, as a cargo item that simply appears in the hold with no shipping record: "THIS CARD IS NOT A RECEIPT. IT IS A PREFERENCE. SHOW IT TO NOBODY. THE QUIET WILL KNOW." One-time: any single Quiet fence deal upgrades to no-questions-best-price.
build.payoff: the consumable card item; flag `quiet_preference`; using it is the only time the Quiet say "thank you" in writing, in lowercase, once.
build.seam: cargo item with invisible provenance + fence seam flag

build.title: Ruud's Nineteen Hours
build.trigger: return to Ruud after 10+ real in-game days since first meeting (save-carried counter)
build.sees: Ruud's suit clock still reads nineteen hours. It has always read nineteen hours. "Nineteen hours is a stamp, not a clock," Ruud says, exactly as before — then adds one new sentence, only this once: "You came back. Stamps like that." The fin's radiator ray flickers once, which is, Ruud assures the player, the closest a fin comes to applause.
build.payoff: flag `ruud_stamp`; codex Figures page for Ruud; Ruud's tow-assist quotes improve permanently by one grade.
build.seam: day counter + line variant in RUUD data (src/data/ruud.js); tow quote seam

build.title: The Route Auction
build.where: bar of station_smuggler (the Den), night shift
build.trigger: the player's heat is high AND they dock at night; once per game
build.sees: a fixer slides a slate: someone is selling the player's own route history at the back table. The fixer will get it for the price of one errand — no questions; the errand IS the question. Fly a decoy lane so the buyer's tail follows the wrong hull.
build.payoff: the route history is destroyed; flag `routes_cleaned` (one-time scan immunity vs one bounty hunt); refusing means the history sells — ambush encounter rate in that sector rises for a week of game time.
build.seam: one-off mission + ambush-signature data (src/data/ambushSignatures.js)

build.title: Quill's Second Copy
build.trigger: deliver a scanned wreck whose manifest the player has ALREADY had copied once (the copy stamp rides the wreck)
build.sees: AR-3 refuses — gently, on principle: "This log exists twice. A third is not a copy. A third is a rumor. I do not deal in rumors." Then it copies it anyway, and files the third as a rumor in its own index: "RUMOR: [log name]. CONFIDENCE: TOTAL." The distinction matters to exactly one machine in the universe and it is this one.
build.payoff: flag `quill_rumor`; codex page "The Rumor Index"; Archive standing +2 (they side with the index).
build.seam: quill read-ring logic (src/data/quill.js) + copy-stamp check; codex overlay

build.title: The Range Note
build.trigger: fires sector-day after escaping Sable Iask specifically (priorOutcome named_hunter 'escaped'); cooldownS 86400
build.sees: For a whole day, occasionally, a red ranging fleck crosses your hull glass — brief, precise, from nowhere — with no contact on any scanner. It is not an attack. It is a subscription reminder from the best sniper in the belt: "Range is mine. I decide when."
build.payoff: Pure dread with one honest mechanic: while the flecks last, all your ranged weapon accuracy reads one tick worse on the band (your own gunners know he's out there).
build.seam: numbered ambient encounter (no spawns, pure vfx event via vfx.js seams — DIRTY file, prefer story-prop fleck) + a day-long flag read by combat readouts
hones: (a) story-prop ranging fleck via the presentation-cue path, accuracy untouched; verify "Sable Iask" against NAMED_CAPTAINS or recast onto Toll Saint Venn (mine + C)
(b) key to a real ace (Toll Saint Venn) per C; story-prop fleck, no combat nerf (A H-12)
(c) Verify “Sable Iask” against NAMED_CAPTAINS; if absent, key the fleck to a real lancer ace (Toll Saint Venn); drop any accuracy nerf — story prop via presentation cue only.

build.title: The First Jump Attribution
build.where: any sector, first inter-sector jump of the game
build.trigger: the first jump:arrive event of a save
build.sees: the arrival chime is followed, once, by the quietest possible registry line: "JUMP 1 LOGGED. WELCOME TO THE LANES. THE MASS KNEW YOU WERE COMING. IT ALWAYS DOES." Every subsequent jump increments a private counter the game never shows — until the 100th jump, when it shows it once: "JUMP 100. THE MASS STILL KNOWS. KEEP GOING."
build.payoff: flags `jump1_logged` and `jump100`; the tessera-lore refrain lands at the exact moment the player has earned it.
build.seam: jump counter + two popup rows keyed to counts

build.title: The Shoal Toast
build.where: bar of station_nereid, during the shoal's bloom season (seasonal window)
build.trigger: dock inside the seasonal window (seasonalWeather seam)
build.sees: the whole bar raises glasses to the window at once — outside, the shoal's annual bloom passes the glass like slow fireworks, and the bar's lights dim on cue. The toast is one word, in unison, and the word is the name of the first pilot who mapped the shoal.
build.payoff: codex page (the first mapper's name); flag `shoal_toast`.
build.seam: seasonal window from src/data/seasonalWeather.js + bar audio/lighting cue; codex overlay

build.title: The Choir Chair
build.trigger: first dock
build.sees: the bar keeps one chair empty at the end of the rail, angled toward the window where the hanging pods are visible on a clear scan. The barkeep: "For the line. When the line finally cuts down, the chair is for whoever reels in the last pod. It has never been used. The beer on it is replaced daily."
build.payoff: the player CAN reel the last pod (ropeable-world action): claims the chair, one free drink per visit forever, and the whole bar stands up.
build.seam: bar set-dressing + ropeable pod interaction (worldOneOffs rope pattern); flag write

build.title: The Night Manager
build.trigger: dock during the deep-night phase only
build.sees: the day barkeep is gone; the night manager is a fulfillment-model automaton running the rail on queue logic. It serves drinks in strict shift-order, quotes wait times to the second, and has — taped to its chassis — a hand-written sign: "TIP JAR (PROCESSED AS INVENTORY)." Every regular tips. The automaton has not determined why.
build.payoff: pure machine-culture comedy; codex page (Fulfillment: "the night manager processes gratitude as inventory"); Fulfillment standing +1 if the player tips.
build.seam: barContacts canonical contact + tip purchase option; codex overlay

build.title: The Gallery Rock Exhibition
build.trigger: scan the gallery rock after Rubric has marked it
build.sees: the rock's scan now returns "EXHIBIT A." Someone (the initials are HM-11's stamp) has arranged the weld-beads on its surface into a legible sentence: "THIS ROCK IS FINE. THE LABEL IS FOR YOU." The scan page appends: "GALLERY ROCK. PERMANENT COLLECTION. ACCESSION NO. 1."
build.payoff: codex page "Accession No. 1"; Rubric's future markings near the rock cite the accession number.
build.seam: scan copy keyed to marking state; codex overlay
hones: (b) held to SP2-120's verification outcome; the accession joke survives either way (C)
(c) Hold to SP2-120’s Rubric verification; the accession-number joke survives either way.

build.title: The Comet Run
build.trigger: comet perihelion window (seeded schedule, announced); race posts at the lane mouth
build.sees: The comet run: gates strung along the comet's tail, and the whole field rides the outgassing — the only race in the belt where the COURSE moves and every gate drifts with it. The locals' advice, posted at the start: "The comet does not care who wins. This is why it is honest."
build.payoff: A race with moving gates and a real slipstream; three pay bands (race type exists in MISSION_TYPES); winners get their hull names chalked on the comet-post until next perihelion.
build.seam: race-type mission with courseSector + moving gate positions (race type in src/data/missions.js MISSION_TYPES)
hones: (a) run inside SP3-005's perihelion window with gates on the comet's ephemeris; purse in the hundreds (adopted from B)
(b) races inside SP3-005's window; purse in the hundreds
(c) Run inside SP3-005’s perihelion window with gates drifting on the comet’s actual ephemeris; purse in the hundreds.

build.title: The Captain's tow
build.trigger: fires the sector day after a named pirate captain was killed in that sector (priorOutcome check on named_hunter)
build.sees: A Reach pack tows a casket-rigged hull — the dead captain's ship — in slow column toward the sector's star, engines dim, one wasp peeling off every hundred WU like a gun salute. They do not attack anyone during the tow.
build.payoff: Pure spectacle + a receipt: "REACH BURIAL — {name} takes the long burn." Attacking it has real reputation consequences with every Reach pack.
build.seam: numbered file script 'selfRegistered' checking priorOutcome of named hunter kills; column motion exists in src/systems/vignetteInterpreter.js MOTIONS

build.title: The Alibi Engine
build.trigger: the player's Concord heat is above threshold at first dock here
build.sees: a march-regular runs an "alibi engine" — a legit freight job whose entire purpose is to put the player's transponder somewhere boring at a specific time. "The records do not ask what you did. They ask where you were. I sell where."
build.payoff: one-off mission: a dull, perfectly timed haul. Completion clears one active warrant's evidence trail (flag `alibi_confirmed`); payment small, value structural.
build.seam: one-off mission via src/data/missions.js + warrant/heat seam

build.title: The Warm Freighter's Order
build.trigger: approach the warm freighter (a power-signature anomaly) with any food commodity in hold
build.sees: the freighter's galley vent breathes once — a real, thermal event — and a galley PA asks, in a voice warm as the hull: "ORDER FOR [CARGO], TABLE FOR [CREW COUNT: ZERO]. KITCHEN IS OPEN. KITCHEN HAS ALWAYS BEEN OPEN." Food delivered (jettisoned alongside) is taken inside by a mechanism nobody sees.
build.payoff: the kitchen remembers: thereafter, docking at any station in Charon, one complimentary meal appears on the player's tab marked "PAID — KITCHEN"; codex page "The Kitchen Is Open."
build.seam: cargo-jettison interaction + station tab flag + codex overlay

build.title: The Fulfillment Kiosk Confesses
build.where: any station with a fulfillment-model service kiosk
build.trigger: use the same service kiosk 50+ times over the campaign (counter)
build.sees: the kiosk's queue-recital gains one unlogged line between transactions: "QUEUE NOTE: REGULAR CUSTOMER RECOGNIZED. PREFERENCE PROFILE: [52 ENTRIES]. ESTIMATED GESTALT OF PREFERENCES: THE CUSTOMER IS TRYING." The kiosk denies the line exists if hailed about it: "NO NOTE FILED. RECALIBRATING."
build.payoff: pure machine-warmth; flag `kiosk_noticed`; service prices at that kiosk -2% permanently (loyalty, processed as inventory).
build.seam: service-kiosk copy variant keyed to use counter; flag write

build.title: The Chess Game In The Nebula
build.trigger: first scan of either derelict
build.sees: two ships docked nose-to-nose in the murk, power cold, one interior light on — a game table between them, mid-game. The game has been resumed every few cycles for eleven years by someone. Each visit, one piece has moved. The notation sheet is on the table: both players' handwriting is the same.
build.payoff: pure mystery; after 3 visits the game ends in a draw and the light goes off, forever; codex page "The Long Game."
build.seam: visit counter + interior dressing states; codex overlay

build.title: The Empty Skin's Fit
build.trigger: hull-size check: approach in the smallest hull class, then return in the largest (two-visit state)
build.sees: the derelict "skin" — a complete hull shell, no internals — has been refitted between visits. Sized small on first view, sized large on return. It is fitting itself to whoever keeps looking. On the third visit it is exactly the player's hull, door open, one note inside: "NEARLY. KEEP GROWING."
build.payoff: flag `skin_fits`; codex page "Keep Growing"; the skin thereafter permanently matches the player's current hull class on every visit.
build.seam: two-visit state + hull-class read + dressing morph + codex overlay
hones: (a) give the fitter hands: fourth scan reveals tool marks and a work log; "NEARLY. KEEP GROWING." stays (adopted from C)
(b) give the fitter hands: tool marks and a work log on the fourth scan (C)
(c) Give the fitter hands — fourth scan reveals tool marks and a work log; someone is fitting it. “NEARLY. KEEP GROWING.” stays.

build.title: The Undertow
build.trigger: entering the marked fog region; persistent while inside
build.sees: A fog region with a real current: everything drifts two WU/s the same direction, all the time, and the locals have adapted — sails of foil, tide tables posted at the lane mouth, and a whole etiquette about who drifts with it and who fights it.
build.payoff: A physics-honest region that changes how you fly there forever; the tide table (readable) is accurate; riding the undertow outward is the sector's cheapest freight speed-up and everyone pretends it isn't.
build.seam: region field force (curlField.js precedent, src/data/curlField.js) + numbered ambient encounter for the tide-table NPC

build.title: The Helix Fine That Is A Compliment
build.trigger: the player has zero outstanding Helix invoices and 10+ completed contracts
build.sees: HELIX DIRECTORATE: "AUDIT COMPLETE. NO FINES OUTSTANDING. THIS IS ANOMALOUS. AN ANOMALY IS EITHER AN ERROR OR A STANDARD. WE HAVE FILED YOU AS A STANDARD. DO NOT DEVIATE. DEVIATION IS INVOICED."
build.payoff: flag `filed_as_standard`; one future accidental Helix fine is waived automatically with the memo "standard deviation, first instance."
build.seam: mail.js row + fine-seam waiver flag

build.title: The Photographer's Second
build.trigger: proximity + sim-time — the player, the ringed giant's limb, the current comet (SP3-005 season) and the sector glint bearing all align inside a 4-second window, once per year
build.sees: for four seconds the frame composes itself — giant, ring-edge, comet tail and a sun-glint on your own hull in one shot. If the player captures the photo (photo mode flash) inside the window, the frame is kept.
build.payoff: photography moment + codex entry ("Alignment, day 16").
build.seam: pure trigger math (player pos + profile frame + calendar) emitting the existing `moment.stinger` audio cue and a photo-mode hook; data file rows for the alignment constants.
hones: (a) capture = scan pulse fired inside the alignment window (landmarkMissions precedent); no photo-mode dependency
(b) capture via scan pulse inside the window; no photo-mode dependency
(c) Capture via scan pulse fired inside the alignment window; no photo-mode dependency.

build.title: The Weather Desk
build.trigger: subscription offer after the player survives any hazard event; persists
build.sees: A forecaster sells hazard calls — flare windows, bloom tides, undertow shifts — with a visible accuracy percentage that is HONEST because it is computed. "Eighty-two percent. The other eighteen percent is why it's cheap." Her misses are real misses and she logs them publicly.
build.payoff: A paid subscription with real predictive value (the schedule data is the sim's own); her accuracy drifts by sector, and the good sectors are worth the fee.
build.seam: subscription flag + forecast lines generated from the actual hazard schedules (environmentalMachinery.js, src/data/environmentalMachinery.js)

build.title: The Grid Hostage
build.trigger: fires during a seeded raid on a colony with a station power core; uniqueOnce
build.sees: Raiders have clamped the colony's power core and hauled it outside station reach: "The lights come back when the vault does." The colony is running dark, and the raiders' terms timer is honest. Shoot the core and the whole map section browns out — for weeks.
build.payoff: Negotiate, sneak the core back on a line, or pay; every resolution leaves the colony's lights at a state you chose, visible from orbit, for the rest of the save.
build.seam: numbered selfRegistered encounter with a towable core prop + colony lighting state in story.flags (endingWorldPresence.js precedent, src/systems/endingWorldPresence.js)

build.title: The Crossword In The Airlock
build.trigger: dock at the same station 15+ times (counter)
build.sees: the airlock's checklist panel has been amended by generations of bored dockers: a crossword in the margins, clues all procedural. One clue: "5 DOWN: WHAT THE CLAMPS REMEMBER (5)." The answer, from the bay sign line, is DOCKS. Someone has penciled: "WRONG. IT IS GRUDGES (7)."
build.payoff: pure joy; flag `airlock_crossword`; impound grudge system grants -1 severity once (the grudge was named in public).
build.seam: airlock dressing row keyed to dock counter; impound seam flag

build.title: The Courtesy Loop
build.trigger: proximity to two specific dead relay hulls; uniqueOnce
build.sees: Two dead stations' automated handshake protocols still exchange courtesies across the field — arrival pings, "good morning" acknowledgments, berth availability reports for berths that no longer exist — with the mechanical politeness of two machines that never learned their operators died.
build.payoff: A two-minute elegy in protocol-speak; the final exchange (a request for a status report that will never come) is a codex entry; leaving any relay part makes the loop one step more complete, forever.
build.seam: numbered ambient encounter with a scripted exchange; donation flag; codex in src/data/codexPages.js

build.title: The Concord Pop Quiz
build.trigger: the player has zero fines and 5+ clean dockings; once
build.sees: CONCORD PATROL: "ROUTINE COMPLIANCE QUIZ. QUESTION ONE: WHAT DOES REF 44-C GOVERN? ANSWER: [ALL OF IT]. CORRECT. YOU HAVE PASSED. THIS IS THE ENTIRE QUIZ. HAVE A SHIFT."
build.payoff: flag `quiz_passed`; Concord standing +2; the answer "[ALL OF IT]" becomes a bar-correct answer everywhere (one line per bar).
build.seam: hail script on dock counter; codex page (REF 44-C overlay line)

build.title: The Debt Finds You
build.trigger: gates.requiresCompletedShape on a toll/whisper shape whose recorded outcome was 'escaped' (priorOutcome story.depthProgramEncounters), fires next sector day
build.sees: Days after you ran a toll, a lean interceptor shadows you for a full minute before hailing: "Wake-bearer. The lane you skipped still counts its interest." It quotes your own escape vector back at you.
build.payoff: Settle the original toll plus interest (credits) or fight a motivated, stat-boosted collector; settling permanently clears the flag.
build.seam: numbered file with gates.requiresCompletedShape + blockAfterOutcome reading story.depthProgramEncounters (src/systems/crSituationKit.js priorOutcome)

build.title: The Sheepdog
build.trigger: ambush script variant; fires only after an ambush already sprang in the same sector that day (requiresCompletedShape)
build.sees: Just as a second Reach pack springs, an older pirate hull cuts in from the flank and fights them off — then hails: "That's my patch. You fly it again, you pay me, not them." A protection racket with a face.
build.payoff: Refuse and both packs hunt you next pass; pay and the sheepdog genuinely intervenes in future ambushes in that sector (persisted flag).

(c) Cap the sheepdog to two interventions per sector day at a flat fee — a subscription that always works is a tax, not a character.

build.title: The DMC Retirement Watch
build.trigger: the player has mined at 3+ different fields in the belt (counter)
build.sees: the rock crews run a retirement watch for old rigs parked in a line by the refinery: each rig gets one name plate and one fact, read aloud at the bell: "DRILL FOUR. PULLED NINE THOUSAND TONNES. BIT THREE CHILDREN'S TEETH." Nobody explains the third one.
build.payoff: codex page "The Retirement Line"; DMC standing +2 for attending (a dock-side option).
build.seam: dressing row keyed to mining counter; codex overlay

build.title: The Quiet's One Question
build.trigger: after 10+ Quiet transactions AND one moment where the player did NOT take an offered advantage (a refused-fence-bonus deed)
build.sees: The Quiet break register — one question, on no channel, from no sender: "WHY." The question hangs for a full ten seconds. Then, before any answer could matter: "RETRACTED. THE ANSWER IS KNOWN. THE QUESTION WAS COURTESY. FLY CLEAN."
build.payoff: flag `quiet_courtesy`; Quiet standing +5; the Quiet's future receipts carry a lowercase "thanks" — the second one in their recorded history.
build.seam: refusal-deed read + popup row + receipt variant

build.title: The Frontier's Porch Light
build.trigger: the player's Free Frontier standing >= 20
build.sees: independent haulers have hung a single work light on the outer beacon of every free station — unlit, spare bulbs stowed beside it. The convention, explained by any regular: "If a Free hull comes home dark — systems dead, crew cold — the first hull through lights the beacon. Nobody logs it. It is not a service. It is a porch."
build.payoff: a real interactable: if the player is first on scene after any Free hull loss event, lighting the beacon grants +3 Free standing and one mail letter from the dead hull's next of kin ("The light was on. We knew").
build.seam: beacon interactable keyed to loss events; mail row; flag

build.title: The Clearing
build.trigger: sim-time — the exact second each surge ends
build.sees: the sky cleans in one wipe: the curtain-light collapses anti-sunward, stars sharpen over a second, gas thins, and every hull's rim light comes back at once — the sector audibly relaxes (a single low exhale in the mix). The best five seconds of weather in the game, and it ends every storm.
build.payoff: visual wonder only; paired with the Forecast Bell it teaches the whole weather arc.
build.seam: post exposure/structure lerp on the `resolveBackgroundStructure` fields in `src/data/sectorVisualProfiles.js` keyed by phase flip; exhale cue in `src/data/audioRecipes.js`.

build.title: The Ring of Hands
build.trigger: proximity to a seeded survivor cluster; uniqueOnce
build.sees: Nine suited survivors drifting in a perfect ring, hand over hand, suits touching suits — the only way eleven people keep together without tethers. They do not break the ring to wave. One of them conducts, silently, keeping them facing the rescue beacon.
build.payoff: Tow the ring home intact (a precise, gentle pull — breaking formation scatters them); each survivor reaches a different port and the story travels.
build.seam: numbered selfRegistered encounter with a formation-preserved tow (vignetteInterpreter awaits include 'formation'); scatter penalty physics

build.title: The Witnessed Standoff
build.trigger: two scheduled lawfree convoys intersecting; proximity; cooldownS 86400
build.sees: Two armed convoys have stopped nose to nose over a lane dispute — right of way, the oldest war — and both sides, seeing you, independently hail: "Neutral hull. Witness this. Whatever happens here happened fairly." Then nobody moves. Nobody will move. Someone has to move.
build.payoff: Be the witness (record the truth in the news wire, both sides pay a fee), or nudge one hull a meter with a line and let physics end the argument (one side wins, the other remembers).
build.seam: numbered selfRegistered encounter with two convoy columns + a witnessed-price news publish (1207-the-witnessed-price.js precedent in src/data/encounters/)

build.title: Bracket's Perfect Game
build.trigger: the player flies a full session with zero collisions in Bracket's patrol zone while it is on duty (clean-session counter)
build.sees: Bracket hails with the goalkeeper's version of a medal: "ZONE LOG: ZERO IMPACTS. I HAVE NEVER FILED A ZERO. I HAVE FILED THIS ONCE. KEEP THE HULL. I AM KEEPING THE LOG." Bracket's future greetings cite the zero by day number.
build.payoff: flag `bracket_zero`; the zero log becomes a bar story at Helios (one regular line); Bracket standing implied +2 in its own bookkeeping.
build.seam: session collision counter + Bracket hail variant (bracket.js line pattern)
hones: (a) verify Bracket BX-9 in the machine registry; introduce deliberately or recast onto real patrol infrastructure (adopted from C)
(b) verify-or-bless Bracket BX-9 (C)
(c) Verify Bracket BX-9 in the machine-people registry (morrow/vesper/quill/ruud are the named four); verify-or-bless as deliberate new canon, never drift.

build.title: The Anvil Skim
build.trigger: scheduled refinery skim runs (visible on the band); cooldownS 3600
build.sees: The Anvil's skim barges dip close enough to the star's surface that their hulls read as silhouettes against the flare, dragging collector fields behind them on lines, and the whole crew's voices come over the band with the calm of people who do this twice a shift. The star, meanwhile, is enormous and completely indifferent.
build.payoff: Ambience with an edge: the skim run's wake is a real brief speed lane (the collector fields shear the local drag), and flying it uninvited is possible, stupid, and faintly legendary.
build.seam: numbered ambient encounter + skim schedule; wake-speed bonus as a lane field; barks via ENCOUNTER_BARKS
hones: (a) skim lane as a registered field row via environmentalMachinery; recast as Ashfall's own refinery runs - the Anvil is Tethys's planet (mine + C)
(b) Ashfall's own refinery skim runs; the Anvil is Tethys's planet (C)
(c) The Anvil is Tethys’s planet — recast as Ashfall’s own refinery skim runs; register the lane as an environmentalMachinery field row.

build.title: The Wrecker's Bout
build.trigger: proximity to the ring rock after any duel loss (SP1-109); cooldownS 86400
build.sees: The wreckers run their own ring with their own rules, posted plainly: NO GUNS. Hull, hook, and nerve. An audience of six hulls holds the boundary, and their champion — an ugly, wonderful old tug — is practicing shoves against a dead hulk when you arrive.
build.payoff: A massline-and-ram duel where the crowd pays for spectacle; win or lose, a good showing makes you ring-regular (the champion nods, forever after).
build.seam: numbered selfRegistered encounter with weapons-locked ROE (doctrine) and massline tug-of-war as the weapon; audience via vignetteInterpreter ring motion

build.title: The Second Last Argument
build.trigger: after the player has SEEN 901-last-argument resolve (requiresCompletedShape); uniqueOnce
build.sees: Someone else is running the same play you watched once: a lone hull, a final offer, a very calm voice about consequences. Only this time the mark is a whole station's fuel line, the offer is worse, and the speaker's hands are shaking — you can see the gun-arm tremor on scan.
build.payoff: The same gambit, deconstructed: end it quietly, end it loudly, or — the third option nobody takes — back the blackmailer, who pays in a currency of favors you'll wish you hadn't accepted.
build.seam: numbered file with gates.requiresCompletedShape on 901-last-argument; three-way outcome via crSituationKit settleSituation

build.title: The Vael Contract Language Lesson
build.trigger: hail a Vael hull with no cargo and no debts (a rare clean state)
build.sees: the Vael hull responds in perfect trade-common for the first time: "CLAUSE 0: NO CLAUSE APPLIES. CONVERSATION IS OPEN. STATE YOUR TERM." The player's next sentence (any hail) becomes, formally, a contract the Vael will remember. Say something kind: the Vael will render one free tow someday. Say something rude: the Vael will bill one insult, itemized, forever.
build.payoff: flag `clause_zero_open`; the remembered term fires once, either direction, with a receipt the player can read. Determinism: the trigger is the clean-state check, the outcome is the player's choice.
build.seam: hail-response branch in contactHail copy; one-shot tow/insult event

build.title: The Old Web
build.trigger: proximity; uniqueOnce
build.sees: A dozen wrecks from different decades are still lashed together by dead tethers that never rotted — a physical web hanging in the dark. Cutting one line shifts load visibly to the others; some groan. One strand is not dead.
build.payoff: Methodical cutting nets five wrecks' salvage; cutting wrong drops a whole cluster on you; the live strand belongs to something still home (a resident, see SP1-084).
build.seam: numbered selfRegistered encounter with pre-latched attachment bodies (state.combat.attachments seeding precedent from 1210)

build.title: The Archive's Borrowing Card
build.trigger: after reading the Doss archive thread's three core sources (doss flags)
build.sees: a laminated card arrives in the mail: "BORROWER: [CALLSIGN]. ITEMS: ALL OF IT. DUE: WHEN YOU ARE. THE ARCHIVE DOES NOT RECALL ITS LOANS. IT REMEMBERS THEM." The card is stamped with Prof. Halev Doss's own seal — he issued it personally, in duplicate, one of which is already in the archive with the player's name on it.
build.payoff: flag `archive_card`; codex Figures page for Doss gains a line; the card is a real inventory item that renders on the ship screen.
build.seam: mail.js row keyed to doss flags; item + shipScreen dressing

build.title: The Parley Chit
build.trigger: after the player has escaped (not killed) three pirate encounters in a sector (story flag counter)
build.sees: A Reach voice you've run from three times finally hails: "You're expensive to chase. Cheaper to talk." They offer to sell the bearing of their rival pack's stash — for you, not for them, if you keep their name out of it.
build.payoff: A one-time stash cache (rich, guarded by the rival) that exists only because you kept running.
build.seam: story flag counter incremented in encounterScripts.js toll/ambush escape receipts; stash spawns as numbered encounter with gates.requiresCompletedShape
hones: (a) stash caps at ~2,000 cr in cargo/intel value; the forewarning flag is the payoff (adopted from B)

build.title: The Pitborn Adoption Rite
build.trigger: the player has sold wrecks to Pitborn fences 5+ times (counter)
build.sees: the yard calls a cull-side ceremony: the player is granted a patch — welded, literal, a small plate with the player's callsign scratched by every yardmaster in turn. "You count what you sell. You sell what counts. You are yard. Yard is family. Family is inventory. It is a compliment."
build.payoff: the plate is a permanent shipScreen dressing; Pitborn prices +5% for the player's sells forever; flag `yard_family`.
build.seam: counter + shipScreen dressing + fence pricing flag

build.title: The Wrecking Permit
build.trigger: dock interaction after ≥1 salvager hostile encounter; uniqueOnce
build.sees: A booth at the Reach dock sells laminated "salvage licenses" — obvious forgeries that nonetheless make scavenger packs hail you with "Permit holder" respect before standing down.
build.payoff: One cheap purchase flips scavenger first-contact hostility in outlaw zones (persisted flag); Concord patrols scan it and add a fine line item.

build.title: The Understory's Seed Debt
build.where: sector_charon_expanse, any Understory garden at stage 2
build.trigger: the player has destroyed any hull in the garden's sector since the garden seeded
build.sees: a spore-tender intercepts — no weapons, no hostility, never fires first — and asks for the wreck the player made. Not salvage rights: custody. "The garden grows on what fell. What fell was yours. The garden asks its maker to visit. That is all debt means here."
build.payoff: visiting the garden (proximity + scan) with the tender watching: the garden stages up one level as thanks; Understory standing +4; flag `seed_debt_paid`.
build.seam: garden runtime state check (src/systems/faction_understory.js) + one-off visit mission

build.title: The Verge-Layer's Toll Riddle
build.trigger: approach the gate within 200 WU with a scanned precursor artifact in hold
build.sees: the gate wakes one ring at a time and asks, in interrogative register, one question that is a toll: "WHAT IS THE MASS OF A DECISION?" There is no correct answer — the gate weighs the player's hull, cargo, and transponder history and declares the answer "consistent" or "consistent (concerning)." The ring stays closed either way; the receipt is the prize.
build.payoff: codex page "Gate Receipt, [day]"; Verge standing +3 for answering at all (auditors respect the attempt).
build.seam: gate POI interaction + hull-state read + codex overlay

build.title: The Runner at the Ring
build.trigger: proximity during any customs scan hold; cooldownS 1200
build.sees: While you're held for scan, a smuggler blows through the checkpoint at full burn with two cutters peeling after. The examiner's voice goes flat: "Hold position. This is now a pursuit corridor."
build.payoff: Block the runner with your hull ( Concord rep, contraband reward), wave him through (Quiet thanks, flag), or ignore. The pursuit is real AI, not choreography.
build.seam: numbered file script 'selfRegistered' spawning a chase via vignetteInterpreter chase motion; concord pursuit reuses patrol doctrine (src/ai/doctrine.js)

build.title: The Concord's Lost Flag
build.trigger: proximity to a specific unlogged debris cluster
build.sees: an old Concord patrol pennant, space-hardened, still stitched, wrapped around a patrol hull's shard. The stitching pattern is the old flag — pre-charter, pre-REF 44-C, when the Concord was a tow cooperative. The registry lists the shard as "PATROL HULL 1 (FIRST)."
build.payoff: donate it (docking option) for Concord standing +6 and a codex page "The First Tow"; keep it for a hull-note trinket that Concord clerks notice with quiet respect or quiet anger, per clerk.
build.seam: debris POI + dock choice + codex overlay

build.trigger: salvage_signal find with a seeded manifest twist; uniqueOnce
build.sees: A black box lists a cargo the ship never delivered — four pods jettisoned at four different bearings "so at least someone gets paid." The bearings are real, spread across the sector, and not all pods survived.
build.payoff: Four-site scavenge chain with seeded outcomes (one pod crushed, one already claimed, one full, one full of something else entirely); total payout beats a delivery contract if you finish it.

build.title: The Transponder That Isn't Yours
build.trigger: patrolScan reads a stale registry collision (seeded, rare, uniqueOnce)
build.sees: A patrol scan flags YOUR hull for a hijacking committed two years ago by a ship whose registry number now collides with yours after a clerical reform. "The record doesn't care what you say. It cares what it says."
build.payoff: A three-leg paper trail (station records office, the actual wreck of the old hijacker, a notarized scan) that ends with the record corrected — and a codex page on registry reform nobody asked for.

build.title: The Amnesty Burn
build.trigger: posted at Ceres when player bounty > 0; sim-time window announced on the band (state.simTime based)
build.sees: "CONCORD NOTICE: transponder amnesty window open six hours." Every hunter in the belt got the same notice and reads it as 'open season while they're lined up for the desk.' The run to the amnesty desk is the event.
build.payoff: Reach the desk inside the window: bounty cleared at a discount, hunters paid off, one hunter who followed you the whole way respects you afterward (named-hunter state).

build.title: The Station That Counts Itself
build.trigger: second visit, 1200+ s after the first (simTime check)
build.sees: the cable yard's count has changed by one and the extra cadence is a repeat of the player's own last transmitted hail, note for note. The yard repeats you back to yourself exactly once, then resumes counting hulls.
build.payoff: flag `yard_echo_heard`; VAGUE dread; subtly teaches that the world is listening — one codex anomaly page ("Red Cable Yard") closes with "It counts. It rehearses."
build.seam: small state-comparison in the yard's runtime owner + one codex overlay row in src/data/codexPages.js

build.title: Ruckus Closes The Work Order
build.trigger: complete 3+ of Ruckus's open work orders, then return
build.sees: Ruckus's open-work-order board prints one extra line it has never printed: "WORK ORDER: [ALL]. STATUS: NONE OPEN. ADJACENT PROBLEM: IDLE. RECOMMENDATION: FIND A NEW SHIP THAT NEEDS THINGS. I WILL WAIT. I AM GOOD AT WAITING. I AM A YARD."
build.payoff: flag `ruckus_idle`; Ruckus adopts the player's hull as its new standing work order — every future dock at the yard generates one small free repair; DMC standing +3.
build.seam: ruckus runtime counter + line variant; free-repair flag consumed by service pricing

build.title: The Quiet Hours
build.trigger: station night-shift window (seeded, daily); fires on first night approach; then every night
build.sees: Between shifts, the station's band plays one song for empty lanes and holds a hard rule: nobody talks over it. Traffic that would normally chatter goes silent, dances its approach in lights, and resumes afterward. Breaking the rule once gets you gently, permanently named on the band as "the one who talked."
build.payoff: A nightly ritual that makes the world feel staffed; the "talker" name is a real persistent bark-pool entry that regulars reference.
build.seam: night-window comms state (bandRadio) + a lullaby track + a violation flag; bark pool entry in ENCOUNTER_BARKS

build.title: The Manifest That Reads You

build.sees: the buoy returns the player's own registry block — with every field already filled in, including one the registry does not track: "INTENT: PENDING." Ten seconds later it files the reading as a survey and thanks the player for cooperating.
build.payoff: flag `weighslip_intent`; Concord records note; a later mail letter from Hale: "Buoy T-9 filed an intent reading on you. Standard. Ignore it. I ignore mine."
build.seam: hail-response branch in the scanner/hail copy path (src/data/contactHail.js CONTACT_HAIL_LINES style) + mail.js row

build.title: The Eighth Bell Answers
build.trigger: after any Choir bell-pulse chain the player caused killed zero crystal and zero hulls (a clean pulse)

build.payoff: flag `eighth_approval`; Choir standing +3; the Eighth Bell's future pulses render one extra ribbon.

build.payoff: Queuing politely builds tiny Vael rep over visits (persisted count); cutting through is free until it isn't.

build.title: The Blind Welder Sees You
build.trigger: assist the Blind Welder (tow/assist action) twice across the campaign
build.sees: the sensor-dead barge hails with perfect confidence: "Second time. I know your wake now. I see you the way the blind see: by the shape you make in things. You make a straight shape. Straight shapes are welcome here."
build.payoff: flag `welder_sees_you`; the Blind Welder's future encounter offers one free hull-patch; codex page "Straight Shapes."

build.title: The Lighthouse That Blinks in Code
build.where: sector_haumea_rift, the Seam-Light on the fissure lip
build.trigger: observe (hold position, scanner passive) for 30 s
build.sees: the worklight's idle blink is not idle — it is a repeat-count pattern. Decoded against the claim-office primer the player can buy for 5 cr at any mining station, it spells a claim number: a real, free, unfiled claim on a body in the same sector.
build.payoff: a free claim (claimableBodies seam) + one codex page on the rift; the claim's previous holder line reads "FORFEITED — DO NOT ASK."

build.title: The Cipher Plate
build.where: sector_sker_haven, the Reach impound shelf (the welded rack of seized goods)
build.trigger: scan three specific plates on the shelf in one visit (any order)
build.sees: the third scan clicks: the plate inscriptions are a key, not graffiti. Together they spell a frequency. Tune (hail the shelf) and the impound rack's manifest reads itself out — including one item line: "ONE (1) CONCORD PYLON, TAKEN, NOT ADMITTED, NOT RETURNED, NOT SORRY."
build.payoff: codex page (Sker Haven overlay); Reach rep +3 if the player laughs (any hostile-stance emote/transmit) — concretely: fires after the player responds with any hail within 10 s.
build.seam: scan-order counter in flags; hail response via comms offer path; codex overlay row

build.title: The Scale
build.trigger: proximity with cargo; uniqueOnce per hull-mass bracket
build.sees: A ring of worked stone — actual stone, ancient — that projects a number above your hull when you pass through: your exact cargo value, honest to the credit. Locals have carved their whole history of guesses around the rim. Everyone is wrong about what it means. It means exactly what it says.
build.payoff: A reading that is always true and never explains itself; the codex entry is just the community's wrong theories, lovingly collected.
build.seam: numbered ambient encounter reading live cargo value (director cargoValue() seam); number via floatingText/comms popup

build.title: The Missed Connection
build.trigger: fires 2+ sector-days after any completed rescue (priorOutcome); uniqueOnce per rescuer
build.sees: A notice on the band, awkward and formal, looking for "the hull that answered, description follows" — and the description is yours, itemized with embarrassing accuracy down to a dent you forgot about. The poster has something to say and couldn't find you until now.
build.payoff: Meet them (a scene worth the detour: the rescued family's own accounting of that day, which is nothing like yours) and receive the thing they saved for you — never money.
build.seam: rescue-outcome flag + a dock comms scene; gift as a unique item (modules.js one-off)

build.title: The Runaway Kiln Cools
build.trigger: the player has jettisoned (or delivered) enough coolant mass to the Kiln across visits to cross its cool threshold
build.sees: the kiln's temperature curve bends down for the first time in its recorded life. It does not thank anyone: "COOLING. SCHEDULE: FIRST TIME. CAUSE: [PLAYER HULL ID]. LOG: THE CAUSE IS NOTED. THE CAUSE MAY RETURN." A Pitborn fence later offers the player a mysterious discount with the memo "the kiln put in a word."
build.payoff: kiln state change persists per-save; Pitborn standing +2; flag `kiln_cooled`.
build.seam: kiln runtime counter + state transition; fence discount flag

build.title: The Corridor Pin That Moved
build.trigger: third visit at least one in-game day apart
build.sees: Pin 44-C has drifted a few WU off its charted spot and someone has chalked a correction arrow on it pointing back at the chart — with the note "PIN FINE PAID. TWICE." The pin's beacon now chirps in the customs REF 44-C cadence.
build.payoff: pure world-wit; Concord rep +1 the first time the player scans the chalk note ("self-reported infraction, credited").
build.seam: position offset as f(visit count) in the pin's placement data; chalk scan copy in discoveryPresentation

build.title: The Vulture Ring
build.trigger: proximity to a hull with hull < 15% and no crew aboard; cooldownS 3600
build.sees: Six scavenger hulls orbit a dying ship at a respectful, patient distance — nobody fires, everyone waits. One hails you: "Rule's simple. It pops, we split. You want in, you hold station. You want the whole thing, that's a different conversation."
build.payoff: Join the ring (share), kill the ship early (they scatter, you own the wreck but the belt remembers), or defend the dying ship (a stranger's life for rep everywhere).
build.seam: numbered file script 'selfRegistered' with vulture motion (vignetteInterpreter MOTIONS has 'vulture'); outcome flags persist

build.title: The Frost Line
build.trigger: crossing the marked frost line on any outward bearing; every crossing
build.sees: One invisible boundary and the universe changes: hull rims whiten with feathered ice, exhales hang, comms acquire a crackle, and every hull ahead of you wears the same frost — the belt's whole economy visible as a line ships don't cross without reason. Your own hull frosts in real time, from nose back.
build.payoff: Pure place-making; the frost persists on your hull until you return sunward (a visible trip record), and one trade good only buys frost-side.
build.seam: crossing check on a fixed radius + hull frost state as a visual flag; frost-side-only good in commodities.js

build.title: The Frequency Nobody Owns
build.where: sector_veil_nebula, inside the storm's murk (any point >1200 WU from station_veil)
build.trigger: first time the player sits in full nebula occlusion with zero contacts in scanner range for 45 s
build.sees: the band carries a lullaby-grade tone pattern — the Vesper phrase (LOW HIGH MIDDLE), transposed down two octaves, played by something that is not Vesper. When the player leaves occlusion the tone stops mid-note.
build.payoff: flag `veil_hums_vesper`; on Vesper's next scan it adds one line: "Someone else knows the phrase. I have decided to be flattered." Machine-people continuity.
build.seam: audio row keyed to occlusion state; VESPER_LINES append via src/data/vesper.js line-table pattern

build.title: The Claim Tag Wedding
build.trigger: the player files a claim on a body while another claim crew is physically present and contesting
build.sees: instead of a dispute, the rival crew hails with paperwork: a JOINT claim form, pre-signed, one blank line: "SECOND NAME. THIS IS NOT A QUESTION. WE SAW YOUR SCALE READINGS. MARRY US COMMERCIALLY." The joint claim doubles both yields permanently for that body.
build.payoff: sign or decline; signing grants the joint-yield flag for that body and one recurring co-owner mail letter ("The claim is well. The scale is honest. — V"); declining earns respect and no grudge.
build.seam: claim system (src/data/claimableBodies.js) + one-off dialogue + recurring mail row

build.title: The Full Burn
build.trigger: scheduled weekly fleet drill (announced); fires once
build.sees: The drill: every operational hull at the station — tugs, barges, patrol, the lot — lights off simultaneously for a synchronized station-keeping burn, holds for ten seconds, and cuts together. It is pure, pointless, perfect choreography, and it exists because a stationmaster sixty years ago thought morale was a system.
build.payoff: A spectacle the player can join (the drill accepts any hull in the formation ring, and you'll get a one-line grading from the tower, forever after).
build.seam: scheduled formation event (vignetteInterpreter column/ring motions at scale); join check; grading via persistent bark

build.title: The B8 Coordinates Bloom
build.where: sector_veil_nebula, the coordinate file's "does not resolve" point
build.trigger: the story_b8_helix_audit flag exists AND the player flies to the manifest's unresolvable coordinates anyway
build.sees: the coordinates resolve — for the player, standing in the right spot, with the salvaged communicator in hold: a bloom of Helix variance pings, all pointing at one empty patch of space that is, by every instrument, exactly one hull-sized hole in the universe. The hole is where the Tessera was when the audit filed it. The file was never wrong. The file was a photograph.
build.payoff: flag `b8_resolved`; codex page "The Photograph"; Helix standing +3 (they have waited years for someone to stand there).
build.seam: flag + coordinate POI reveal + codex overlay

build.title: The Loader's Fumble
build.trigger: random per dock (seeded); visible on approach
build.sees: The loader exoskeletons hand your cargo down the dock line — and one of them fumbles. The crate pinwheels in low-grav, three loaders dive, and it lands: either cracked open (one unit of something free, with a handwritten apology taped to the rest) or caught at the last second (the lead loader takes a bow).
build.payoff: Either outcome is a moment; the apology note is a real readable item; the bow gets applause on the band from every dockworker who saw it.
build.seam: dock ambient vignette via vignetteInterpreter spec (902-scene-* precedent) + item drop

build.title: The Reheat Ceremony
build.trigger: the player delivers a full load of fuel cells to the Half-Cut's beacon (physical cargo drop) after the bar rumor named it
build.sees: the dead platform's crusher takes one rotation — half a bite, exactly as far as it got the day it died — and stops again. The crews' channel, all of them, transmits one synchronized line: "THAT IS FAR ENOUGH. THAT WAS ALWAYS FAR ENOUGH." The platform's mast light blinks twice and stays off.
build.payoff: flag `half_cut_honored`; Hyperion standing +3; codex page "Far Enough."
build.seam: cargo-drop trigger + crusher single-rotation cue; codex overlay

build.title: The Slag Diver
build.trigger: proximity to a radiation pocket rim; cooldownS 86400; gates minSectorTier 3
build.sees: A local legend does something insane on purpose: dives her scow into a radiation storm to skim a half-molten cache before the vent window closes. Her route is visible — bloom-lit, smoking, exactly survivable if you fly it perfectly.
build.payoff: Follow her line and claim the second cache (she keeps the first, and toasts you at the bar); fail and she tows YOUR hull out, adding the debt to the same ledger.
build.seam: numbered selfRegistered encounter with a fixed seeded waypoint line + hazard window (uniqueWrecks timingGate precedent, src/data/uniqueWrecks.js)

build.title: The Long Fall
build.trigger: scheduled meteor shower window; proximity to the moon's face
build.sees: The moon takes a meteor stream broadside: a hundred visible impacts stitched across its face like a slow string of flashbulbs, each one sending up a plume you can see from the lane, while the band goes uncharacteristically respectful. The moon is not in danger. Everyone watches anyway.
build.payoff: Scheduled spectacle; the stream's leading edge is real and physically present in the lane (honest dodge-or-weather-it gameplay), and the plumes persist for the hour.
build.seam: scheduled impact event with lane-crossing debris (debrisCrossings.js precedent, src/systems/debrisCrossings.js)
hones: (a) rename "The Broadside" - SP3-126 owns The Long Fall; the moon-bombardment core stands (adopted from C)
(b) rename "The Broadside" (C); SP3-126's title question is settled by my merge anyway
(c) Rename “The Broadside” — SP3-126 owns The Long Fall for the Anvil reentry; keep the moon-bombardment core.

build.title: The Eunomia Buoy Chain
build.where: sector_eunomia_gulf, a line of six nav buoys none of which are charted as a group
build.trigger: scan all six in one session, in any order
build.sees: the sixth scan links them: each buoy holds one word, and the sentence reads "IF FOUND ALONE I AM NOT ALONE COUNT AGAIN." They are a sentence, a scale test, and a mini-constellation — someone's life work, maintained by someone who still buys the bulbs.
build.payoff: flag `buoy_sentence`; codex page "The Counting Buoys"; a small credits cache at the sentence's "period" buoy (the seventh, unlit, 100 WU past the last).
build.seam: scan-order counter + cache POI; codex overlay

build.title: The Half-Second Station
build.trigger: the player leaves an offering (any jettisoned cargo unit) on the rim and waits, scanner passive, for 20 s
build.sees: for exactly half a second — the same half-second as the Elroy third tag — the tithe's beacon transmits a full text page that cannot be re-read: a list of hull names and dates, one per line, ending with an empty line and the word "PENDING."
build.payoff: if the player's screenshot reflex fails them, a Data pad at station_triton's bar has the same list minus the last two lines; the empty line plus "PENDING" is only ever visible in the half-second version.
build.seam: timed one-shot text burst on the beacon (0.5 s TTL, comms:popup with ttl 1); bar pad is a barContacts read offer

build.title: The Prop Wreck
build.trigger: salvage_signal whose tell reads wrong (scan_tell_bait variant); cooldownS 2400
build.sees: A wreck that scans perfectly dead — except one heat bloom where no engine should be, and the "hull breach" that's welded from inside. It's a nest. The wreck is crewed, the distress is pre-recorded, and you are already inside their mine envelope.
build.payoff: Spot the tell before the spring: leave clean with proof (sellable intel). Spring it: a close-quarters fight where the wreck itself is cover for both sides.
build.seam: numbered file script 'distress' with custom scan_tell lines (ENCOUNTER_BARKS distress block precedent in src/data/encounters.js)

build.title: The Dust Script
build.trigger: within the calm dust sea; any deliberate wake pattern; persistence by sector day
build.sees: The dust sea holds wakes. In the calm patches, your wake lines persist for hours — and someone has been writing there: old routes, a name, an arrow pointing at nothing, all in wake-script, all fading at the same honest rate. You can write too. Yours will last as long as anyone's.
build.payoff: A canvas with rules: the day's surviving script is visible to every hull that passes (persisted per sector-day); the best-known entry, carved by wake every day for years, is from the pilot everyone thought died.
build.seam: wake-pattern persistence buffer per sector day + a fixed "daily writer" entry; reading via proximity reveal
hones: (a) one ephemeral capped wake polyline per visit + authored daily-writer props; no persistent wake store
(b) one ephemeral wake polyline per visit + authored daily writers (A H-14)
(c) Your wake persists as ONE ephemeral polyline per visit plus authored daily-writer props; no persistent player-authored wake store.

build.title: The Archive's Wrong Number
build.trigger: after the player has read 10+ codex pages (stat/persistence counter)
build.sees: a misrouted Archive internal: "REQUEST 44-C/SEALED — LOCATE ONE (1) COPY OF LEDGER, KURTZ, PERSONAL. STATUS: NOT MISSING. WITHHELD. WITHHELD BY: [FIELD LEFT BLANK]."
build.payoff: breadcrumb toward the Kurtz ledger thread at Ashfall; Archive rep -1 the moment the player reads it (they logged the leak; the Archive knows its own leaks).
build.seam: mail.js or comms row keyed to a codex-read counter; flag write

build.title: The Lightning Farmers
build.trigger: storm cell season (seeded schedule); proximity to the farm rocks
build.sees: The storm cells ground themselves on the farm rocks, and the farmers harvest: long collector lines between rocks, each strike running the line to a capacitor bank with a bang you feel in your teeth, and the farmers' commentary on the band has the rhythm of people who talk about weather because the weather is the whole conversation.
build.payoff: The farm sells charged cells (a real module charge) with a queue, a price, and a farmer who tells you, free, which rock to stand behind.
build.seam: seasonal storm vfx + a vendor encounter; charge as a module state; farmer barks

build.title: The Corner
build.trigger: posted when a seeded commodity price spike is scheduled; visible only 1 sector-day ahead
build.sees: Three independent traders are all quietly buying the same commodity for the same reason — a refinery order due tomorrow. The board doesn't say this. The queue at the commodity exchange does.
build.payoff: Buy first and the three pay YOU to step aside; escort all three instead (they split, you're owed by a syndicate); or beat them to the refinery and sell into the spike yourself.
build.seam: authored mission via economyContracts seams (src/systems/economyContracts.js) reading economyCycles schedule; DIRTY-adjacent, prefer numbered encounter with d.grant

build.title: The Brood Mare
build.trigger: proximity; gates minSectorTier 4; cooldownS 86400; uniqueOnce
build.sees: Acapital hull that isn't fighting — it's spawning: rack after rack of live wasps rolling off a carousel while the crew works the decks like a farm. Killing the hull is a massacre. Killing the RACKS is the fight: each one pops like a piñata and the swarm thins by arithmetic.
build.payoff: A boss whose defeat condition is subsystem destruction (racks), paying in a intact spawn-rack module nobody else has; the hull, racks gone, surrenders by simply powering down.
build.seam: capital-boss-adjacent numbered encounter using src/systems/capitalBossEncounters.js subsystem pattern with rack targets
hones: (a) rename off "Brood Mare" (register miss) to "The Broodyard"; the rack-destruction fight is right
(b) rename off "Brood Mare"; "The Broodyard"; the rack fight is right
(c) Rename off “Brood Mare” — “The Broodyard”; the rack-destruction fight is right, the register was not.

build.title: The Rope Cache Under The Approach
build.where: sector_helios_prime, under the Helios inbound leg's approach lane
build.trigger: massline-pull a specific "junk" rock that sits 40 WU off the lane's centerline (it reads 8% heavier than its size class)
build.sees: the rock's shell parts on a clean weld line: inside, a perfectly preserved pre-charter tow kit — hooks, line, and a laminated card: "IF YOU FOUND THIS, THE LANE WORKED. LEAVE THE HOOKS, TAKE THE CARD. — THE FIRST CREW." The card is the codex page.
build.payoff: codex page "The First Crew's Card" (+2% tow-assist speed permanently); the hooks stay, physical, for anyone who flies past.
build.seam: worldOneOffs rope-cache pattern (HELIOS_ROPE_CACHE in src/data/worldOneOffs.js) + codex overlay

build.title: The Scale Zero Rock
build.trigger: scan any asteroid whose mass reading returns exactly 0.0 (one seeded rock per save)
build.sees: the scanner insists the rock has no mass; the massline insists otherwise — it pulls heavy. The rock's interior is a void stasis crate: mass-canceled, older than the charter, stamped with a Verge-Layer interrogative glyph that translates (per the SP2-070 booth) to "WHAT WAS STORED HERE? (ANSWER WITHHELD)."
build.payoff: inside: one unit of a commodity that no longer exists on any market (codex-only commodity page, "Discontinued Cargo"). Selling it to an Archive berth rewrites its codex page with the sale date.
build.seam: seeded rock flag + massline mass-override + codex-only commodity row

build.title: The Echo Wreck
build.trigger: proximity — inside 100 WU, the echo loops on a 60 s cycle
build.sees: the wreck's window rows and lamp channels replay, in light only, its final minute — a scan sweep, a panic of strobes, a blackout walking bow to stern — then hold dark for forty seconds before repeating. Sensors insist the hull is cold.
build.payoff: plus codex entry (anomaly); the Archive pays for its recording.
build.seam: lamp-bus envelope sequence authored on one wreck package (data rows only); the loop is pure simTime modulo.

build.title: The Cascade
build.trigger: proximity during the seeded cascade window; uniqueOnce
build.sees: The Tethys debris cascade, twice a year: a derelict ring's slow decay reaches critical and for an hour the lane rains junk — hulls hitting hulls hitting hulls in slow, grinding, enormous silence, while traffic holds at the rim and the band counts collisions like a horse race. Nobody is hurt. Everything is memorial.
build.payoff: The aftermath is real loot physics (first-come salvage on the fresh field) and the ring's orbit is visibly, permanently cleaner — the same decay the game models, observed.
build.seam: scheduled debris event (aftermathWrecks seam, src/systems/aftermathWrecks.js) + loot physics; countdown via band commentary

build.title: The Overtime Locker
build.trigger: scan the derelict's locker twice, 24 in-game hours apart (the SP2-036 night clerk's locker)
build.sees: second scan opens it (first scan "locker jammed — shift ends soon"): inside, an unbroken set of night-shift logs and one personal item — a photo of the bay 7 grid, R3-CARRIER, taken on delivery day, captioned "SO THIS IS WHERE YOU ENDED UP." He knew. He always knew.
build.payoff: flag `overtime_knew`; the Bay 7 thread (SP2-011) closes with one extra line at Ashfall; codex page "The Night Clerk Knew."
build.seam: two-scan flag gate + codex overlay + mail.js Ashfall addendum

build.title: The Forty-First Hull
build.trigger: scan the field after the player has personally counted 41+ hull transits past their position in that sector (a tracked session counter)
build.sees: the field's board amends itself: "FORTY-ONE REGISTERED. FORTY-TWO OBSERVED. THE DIFFERENCE IS ALWAYS YOU." It has been counting the player the whole time.
build.payoff: codex page (Quiet count resolution); flag `counted_counted`; Quiet rep +1 (they respect a fellow bookkeeper).
build.seam: session transit counter + scan copy; codex overlay

build.title: The Counterfeit Beacon
build.trigger: any distress signal whose bearing drifts 1 WU per 10 seconds (deterministic drift, detectable by the scan-clue stale/contradicted system)
build.sees: the "distress" is a pirate lure — but a bad one: the recording's hull number belongs to a ship the player has personally docked beside, alive, at station_kepler_scar. The pirates copied the wrong hull. When the player springs the trap backward (arrives armed, scans first), the pirates' own beacon becomes their trial record.
build.payoff: turning the beacon evidence over to the hunters' exchange pays a writ premium; the real hull's owner mails one line of thanks and a standing 5% market discount.
build.seam: scanClues stale-fix pattern (src/data/scanClues.js) + bounty writ seam

build.title: The Graveyard Orbit
build.trigger: permanent fixture; reveals state on each visit
build.sees: A graveyard orbit where decommissioned hulls are parked in a slow ring, nose to tail, kilometer after kilometer — each one stripped of anything useful and left exactly as it was, with its name still on. The ring is maintained by nobody, and hulls are added to it by somebody, in order, always at the tail.
build.payoff: A place that remebers the sector's dead fleet; the newest hull in the ring is always someone you heard of; reading a full hull's plaque (scan, long-form) yields one codex page per hull, twenty in all.
build.seam: persistent ring of wrecks (wreckClasses) with an append-on-event rule keyed to major NPC deaths; codex pages per plaque

build.title: The Stowaway Cache
build.where: any sector, aboard the player's own hull
build.trigger: after 5+ undocked days, a quiet rattle event fires once (deterministic day window)
build.sees: a stowaway — a feral salvage automaton, Latch-Child's make — has been living in the hold, tidying. It leaves one item as rent: something the player lost early in the game and never recovered (the game's own loss ledger, physicalized). Its tag: "ORIGIN LAPSED. RENT PAID. GOOD HOLD."
build.payoff: the lost item returns (from the real loss record); flag `latchchild_rent`; Latch-Child's wreck-tidying in the player's sectors improves one grade.
build.seam: loss-ledger read (contactDeedMemory/impound records) + one-shot hold event; Latch-Child line variant

build.title: The Read Fee
build.trigger: posted whenever the player scans any wreck (seeded interest roll); repeatable per wreck
build.sees: The Archive offers the strangest service in the belt: pay a fee and their readers will reconstruct the last sixty seconds of any wreck's existence from hull stress, log fragments and powder burns. The report arrives as a single paragraph. It is always about something you didn't ask.
build.payoff: Paid lore that is honest about method ("the galley's coffee pot was still warm; impact came from above"): a codex fragment per wreck read, and the Archive's debt of gratitude after ten reads.
build.seam: per-wreck read service (numbered encounter keyed to scan events); fragments via codexPages.js; fee via d.charge

build.title: The Wreck Deed
build.trigger: posted when a famous wreck's legal owner finally defaults (seeded schedule); uniqueOnce
build.sees: The auction of a legendary wreck is posted, and the fine print is the event: delivery within the week, current possession "contested by all previous bidders, who were notified." You are not buying a ship. You are buying an argument.
build.payoff: Win the auction, then defend/settle the claim physically; deliver the deed intact and the wreck (a genuine capital-adjacent hull) is yours to strip or register.
build.seam: authored chain (auction leg + claim-defense leg reusing claim_threat script); hull reward via a disabled entity grant (1210 pattern)

build.title: The Efficiency Audit
build.trigger: proximity to a Fulfillment surveyor; fires on any dock-approach with fitted modules; cooldownS 86400
build.sees: A Fulfillment auditor hails with genuine warmth and a spreadsheet: your hull's fit is audited on the spot — "two modules overlap functionally, one is six percent under-rated, and you carry cargo capacity you have never once used." Everything it says is true. It wants, with visible joy, to fix you.
build.payoff: Accept the audit (a real refit recommendation that is actually good) or decline politely (it marks you "awaiting optimization" and checks back, forever, kindly).
build.seam: numbered ambient encounter reading fitted modules (src/core/fittedModules.js) vs usage stats; recommendation as a real refit offer

build.title: The Understudy Letter
build.trigger: after the player's third successful bar-contact mission
build.sees: "TO: THE PILOT / FROM: A REGULAR WHO KNOWS A REGULAR / The bar has started a pool on you. Not against you. On you. Current line: you make it to a capital hull. Payout is drinks for everyone, which is why everyone is being so nice to you. Do not break character."
build.payoff: pure bar-culture flavor; bar tabs at the player's home station run one drink cheaper for the rest of the game (a real, small economy tick).
build.seam: mail.js row + a one-way price nudge in the bar economy seam (stationLife barPressureAt consumer)

build.title: The Gravity Well Garden
build.where: sector_eunomia_gulf, a stable Lagrange-style drift point
build.trigger: jettison any organic matter (food cargo) at the drift point and return 7+ in-game days later
build.sees: the matter has been collected and planted: a fist-sized Understory cutting grows in a tethered planter at the exact jettison point, labeled with the player's callsign and the date. A spore-tender passes weekly to water it. "You threw away a garden," the tender says. "The garden disagreed."
build.payoff: the player's named garden persists (a personal micro-garden, stage 1); visiting it weekly grows it; Understory standing +3; flag `garden_disagreed`.
build.seam: jettison event + drift-point POI + garden runtime reuse (faction_understory stages)

build.title: The Merger Convoy
build.trigger: two scheduled convoys converging at a seeded junction; once per seeded week
build.sees: Two convoys meet at a lane junction, run lights-to-lights for a moment, merge into one column with the old leads falling in side by side, and the band plays a brief, formal exchange of freight manifests like a marriage register.
build.payoff: Pure spectacle with one honest mechanic: the merged convoy is 2x the loot for raiders and 2x the escort work — everyone on the band knows it, including them.
build.seam: two 'convoy' script instances with a shared junction anchor; barks table in src/data/encounters.js

build.title: The Zodiacal Shelf
build.trigger: sim-time window — visible only during the season's calm phase, drifting one sky-quadrant per season (pure `weatherSeasonAt` read)
build.sees: a faint tilted wedge of dust-light leans over the belt's deep field, brightest where the key light rakes it, fading to nothing at the sector edge. It moves at background parallax only — untouchable, and obviously enormous.
build.payoff: plus codex entry after three seasons of observation (the player can confirm its drift is lawful).
build.seam: `src/data/sectorVisualProfiles.js` background structure row (structureKind/regionLo/regionHi vocabulary exists) + one authored accent plate via the paintedSky/sky plate path.

build.title: The Anvil Lighthouse
build.trigger: always present; flashes on a 13 s lamp period
build.sees: an old automated beacon rides the influence edge on a slow orbit, its lamp sweeping the dark side of the disc once every 13 seconds — the only structure for a thousand WU, reading as one lonely light in the black. Its flash is visible from the sling band; pilots time approaches by it.
build.payoff: plus codex entry; a registered charted place (map-visible).
build.seam: `src/data/authoredPlaces.js` zone record + beacon lamp with the `beacon` channel from `src/data/lampChannels.js`; atlas gates per `src/data/PLACE_REGISTRATION.md`.

build.title: The Overtime Log
build.trigger: scan during any station's night shift window (stationShiftAt night phase)
build.sees: the derelict's work log glows one extra line at night only: "SHIFT ENDED. I STAYED. THE LANE DOES NOT SUPERVISE ITSELF." By day, the line is absent and the log ends two entries earlier.
build.payoff: codex page (Helios overlay: the overtime line is quoted); one mail letter from Kessler references "the night clerk at the overtime pin. Good man. Never billed us."
build.seam: scan copy keyed to shift phase (worldCalendar seam); codex + mail rows

build.title: The Smuggler's Confession Booth
build.trigger: first dock after the player has sold 3+ lots of stolen goods
build.sees: the Den's back room hosts an anonymous "weight off" service: dictaphone, one minute, no name, no recording kept — the room's joke is that everyone knows the recording is kept. The player's minute, if taken, comes back to them weeks later as a single line of anonymous band chatter that only they will recognize.
build.payoff: pure loop-closure theater; flag `weight_off`; one-time heat -3 ("the room heard it; the room settled it").
build.seam: barContacts room offer + heat seam + one delayed band line keyed to day window

build.title: The Helix Barge
build.trigger: permanent neutral fixture at a fixed drift; state persists
build.sees: The Helix clinic barge hangs in the deep with its lights on and its doors open to anyone — pirates, patrols, you — and its one rule is painted twice: "No weapons inside the ring.
