No exceptions except yours." The ring is honest: fire inside it and every faction's ledger hears about it within the day.
build.payoff: Free repairs with a waiting queue and real triage (worse hulls first, including your enemies, which you watch); the ring's sanctity is a mechanic the whole sector respects, and testing it once is permanent.
build.seam: persistent vendor fixture with a queue system; ring-violation broadcast via news:publish; faction-wide rep penalty
hones: (a) free repairs cost visible queue TIME with triage order displayed; verify Helix's remit before the clinic ring (B + C)
(b) free repairs cost visible queue time with triage on display; verify Helix's remit (C)
(c) Verify Helix’s clinic remit before the ring; free repairs cost visible queue TIME with triage order on display — the ring-violation flag stays the one permanent consequence.

build.title: The Sedna Marker Cache
build.where: sector_sedna_dark, the lane pin that points at nothing
build.trigger: follow the pin's bearing for 4,000+ WU in a straight line (its "unfinished route")
build.sees: the route's end: a survey stake, driven into a rock, with a flag made of tarp and a tin cup. Beside it, sealed: the original survey crew's route log, ending mid-entry: "DAY 214. THE DARK DID NOT WIN. WE STOPPED FOR LUNCH. RE—". The entry is the cache.
build.payoff: codex page "Day 214"; Sedna standing +2; the stake becomes a real charted beacon ("Route 214, Terminus").
build.seam: bearing-follow check + POI reveal + codex overlay

build.title: The Sun Dogs
build.trigger: sim-time window — days 20–22 of every year, first watch
build.sees: two bright mock suns flank the key at exactly 22 degrees, each with a short tail of colored fire, for about a minute. They hold formation while everything moves — haulers fly "through" them. The bar keeps a bet running on which one goes out first.
build.payoff: plus codex entry; a barContacts line on day 20.
build.seam: sky-plate accent pair (paintedSky strength pulse) in `src/data/sectorVisualProfiles.js` — no new renderer work.

build.title: Postcard From a Dead Sector
build.trigger: first mail delivery 2+ in-game days after leaving Ashfall
build.sees: a postcard photograph of the debris floor — the dead liner, the eleven-year count. On the back, in pencil: "Still here. Still counting. The count is now [N]." The number is genuinely current, pulled from the live ledger value.
build.payoff: pure warmth-horror; the postcard's N advances with each later reading of the same mail item.
build.seam: mail.js body is a template; the mail system already interpolates tokens (marketNews token pattern) — glue is a live-value token in the mail body path

build.title: The Proteus Double Take Double
build.where: sector_proteus_well, the Double Take stash rack
build.trigger: after SP2-034 (admission note read), return and re-scan the rack's shadow
build.sees: under the rack, a second, smaller rack. First crew named the big one. Second crew agreed and left it. The small rack is third crew's: "FIRST CREW NAMED. SECOND CREW LEFT. THIRD CREW DOUBLED. FOURTH CREW: YOUR TURN." The small rack holds a starter kit of one decent module and a note of honest advice.
build.payoff: one free module (real inventory); flag `third_crew_doubled`; the rack grows one shelf per century of lore the player uncovers (cosmetic, capped).
build.seam: scan-shadow interaction + module grant; codex overlay

build.title: The Hours
build.trigger: first dock at Ceres after the player has 20+ hours of logged labor (persistent counter)
build.sees: The Collective's tally office converts your logged work hours into their internal currency — "credit hours," one per hour worked, never spendable, always counted — and stamps your ledger with your number. The number is lower than you'd guess. Everyone's is. That's the point, says the clerk, and the clerk has done this ten thousand times and believes it every time.
build.payoff: A permanent, useless, perfectly meaningful number that other Collective NPCs reference with respect proportional to its size.
build.seam: labor counter in story.flags; stamp via dock comms; referenced in Collective NPC barks

build.title: The Ore Hound
build.trigger: proximity to a derelict mining rig; uniqueOnce
build.sees: A quadruped assay drone, twenty years past its warranty, still "hunting" — pointing rigidly at the nearest ore body every few minutes like a bird dog, waiting for a handler who retired. It follows anyone who scans it.
build.payoff: Adopt it: it parks on your hull and points at one hidden ore body per sector day (a real, bounded, deterministic hint). It cannot be repaired, only kept.
build.seam: numbered ambient encounter + a persistent companion prop with a daily seeded pick from actual ore positions; codex entry

build.title: The Haumea Tool Ledger
build.trigger: massline-recover the extraction mast's loose tool (ropeable item beside the seated mast)
build.sees: returning the tool to any mining-station claim office files it in a physical ledger: "1 TOOL RETURNED BY [CALLSIGN]. 1 TOOL STILL OUT. THE RIFT KEEPS SCORE." The ledger has run for years. The player is the first return in eleven entries.
build.payoff: Haumea standing +3; flag `tool_returned`; the claim office's future claim approvals for the player skip one procedural step ("they return tools").
build.seam: ropeable item + claim-office return interaction + flag

build.title: The One Favor
build.trigger: posted when the player's Frontier rep crosses zero (from either side); uniqueOnce
build.sees: The Frontier doesn't recruit. A recruiter buys you one drink and explains the actual arrangement: "One job. You can say no. If you say no, we'll like you anyway, and this conversation never happened. If you say yes, you're one of ours until the job's done, and the job is real."
build.payoff: A genuinely hard job with Frontier-standard honesty (the briefing names every risk, correctly); refusing is honored forever; accepting makes the Frontier yours and you theirs.
build.seam: authored mission via missions.js authored pattern (DIRTY — fallback numbered selfRegistered job chain); rep gate on faction_free

build.title: Letters For The Dead Crew
build.trigger: day >= 6; fires once; requires no other flag (baseline thread)
build.sees: a letter addressed to the player's hull's DEAD CREW, not the player: "TO: CREW, TESSERA / RE: THE SEVENTH RUN / We are still holding your deposits. They have matured. Come collect. Bring registration." The sender is a Concord benefits desk.
build.payoff: replying with the player's own registration instead of the crew's is the only correct move: the desk closes the account — "ACCOUNT CLOSED BY SUCCESSOR. DEPOSITS FORFEITED TO THE COUNT. FLY HER WELL." Small credits payout; big lore payoff.
build.seam: mail.js cast row with a reply-option glue; ties into the SP2-007/SP2-001 Tessera thread

build.title: The Null Auction
build.trigger: proximity at a seeded auction time; uniqueOnce
build.sees: A ring of hulls bidding on nothing. There is no lot, no seller, no cargo — only a price climbing on a public board, paid in jettisoned credits, with total solemnity. When you hail, the answer is serene: "The lot is the auction. Everything is the lot. You are early; the lot has not been chosen."
build.payoff: A memory-market: the winning bidder chooses one event from the sector's history and buys the right to have it remembered differently (one news-wire line, rewritten, permanently).
build.seam: numbered selfRegistered encounter with credit-jettison bids; news rewrite via news:publish with sourceRef override; history pool from deedRecord
hones: (a) auction sells the framing of the event's next wire mention, bids capped at pocket change; the new memory is a retraction-with-footnote because this world keeps receipts (mine + C)
(b) tiny bids; the prize is a retraction-with-footnote of one seeded event's next mention
(c) Bids capped at jettison pocket change; the prize is one news line’s reframing as a retraction-with-footnote — the original line stays legible somewhere, because this world keeps receipts.

build.title: The Triton Tithe Audit
build.trigger: the player has left offerings on the rim 3+ separate visits (jettison counter at the rim)
build.sees: on the fourth visit, the tithe has been curated: the player's three offerings are arranged in a neat row with a tally plate reading "3 FOR 3. NOBODY EVER TAKES. YOU KEPT GIVING ANYWAY. THE RIM NOTICES." The tally plate is signed with a single glyph: the anomaly's own.
build.payoff: flag `tithe_notices`; one guaranteed rare commodity find at the rim thereafter; codex page "The Rim Notices."
build.seam: rim jettison counter + arrangement dressing + codex overlay

build.title: The Belt Strike
build.trigger: fires when a seeded toll increase lands; uniqueOnce per toll change
build.sees: Belt miners have downed tools over a new toll and are holding a physical picket line across the lane — beacons, banners, and a pot of the worst coffee in the belt. The company is hiring non-union haulers. Both sides post. The band is a mess.
build.payoff: Haul for the company (pay, miner resentment flags) or run supply through the picket for the union (rep, company resentment flags); either way prices and patrols visibly shift for days.
build.seam: numbered encounter pair reading a shared story flag; consequences via faction rep intents (d.rep) and economy notes

build.title: The Busker
build.trigger: dock proximity; one per station; seeded rotation of three drones
build.sees: A refit drone with a speaker bolted on plays at the dock mouth — old station songs, two of them good — with a cargo-net for tips. Dockhands toss rivets. A pilot once tossed a full canister and the drone still has the canister, displayed, thirty years later, with a small sign: "SOMETIMES."
build.payoff: Tip it (jettison credits in the net — physical, honest); at the third tip the drone learns your hull's name and plays it, forever, whenever you dock.
build.seam: dock vignette with a jettison-tip interaction; persistent name flag; song via audioRecipes (src/data/audioRecipes.js)

build.title: The Phoebe Encore
build.trigger: after SP2-029 (buoy keeping), the player transmits any audio on the dead channel
build.sees: the array rebroadcasts the player's transmission — once — then appends a two-note tone that the whole sector's old-timers will later identify in bars as the array operator's signature. She is still signing work. The channel is "retired" because she is; the array disagrees.
build.payoff: flag `phoebe_encore`; codex page "The Signature"; one mail letter from the array's maintenance estate: "If the array signs for her, the array stays on. You heard it. It stays on."
build.seam: transmission replay event + codex overlay + mail row
hones: (a) keyed to hailing the channel (hail-count); there is no free-form transmit
(b) keyed to hailing the channel; there is no free-form transmit (A H-27)

build.title: The Regular's Empty Stool
build.trigger: dock during night shift (worldCalendar shiftAt); once per game
build.sees: one stool has a drink on it and nobody near it. The barkeep explains, unprompted: "Shift 7's floor lead. Nine of eleven came back from Shaft 7. The drink is for the arithmetic." The drink is refreshed every night by the same crew. Nobody drinks it.
build.payoff: codex page (Shaft 7 memorial); DMC rep +1 for buying the next round for the floor crew (a bar purchase option).
build.seam: bar set-dressing row + purchase option in src/ui/station/screens/bar.js data; codex overlay in src/data/codexPages.js

build.title: The Orcus Tide Ledger
build.where: sector_orcus_shadow, the debris tide's transponder gate
build.trigger: observe a full tide cycle at the gate (proximity hold, one cycle period)
build.sees: the gate has been counting tides: a mechanical odometer, sun-bleached, reading "CYCLE 4,110. COUNT CORRECT AS OF CYCLE 4,110." Someone has to be winding it. Nobody has ever been seen winding it. The windmill-shaped component is the sector's best-kept secret and its least-kept secret simultaneously.
build.payoff: flag `tide_wound`; codex page "Cycle 4,110"; the odometer's next reading, seen later, always ends in the player's hull-number's last digit (deterministic whimsy).
build.seam: hold-timer + dressing state + codex overlay

build.title: Ocean Glint Walk
build.trigger: sim-time — the specular walk crosses the ocean band once per 600 s day, ~40 s duration (pure sun-angle geometry)
build.sees: a single burning point of reflected sun slides across the Anvil's ocean band like a bead of fire, widening into a golden road of specular glint as the angle shallows, then pinching out. For forty seconds the planet reads as water.
build.payoff: visual wonder only; pairs with SP3-001 as the planetary sibling of the Glint Hour.
build.seam: planet-factory specular parametric moment — one authored material band in the `planet_tethys_anvil` constants (`src/data/planets.js` names the palette path via `planetFactory.js`); data-driven, no new shader.

build.title: The Naming
build.trigger: fires on the first dock after the player's first major rescue (priorOutcome rescue)
build.sees: The yard has named a tug. Your hull's name, on a brand-new tug, at the naming ceremony you weren't told about, with a speech that mispronounces it. The yardmaster's explanation is a masterpiece of understatement: "Small yard. We name what we're grateful for. She's yours to borrow, any time she's not working."
build.payoff: A permanent borrowable tug (a real assist verb at that station, capped fairly) and the mispronunciation, which the yardmaster refuses to correct and the tug answers to.
build.seam: rescue flag + a dock ceremony vignette; assist as a docking speed-up; name persisted

build.title: The Pilgrim's Meal Ticket
build.trigger: the player has ferried a pilgrim transport at least once (escort/convoy deed)
build.sees: one pilgrim, mid-meal, quietly orders a second meal and has it sealed to go. Asked why: "For the road. Not mine — yours. Everyone's road is the road." The sealed meal appears in the player's hold as one unit of provisions with a handwritten seal.
build.payoff: eating it (consuming the unit) heals the player's crew morale tick and grants a one-time 5% repair discount at the next Choir berth; flag `pilgrim_meal`.
build.seam: cargo unit with custom provenance + flag; discount consumed by the service pricing seam

build.title: Moonrise Over the Anvil
build.trigger: sim-time — day 30 of every year, the moonlet crosses the disc face over ~4 minutes
build.sees: a small cratered moonlet the background never quite showed before crosses the Anvil's face as a hard black coin with a lit rim, and for four minutes every eclipse-shadow behavior (SP3-002/015 family) reads against the planet instead of the belt.
build.payoff: visual wonder only; pairs into the eclipse chain.
build.seam: background composition `signatureHero` addition in `src/data/sectorVisualProfiles.js` (the resolver already supports hero rows) keyed by calendar day.
hones: (b) keep ONLY fully decoupled from the eclipse: a daily moonrise signature, not a fourth transit

build.title: The Bell Tolls for You
build.trigger: after event — `player:death`
build.sees: as your own hull breaks (the existing death explosion), the audio duck drops everything except a single distant bell tolling once — spatialized to the nearest station, not to you — and the last frame holds half a beat longer than the current cut. Your death gets the same grammar as the wrecks you've watched.
build.payoff: visual wonder only; closure, not punishment.
build.seam: `player:death` subscription in `src/render/vfx.js` already fires the explosion; add the audio duck + toll cue on the same event.

build.title: The Tally Board
build.trigger: permanent fixture rock at a fixed sector-local coordinate; updates on visit
build.sees: A hull plate bolted to the biggest rock in the field, chalked with the field's working scores: who stripped what, who caught the keel, who owes the yard. Your hull gets chalked on it the first time you do anything here — and it never washes off.
build.payoff: Persistent, visible, world memory in physical form; NPC scavengers reference the board's current standings in barks.
build.seam: persistent prop registered like src/data/authoredPlaces.js zones; chalk state in state.story.flags; barks via encounterScripts ambient pool

build.title: The Vael Clause Reader
build.trigger: first dock with any Vael-origin cargo in hold
build.sees: a contract-language reader works the rail: for a flat fee, she reads any Vael-billied cargo's clauses aloud and translates. Most clauses are freight terms. One clause, in every Vael bill — numbered 44-C-coincident by pure coincidence, she insists — reads: "The bearer is a clause. All clauses survive their bearers."
build.payoff: codex page (Vael contract-language primer); flag `vael_clause_heard`; Vael standing +1 (correct recitation is courtesy).
build.seam: barContacts service contact + codex overlay

build.title: The Eris Last Pod
build.where: sector_eris_margin, the Drift Choir's last pod
build.trigger: the player has heard the bell-word roll call (SP2-016) three times
build.sees: the last pod's tether is finally, visibly fraying. The bar knows. The barkeep: "The line has held longer than the writs that ignore it. When it goes, it goes quiet. You want the chair? Cut it clean. Cut it slow."
build.payoff: the SP2-079 payoff made real: a clean cut (massline, low impulse) claims the chair; a messy cut (hard yank) wakes the line — every pod swings once, the whole choir, and the bar does not speak to the player for a week.
build.seam: ropeable pod + impulse-sensitive outcome (masslineImpactDamage read) + bar standing flag
hones: (a) drop the "Drift Choir" name - one Choir; "the line's last pod" needs no second one (adopted from C)
(b) drop the Drift Choir name; "the line's last pod" needs no second choir (C)
(c) Drop the “Drift Choir” name per SP2-016 — the line’s last pod at Eris needs no second choir.

build.title: The Squatter
build.trigger: fires when the player's habitual berth (most-docked berth) is taken by a seeded visitor; once
build.sees: Your berth — your berth — has a stranger in it. They are apologetic to the point of ceremony: your berth fee for the night is paid, there's a note ("they said someone loves this berth; it looked like just a berth; I'm sorry"), and a small gift, chosen with alarming precision from your known tastes.
build.payoff: A stranger who becomes a named contact (the gift's precision makes that inevitable); the berth war recurs once a season, and the third time, they leave the berth to you, permanently, with a formal note.
build.seam: berth-visit counter + visitor vignette; contact flag; seasonal recurrence via seeded schedule
hones: (a) keyed to most-docked station; no berth-number identity exists to squat
(b) key to most-docked station (A H-16)
(c) Key to most-docked station — no persistent berth-number identity exists; the alarming precision about your habits survives the re-key.

build.title: The Hyperion Cell Debt
build.trigger: the player buys fuel cells at the claim station three visits in a row (the ration-run regulars)
build.sees: the claim crews take up a collection — for the player: "You keep buying dear because you buy late. Here is the roster. First cell run each shift is crew-priced. Bring the rack, we fill it first. You are crew-priced now. Do not tell the desk."
build.payoff: permanent crew pricing on fuel cells at that station (-15%); flag `crew_priced`; the roster is a physical inventory item with every regular's name.
build.seam: purchase counter + pricing flag + inventory item

build.title: The Genuine Article
build.trigger: distress in a sector where the player has already escaped ≥2 bait distresses (persistent counter)
build.sees: Another distress ping in the same belt that has burned you twice as bait. Everything about it scans wrong the same way. You'd be right to ignore it — and this once, buried under the same fake signature, there's a real crew that found an old decoy transmitter and is praying you're not as burned as you should be.
build.payoff: Scan past the tell (a second scan pulse, deliberately) to find the real heartbeat; rescue pays double in reputation because you risked it on a read.
build.seam: numbered file script 'distress' with counter-gated tell lines; counter in story.flags

build.title: The Jukebox Ghost
build.trigger: sim-time — The Pale Holiday (dayOfYear 33), one play per sitting, hash-picked minute
build.sees: the bar's ambient mix cuts and something plays — a slow, wrong-temperature melody that no recipe in the catalog matches, ending with the jukebox's mechanical reset clunk. The barkeep's line: "Nobody loaded that."
build.payoff: plus codex entry; the one unexplained audio artifact in the game.
build.seam: one authored "wrong" recipe (detuned, off-scale) gated by the festival row + the barContact system for the line.

build.title: The Bloom Tide
build.trigger: bloom tide wavefront on its seeded schedule (announced on the band); sector-wide
build.sees: The nebula blooms on schedule: a light-front rolls across the whole sector, and every hull, rock and wreck it passes flares briefly in sequence — traffic light up like a coastline at night. Everyone stops what they're doing to watch. It happens exactly as often as it should.
build.payoff: A scheduled spectacle the world treats as weather (jobs pause, tolls pause); one unique cache is visible ONLY during the bloom (its surface phosphors), same window every time.
build.seam: scheduled sector-wide vfx wavefront (bloom ladder/lookMoods adjacent — DIRTY files; prefer encounter-driven story prop) + numbered ambient encounter for the cache
hones: (a) bloom wavefront as a scheduled story-prop light curtain + cache window; no edits to dirty lookMoods/vfx
(b) scheduled story-prop light curtain + cache window; no dirty lookMoods/vfx edits (A H-13)

build.title: The Split Station's Third Half
build.trigger: scan both known halves of the split station, then scan the gap between them
build.sees: the gap scans as occupied: a third station section, mass-verified but invisible, holding the two halves together by mass alone. Its transponder reads the station's own name with one letter changed. It has been the load-bearing piece since the split. Nobody charts it because charts do not record what holds things together.
build.payoff: codex page "The Third Half"; Tethys standing +2; the Split Station's market gains one unlisted commodity slot (stock: mystery, rotates).
build.seam: three-scan sequence + hidden POI + codex overlay

build.title: The View
build.trigger: dock offer after the player has docked 30+ times; purchase persists
build.sees: The station auctions "view berths" — the six docks facing open star — with a price and a waiting list, and the fine print is honest: "The view is the same star. The star does not care. This berth is about what you look at while you drink." The current holders include a legend who bought theirs fifty years ago and has never once docked elsewhere.
build.payoff: A purchasable permanent berth with a real (modest, dignified) visual change at dock and a spot on the view-berth plaque, which is read aloud once a year.
build.seam: dock purchase + a persistent berth flag consumed by dock layout; plaque as a dock fixture
hones: (a) purchasable plaque + greeting + fee; drop the dock-layout claim - dock layout is static UI
(b) plaque + greeting + fee; drop the dock-layout claim (A H-17)
(c) Purchasable plaque + one dock greeting + fee; drop the dock-layout-change claim (dock layout is static UI).

build.title: Shift Change Cascade
build.trigger: sim-time — each station's three shift turns per 600 s day (per-berth offsets already hashed)
build.sees: the station's window rows extinguish in a floor-by-floor wave and relight at the new watch's warmer gain — the building visibly changing hands. Docked, you hear the PA; outside, you watch the lights do the talking.
build.payoff: visual wonder only; makes every station a clock.
build.seam: lamp-bus gain wave keyed by `stationShiftAt` in `src/data/worldCalendar.js`; zero new systems.

build.title: The Statistician
build.trigger: first bar visit after 50 recorded deeds (persistent counter); uniqueOnce
build.sees: A professional rememberer — that's the job title — performs "your legend" to the bar: your career stats as folk numbers ("forty-one rescues! give or take; who counts?"), slightly wrong in the direction of a better story, and corrected live by hecklers who were THERE for three of them.
build.payoff: Your actual statistics, roasted; after the show the rememberer buys you a drink and asks for the corrections, which improve the next performance for every player.
build.seam: deedRecord stats rendered as a bar scene (barContacts adjacent — DIRTY; prefer comms popup); corrections feed the pool

build.title: The Listening Field's Reply
build.trigger: transmit any hail from within the field's radius after SP2-004 (sealed shelf seen)
build.sees: the field replies — to the player, directly, the only unsealed thing it does: "RECEIVED. YOUR TRANSMISSION HAS BEEN FILED UNDER [TODAY'S DATE], CROSS-REFERENCED TO NOTHING. IN ELEVEN YEARS NO ONE HAS FILED FROM HERE. THE SHELF IS PLEASED. CONTINUE."
build.payoff: flag `field_filed_you`; codex page "Filed, Cross-Referenced To Nothing."
build.seam: hail-response branch keyed to flag; codex overlay

build.title: The Ghost Limb
build.where: sector_veil_nebula (outer rim, away from all volumes)
build.trigger: proximity — 240 WU of a fixed-seed point on the rim
build.sees: a rim-light arc draws itself around empty space — the violet-on-black rim exactly as a hull would catch it, describing a ship-shaped absence roughly corvette-sized, holding for three seconds, then gone. It never repeats from the same angle.
build.payoff: plus codex entry (the Archive pays a small bonus for a scan of it).
build.seam: one pooled rim-colored sprite/light from the event pool (`cue` row in `src/render/vfxColorLightDirector.js`) + seeded position data row.

build.title: The Reactor Ferry
build.trigger: posted when a seeded reactor-casualty event fires near a colony
build.sees: A freighter's reactor is in cascade and the ship cannot dock — docking means the station eats the blast. The job: tow the whole dying ship to a disposal trajectory while her crew shuttles off. Every second of the tow, the reactor's countdown is visible and audible.
build.payoff: A pure-tension tow with a real explosion if failed (visible from the colony, remembered by it); success pays from three directions (crew, company, colony).
build.seam: authored tow mission with a sim-time fuse (deadlineS + visible countdown UI via ui:setCourse/deadline); explosion via lootShards

build.title: Lightning Web
build.trigger: sim-time — surge phase only, strike every 8–20 s at hash-picked points inside the band
build.sees: discharge forks walk the storm band's cloud deck — each strike is a white flash that throws real light onto every hull skimming nearby, leaving a fading afterglow patch on the clouds. Count the rhythm: the third strike of a triplet always lands on the richest cloud row.
build.payoff: visual wonder only; the rhythm is learnable and rewards positioning.
build.seam: `explosionIgnition`-family event lights + gas-volume flash; both vocabularies exist in `src/render/vfxColorLightDirector.js` and `vfx._gas`.

build.title: The Broken Shepherd's Flock
build.trigger: destroy or witness the destruction of any hostile hull within 600 WU of the broken shepherd
build.sees: the shepherd's wreck-herding rigs detach, piece by piece, and gather the fresh wreckage into a quiet orbit around it — the flock, re-flocked. Its one working PA loops, softer each cycle: "COUNTED. COUNTED. COUNTED." The count is correct.
build.payoff: flag `flock_reflocked`; the wreckage remains collectible salvage for anyone (Understory gets first claim); codex page "Re-Flocked."
build.seam: kill-event proximity check + wreck-herding presentation (uniqueWrecks) + codex overlay

build.title: The Counter-Contract
build.trigger: while a bounty hunter pursuit is live (bountyHunt.js active), a seeded rival hunter rolls; cooldownS 86400
build.sees: Your hunter's approach is interrupted — professionally — by a second hunter who hails YOU, not them: "Ignore the writ. I pay better for the writ-holder's hull. Or just stay out of my firing line, either way." The contract has a contract on it now.
build.payoff: A three-way fight where any pair can ally for the moment; deliver the writ-holder's wreck to the rival for double; or watch two professionals duel and sell the story later.
build.seam: numbered file script 'bountyHunter' with a second hunter squad keyed to active bounty state (src/systems/bountyHunt.js)

build.title: The Lung's Breath
build.trigger: hold position near the Lung through one full pressure cycle (period known from the hunters' writ wall)
build.sees: the Lung inhales — dust, debris, one careless cargo lid — and exhales a slow, resonant tone across the lane. Everyone on the band pauses. One hunter transmits the traditional response, mandatory, tonal: "BREATHE EASY." The Lung breathes again. The tradition is older than the writ that ignores it.
build.payoff: codex page "Breathe Easy"; flag `lung_exhale_heard`; the tone's pitch is a real instrument: it shifts with sector air-commodity prices (economy-linked, deterministic).
build.seam: cycle-timer + audio event + economy-linked pitch + codex overlay

build.title: The Still Eye
build.trigger: proximity — a fixed-seed 80 WU circle inside the danger band
build.sees: inside the circle the lightning stops, the drag vanishes and loose debris hangs motionless, glittering — a calm pocket the storm flows around. Heat cools at the out-of-band rate inside. It drifts one band-width per season.
build.payoff: plus codex entry; a known fast-repair hole for pilots who track it.
build.seam: zone record in `src/data/sectorZones.js` (anomaly_deep type, no presence) + drag/heat exemption keyed by the same predicate as the bands in `src/data/planets.js`.

build.title: Plunge Runners
build.trigger: sim-time — second watch of market days (heat-treat demand), proximity 400 WU
build.sees: three lightly-built hulls dive the reentry band in a chain, plasma sheaths lighting their bellies white-orange, then pull out trailing ember smoke and sell to a waiting hauler. If you follow and survive, the vendor sells to you at the band's edge.
build.payoff: plus small bonus (discounted heat-treated commodity) and a codex entry.
build.seam: zone presence template (`P.raiders`-style row in `src/data/sectorZones.js`) with a custom route + the existing reentry heat model from `src/data/planets.js` — the NPCs use the player's own physics.

build.title: The Wrong Weather Patch
build.where: sector_helios_prime (one 40 WU patch off the tutorial lane)
build.trigger: proximity — permanent
build.sees: one small patch of Helios behaves like an ion-storm cell every day regardless of the season — crawling static, curtain flickers, a forecast that insists it is clear. The patch is exactly the footprint of a station that isn't there anymore.
build.payoff: plus codex entry; weather as archaeology.
build.seam: a weather-volume footprint with no volume registered (data row + the field-kernel boundary presentation only).
hones: (a) register the patch as its own tiny weather volume plus a forecast line that reads clear
(b) weather as archaeology; registered as its own tiny volume + a clear-reading forecast (A H-45)
(c) Register the patch as its own tiny weather volume plus a forecast line that reads clear; “a footprint with no volume” is not a supported shape.

build.title: The Deadweight Derby
build.trigger: posted at the yard on off-shifts; repeatable
build.sees: The derby is simple: everyone races towing a yard-supplied dead hulk, and the hulks are all worse than yours. Winning is less about thrust than about line discipline — every towed swing through the refinery shallows is a chance to lose the whole thing.
build.payoff: A race where the physics is the opponent; prizes scale with hulk intactness at the line, and the yard re-sells your "raced" hulk with a plaque.
build.seam: race mission with a mandatory latched prop (tow constraint on courseSector); hulk props from wreckClasses

build.title: Hate Mail, Specific
build.trigger: player disables a bounty hunter for the first time (warrant:hunterDisabled)
build.sees: "TO: WHOMEVER / MY COUSIN HUNTS. YOUR WAKE UNHUNTED HIM. HE IS FINE. HE IS FURIOUS. HE HAS YOUR REGISTRATION NUMBER MEMORIZED AS A PRAYER. GOOD LUCK WITH THE PRAYER."
build.payoff: pure flavor; a persistent one-time -2 with faction_free unless the player mails back an apology (a mail reply option — glue), which converts it to +1.
build.seam: mail.js 'hate' row + reply-flag glue in the mail evaluator

build.title: The Reef Light
build.trigger: proximity at night-cycle equivalent (sector shadow window); permanent
build.sees: A dead survey ship's beacon still rotates on the exact period it held in life — and traffic still obeys it. Locals won't say what it warns off, but every hull that cuts the corner here goes wide, silently, first. There is no reef. There is something.
build.payoff: Pure dread as world texture; cutting the corner is survivable N-1 times out of N (seeded), and the one exception has never been explained on any band.
build.seam: numbered ambient encounter + a seeded rare hazard roll on proximity; codex entry

build.title: The Jumped Seam
build.trigger: gates.claimsOnly (player owns a claim in-sector); fires while actively mining the claimed body
build.sees: Mid-cut, a jackal hull screams past and slaps a rival claim beacon onto YOUR asteroid with a harpoon. "Registered before yours expired. Check the paperwork. Oh — you can't. I have it."
build.payoff: Physically pull their beacon out (tug-of-war with their line), pay them off, or let it ride and fight a claim-defense (claim_threat script already handles the war).
build.seam: numbered file on script 'claimThreat' with beacon-as-prop and attachments tug logic; claims read via state.claims (director _gatesPass claimsOnly precedent)

build.title: The Credible Loss
build.trigger: posted by a named wealthy pilot after any race the player wins; uniqueOnce
build.sees: A rich kid's offer, itemized: race my autopilot, lose by less than a length, no crashes, one take. "Father thinks the ship is cursed. It is not cursed. It is embarrassing. Fix the STORY." The contract's success condition is a photo finish you must lose on purpose.
build.payoff: A race scored in reverse; throw it cleanly (harder than winning) for triple pay, or win honestly and double the insult (he doubles your fee out of respect).
build.seam: race mission with inverted scoring bands (rewards on near-miss); autopilot rival via fixed-line AI (combatDoctrine)

build.title: The Requiem For A Tool
build.where: bar of station_forge, at shift bell
build.trigger: first dock after a choir Bell shatter event has destroyed player-placed crystal chains (choir runtime receipt)
build.sees: the foundry crews hold a two-minute standdown for a cutter that finally lost a tooth to crystal shrapnel. It gets named, posthumously, with full honors: "CUTTER 12: IT CUT WHAT IT WAS POINTED AT. EVERY TIME. THAT IS A LIFE." The tooth is retired to the bar's mantel.
build.payoff: pure DMC/Choir collision comedy; codex page "Cutter 12"; flag `cutter12`.
build.seam: bar event keyed to choir:bellPulse receipts; codex overlay

build.title: Ember Trail
build.trigger: after event — any Plunge breakup (existing commit/breakup heat path)
build.sees: the destroyed hull's largest fragments continue along the tangent as glowing embers, drawing a slowly cooling dotted line across the storm band for two minutes — the crash becomes a legible trajectory you can follow to the salvage.
build.payoff: visual wonder only; gameplay-honest (the embers ARE the wreck marker).
build.seam: `emitDestructionLightBeats` + wreck handoff already in `src/render/vfx.js` subscriptions (`entity:killed`); a data row extends the ember lifetime by death tier (`DEATH_MASS_TIER_THRESHOLDS`).

build.title: The Frozen Watch
build.trigger: proximity to a specific cold-drift hull; uniqueOnce
build.sees: A military hull, powered, intact, and four degrees above vacuum — her bridge crew still at stations, frozen mid-shift, watches still on wrists, coffee still in the cup. Nothing killed them. Something turned the heat off and left. The log's last entry is a routine requisition.
build.payoff: The soberest codex page in the game; delivering the crew's effects to their faction's office opens one quiet dialogue that never mentions it again.
build.seam: numbered ambient encounter with an interior-read scan sequence; faction dialogue via barContacts pattern (src/ui/station/barContacts.js — DIRTY; prefer comms popup)

build.title: Festival Bunting
build.trigger: sim-time — festival days (the seven dayOfYear rows in worldCalendar)
build.sees: strings of colored lamps run between the station's spines — each festival its own color scheme (Founders' Day white, Ring Fair mixed trading-house colors, Quiet Night none at all) — and at night watch they carry the whole silhouette. Cheap, human, visible from a mile.
build.payoff: visual wonder only; a calendar you can see.
build.seam: lamp strings as Forge emissive finishes (variant finish idiom from `src/data/lampChannels.js`) toggled by festival predicate.

build.title: The Perishable Sprint
build.trigger: posted when colony food stock hits a seeded low; visible to all, first-come
build.sees: A colony's agri-dome had a blower failure. The station posts a produce run at triple rate, the produce visibly frosts as the clock runs, and every hull in the sector hears the same posting at the same moment.
build.payoff: Triple-rate delivery inside the window; the colony's stock levels (visible on the market) actually recover; latecomers sell at normal rate to a grateful-but-broke dome.
build.seam: economyContracts delivery with a real decay on commodity state (economyCycles); DIRTY-adjacent files — fallback: numbered encounter with deadlineS

build.title: The Interest
build.trigger: fires 10+ sector-days after any refused bargain (persisted refusal record); uniqueOnce per bargain
build.sees: The counterpart from a deal you refused weeks ago finds you — not hostile, just thorough: "You said no. Fair. I've had time to think about why, and I've raised the offer, and I've brought the thing you'd have needed to do it safely. I want this DONE."
build.payoff: The same deal, matured: better terms, real safety included, and a counterpart who has earned the yes; refuse again and they finally, gracefully, accept it — as a person would.
build.seam: refusal records in story.flags; matured-deal numbered encounter; graceful exit flag

build.title: The Notary
build.trigger: dock presence; one offer per deed type (rescue, kill, delivery, refusal); repeats per type
build.sees: A notary drone offers, in perfect legalese, to witness anything: "Your next deed, whatever it is, witnessed and sealed. Witnessed deeds are... different. Ask anyone who has one." The fee is trivial. The drone has witnessed eleven thousand deeds and been thanked by none of them, professionally.
build.payoff: Each witnessed deed type pays its rep once at double weight (the seal makes it official); the notary's ledger of your witnessed deeds is a codex page you can read any time, stamped and dull and wonderful.
build.seam: dock comms offer + a witnessed flag per deed type read at outcome time; ledger in codexPages.js

build.title: The Chalk
build.trigger: persists along routes the player has flown 5+ times; updates on pass
build.sees: Your regular route has developed chalk: marks on the rocks you pass — a tally of your passes, a correction arrow where you once drifted wide, and, on the worst corner, a small, professionally painted sign that just says "AGAIN?" Nobody signs the chalk. Everybody adds to it.
build.payoff: The route remembers you in the world's own handwriting; the marks are persistent, the corrections are real (they mark actual hazards), and the tally increments forever.
build.seam: route-pass counter + persistent chalk props along the lane (story props); hazard data from your actual collision/drift records
hones: (a) one authored lane with flag-gated tallies; no route-usage ledger exists
(b) one authored lane with flag-gated tallies (A H-19)
(c) ONE authored lane (the starter lane) with flag-gated tallies; there is no route-usage ledger and building one for chalk is not worth it.

build.title: The Slurry Relic's Contents
build.trigger: scan the relic after sampling any slurry cargo (commodity context flag)
build.sees: the relic's scan returns composition: "SLURRY, REFINED, BATCH R3-CARRIER. CONTAINER: R3-CARRIER GRID, PANEL 9." Panel 9 of the grid shelved in Helios Bay 7 has been here, full, for fourteen years — the only panel that left the warehouse, and it left as a container, not cargo.
build.payoff: the wrong-grid reveal gains a physical middle chapter; flag `panel9_found`; codex page "Panel Nine."
build.seam: commodity-context scan + codex overlay + Bay 7 thread flags

build.title: The Homecoming Bell
build.trigger: first re-entry to the starter sector after 20+ sector-days away (persisted absence record)
build.sees: The starter beacon rings your arrival home the way it rings nothing else — a pattern the old-timers on the band notice immediately ("someone's come back"), because the pattern is reserved for hulls that left and made it. The tutorial beacon, which taught you the throttle, has one extra line it saved for exactly this.
build.payoff: A two-line homecoming from the game's first voice; the pattern is permanent, and rings differently for hulls that left and hulls that left and got rich.
build.seam: absence record + beacon bark pattern; lines in ENCOUNTER_BARKS

build.title: The Burn Claim Pin's Flame
build.trigger: jettison any fuel cells within 100 WU of the stake (an offering, mechanically)
build.sees: the cells ignite mid-drift — the stake's pilot flame catches them — and the flame grows one color hotter for the rest of the day. The band explains in eleven separate voices: "The burn gets fed." "The burn gets fed." "Nobody who feeds the burn has ever died on this rock." The statistics, checked later, are accurate.
build.payoff: flag `burn_fed`; one real safety buff on that rock (fuel-efficiency in its gravity well) for the day; codex page "Feed The Burn."
build.seam: jettison-ignite interaction + flame dressing + codex overlay

build.title: The Wrong Way
build.trigger: posted at the stream mouth during drift season; repeatable
build.sees: The debris stream flows one way at a walking pace, and the locals race it wrong-way — upstream through the grains, drafting between the big rocks where the current slackens, for a purse paid by the salvors who want the stream mapped at speed.
build.payoff: A course that is also a survey: your run produces a real, sellable map of the stream's slow lanes; the map makes the upstream route permanently faster for everyone.
build.seam: race mission + a persisted map record consumed by navigation (mapWorkbench reads a flag); salvor pool via d.grant

build.title: The Hum
build.trigger: proximity to a specific ancient wreck; scan gate requires 3+ close passes; uniqueOnce
build.sees: The wreck hums — a low, structural tone that only resolves into the whisper-pool's cadence when you hold scan on it across three passes. It is not broadcasting. It is resonating, at the exact interval of the voices, as if the whispers come FROM hulls like this one, all of them, everywhere.
build.payoff: The whisper's source mystery deepens productively: a codex entry that reframes every prior whisper as fleet-wide, plus one new whisper line only readable here.
build.seam: numbered anomaly encounter with requiredPings pattern (140-unique-wreck-deepsurvey-ping-elite.js precedent); whisper line added to WHISPER_LINES

build.title: The Quiet Mast's Silence Toll
build.trigger: transmit three hails within 60 seconds near the mast (chatter detection)
build.sees: the mast dampens the player's channel — not jamming, editing: the player's third hail plays back with all filler words removed. "TRANSMISSION: EDITED. CONTENT: PRESERVED. THE MAST PREFERS YOU." The mast's preference is permanent and takes the form of every future hail costing 20% less airtime.
build.payoff: flag `mast_prefers_you`; codex page "The Mast Prefers You."
build.seam: chatter-rate check + hail audio variant + codex overlay
hones: (a) drop the fake airtime mechanic; payoff is the first-ping register payoff + band priority greeting (mine + C)
(b) register payoff: hails resolve on the first ping and pilots notice; no airtime exists (A+C)
(c) There is no airtime resource — the payoff is the edited-hail audio variant plus a band-priority greeting; other pilots notice.

build.title: The Bet
build.trigger: seeded twice per sector week; plays out over three stations as the player travels
build.sees: Two haulers are having an argument on the open band about whether the Ceres queue or the Forge queue moves faster, with money on it, and the argument is STRUCTURED: each station visit adds a measurement, both cite sources, one of them is increasingly obviously wrong. You can settle it (they ask the nearest neutral hull — you) at the third stop.
build.payoff: Judge correctly (a cut of the pot, two named acquaintances) or get it wrong (they're gracious; the belt notices); the bet's result is on the news wire either way.
build.seam: scripted comms arc keyed to station-visit events (docking hooks); judgment via comms choice; pot via d.grant

build.title: The Wrong Shadow
build.trigger: sim-time — third watch of day 33 (The Pale Holiday), once
build.sees: the Anvil's shadow stretches across the belt pointing away from the sun — backward — for exactly one watch. Hulls inside the false shadow keep normal light; only the belt's dust goes dark. Void_signal's violet rim bleeds faintly onto everything the shadow touches.
build.payoff: plus codex entry (anomaly); Pale Holiday tie ("signals run strange").
build.seam: one-watch rig overlay (ambient dim + violet rim) via the look-lerp path keyed by the festival row in `src/data/worldCalendar.js`.
hones: (a) one-watch rig overlay via the corrected mood-overlay seam; the Pale Holiday canon sanction stands
(b) one-watch rig overlay via the corrected mood-overlay seam (A H-32)
(c) One-watch rig overlay via the mood path — and for the record: resolveLookPost exists (lookMoods.js:339); the Pale Holiday’s “signals run strange” already sanctions the effect.

build.title: The Choir Tender's Lullaby
build.where: sector_helios_prime, near the choir tender derelict (poi_helios_choir_tender)
build.trigger: proximity during the tender's scheduled hymn (worldCalendar window)
build.sees: the dead tender's bell rings one note — a wreck with no crew, no power, one note per day — and every Choir hull in three sectors answers it in harmony, mid-shift, no explanation filed. The note is a lullaby's first note. The tender was a hospital ship before it was a wreck.
build.payoff: codex page "The Hospital Bell"; Choir standing +2; the note's pitch varies by day-seed but always resolves the same.
build.seam: calendar audio event + harmony response + codex overlay

build.title: The Tower's Favorites
build.trigger: after 10+ dockings at the same station (persisted counter)
build.sees: Traffic control has developed opinions. "Helios Tower to hull 4471-T: welcome back. Berth 12, as usual. Try not to dent 12." Then, months in, the one day you dock sloppily, the whole approach goes quiet, and the tower says only: "...noted." The regulars on the band enjoyed that.
build.payoff: A relationship that costs nothing and reads everywhere: favorites get berth preference (a real, small docking speed-up), slobs get the far berth and public numbers.
build.seam: dock-count flags per station; tower lines via dockingCorridor/barkDirector seams (src/systems/dockingCorridor.js)

build.title: The Misdeclared Freight
build.trigger: scan the misdeclared freight after the player has hauled any sealed-alloy contract (campaign context)
build.sees: the freight's seal is Kessler's scale-stamp — the exact stamp, one scale, one clerk, nineteen years. The freight is not contraband; it is a surprise: alloy ordered in secret by someone's crew fund, misdeclared to dodge the desk fee, delivered to the wrong bay on the day everything stopped. The waybill's last line is unfinished: "FOR —"
build.payoff: deliver it to the pit line (poi_helios_pit_line) as-is: the crew fund's beneficiary is found (a retired scale clerk), the delivery completes a nineteen-year-old order, Tycho standing +5, codex page "For —".
build.seam: scan context + delivery mission + codex overlay

build.title: The Band Survey
build.trigger: offered at station_customs during any storm season; requires dropping one buoy at each band edge (reentry/danger/skim/sling from `PLANET_SITE.bands`)
build.sees: each buoy lights when its boundary's hysteresis band crosses it — the planet's regions made visible as four standing rings of lamps. The last buoy's light lands on the first's and the four rings pulse once, together.
build.payoff: plus codex entry (planetary band map) + small bonus.
build.seam: `src/data/landmarkMissions.js` row family + beacon props (existing `place_lane_beacon`); band predicates from `src/data/planets.js`.

build.title: The Welding Constellation
build.trigger: sim-time — third watch only
build.sees: at night watch a lone construction frame's welding drones work in a pattern that, watched from the right bearing, reads as a recognizable constellation's dots — the drones are (obviously, on inspection) just following the frame's weld schedule. The frame's plate calls it "the sky we came from."
build.payoff: plus codex entry; discoverable only at third watch from the marked bearing.
build.seam: everyday-kit frame + drone flash timings hashed to match the pattern (pure data); the bearing is a data row.

build.title: The Broadcast Will
build.trigger: seeded death event at a remote site; fires once per run
build.sees: A dying captain wills his ship live on the band — "to the nearest hull with a clean registry, no offense" — and the nearest hull, per the actual sensor math, is you, while four other hulls dispute the math and one of them starts moving with intent.
build.payoff: An inheritance with contest attached: claim it (a real ship, a real fight, a real registry battle at the dock) or refuse on-band (the will names you as the witness instead, which pays nothing and changes how executors treat you forever).
build.seam: numbered selfRegistered encounter computing the actual nearest hull; ship grant as disabled entity (1210 pattern); contest fight

build.title: The Drill Choir
build.trigger: sim-time — mining watch start, one bass note per drill in launch sequence
build.sees: the refinery's line of six seam drills spins up in sequence — each starter throwing a light beat and a bass note a fifth below the last, so the line plays a rising chord as it comes to life. By the sixth drill the chord fills the sector; when the watch ends they fall silent in reverse.
build.payoff: visual wonder only; the most musical machine in the belt.
build.seam: machine ignition lights (`miningContact` row) + one chord recipe composed of six `ambient_machine_*`-style oscillators in `src/data/audioRecipes.js`.
hones: (a) rename "The Drill Chord" - the Ascendant Choir keeps its word (adopted from C)
(b) rename "The Drill Chord" (C)
(c) Rename “The Drill Chord” — the Ascendant Choir keeps its word; the rising fifth stays.

build.title: The Rival's Round
build.trigger: after Coldburn Rey has been beaten (deed memory: race/escort win vs the named rival)
build.sees: Rey is at the rail, buying. For everyone. Including the player. "Cheapest lesson I ever bought. You flew the line I should have. First round is tuition." Everyone in the bar gets one drink; nobody mentions the race again, which is how you know it mattered.
build.payoff: Rey becomes a recurring friendly rival (follow-up races with real stakes); flag `rey_tuition`; free drinks at that bar for the session.
build.seam: barContacts canonical contact keyed to rival deed; follow-up offers via the mission board

build.title: The Concord Form That Files You Back
build.trigger: the player files 20+ of any form-like transaction (surveys, claims, bounty submissions)
build.sees: CONCORD RECORDS: "NOTICE OF RECIPROCAL FILING: YOUR PATTERNS HAVE BEEN FILED AS A FORM. FORM NUMBER ASSIGNED: 44-C-P[day]. YOU ARE NOW CITABLE." Other clerks start citing the player by form number in unrelated correspondence.
build.payoff: flag `player_is_a_form`; every future Concord letter cites the player's form number in the header; pure recursive-bureaucracy delight.
build.seam: mail.js header variant keyed to flag; counter in receipts

build.title: The Pulse Seam
build.trigger: posted at a Veil station after the player survives one hazard pulse inside the field
build.sees: A survey company posts the impossible job: the sector's richest seam sits inside a radiation pocket that pulses on a fixed clock. Every miner who tried mined between pulses and died between pulses. The clock is public. The rhythm is learnable.
build.payoff: Mine the seam on the pulse's timing (hold-and-dash loops); payout scales with purity; the company's gratitude is real and priced (module discount).
build.seam: hazard-window mining contract (uniqueWrecks timingGate precedent, src/data/uniqueWrecks.js); reward via economyTerms

build.title: The Ash Pin's Second Age
build.where: sector_helios_prime / sector_ceres_belt, both ash pins (poi_helios_ash_pin, poi_ceres_ash_pin)
build.trigger: visit both ash pins in the same in-game week
build.sees: the pins are a pair — same stake design, same paint batch, same era — one in Helios, one in Ceres, marking the same incident from two ends. Reading both gives the full text neither holds alone. The middle of the text, the part neither pin carries, is the part everyone remembers and no one wrote down.
build.payoff: codex page "The Two Pins" (the middle line is the player's own campaign thread number); flag `pins_paired`.
build.seam: two-visit flag + combined codex overlay

build.title: The Choir's Silent Shift
build.trigger: a Choir bell's pulse period coincides with a sector-wide maintenance bell (two calendar events, once per game)
build.sees: for exactly one pulse, every machine in the sector stops — bells, foundries, tugs — a held breath across the whole field. Then everything resumes mid-note. The Choir calls it the Silent Shift. Nobody else calls it anything; most pilots have never seen one, which is the point.
build.payoff: pure physics-as-liturgy spectacle; flag `silent_shift_seen`; codex page "The Silent Shift."
build.seam: calendar-window pause cue via choir:bellPulse + worldCalendar hook; codex overlay

build.title: The Tailings Fire
build.trigger: proximity to a miner camp after a seeded misfire event; cooldownS 86400
build.sees: A volatile tailings heap has self-ignited next to a three-habitat camp and the camp's own tug is too small to move it. The burning pile is drifting — slowly, at walking pace — toward the habitats. You have maybe four minutes and one very useful massline.
build.payoff: Tow or shove the pile clear before it cooks the camp (physics rescue, triumphant); the camp's gratitude is a permanent dock discount and the best fuel in the belt.
build.seam: numbered selfRegistered encounter with a burning prop on a real drift vector; fire prop via vfx-adjacent story props; rescue via massline physics

build.title: The Ring Rules
build.trigger: proximity to a fixed dueling ring rock; any hostile commander present; cooldownS 7200
build.sees: A circle of rocks with a physical PD-screen boundary (331-pd-screen-wall.js's tech, repurposed) and a posted rule in three languages: one hull each, inside the ring, anything goes, nobody's friends intervene. A Reach commander is already inside, waiting for someone worth the fuel.
build.payoff: An honest 1v1 with a real purse; win inside the ring and even their pack respects it (a chalk on the ring's tally); win by cheating (escorts, mines) and every pack in the sector treats it as a debt.
build.seam: numbered selfRegistered encounter with a pd_screen boundary prop and single-spawn rule; purse via d.grant

build.title: The Bond Audit
build.trigger: the clamp holds the player's hull (the tethys rumor's hazard) while the player is fully lawful — zero flags, zero contraband, zero debt
build.sees: the clamp inspects a perfect record and does not know what to do: "MANIFEST: CLEAN. SEAL: TRUE. DEBT: NONE. ANOMALY. ESCALATING TO SUPERVISOR. SUPERVISOR: YOU. SELF-AUDIT: [STAMP]." The clamp releases the player with an apology in triplicate.
build.payoff: the triplicate apology is an inventory item; presenting it at any desk waives one future clerical delay; flag `clamped_the_clamp`.
build.seam: clamp hold check + lawful-state read + item

build.title: The Grease Menu
build.trigger: first dock with heat > 20
build.sees: the barkeep's slate has a second column headed "GREASE": small fixed-price services that legally do not exist — "REGISTRY GREASE (ONE SCAN, CLEAN)," "TOW REMEMBERED (NO QUESTIONS)," "A NAME, SPOKEN QUIETLY." Each purchase is real; each receipt is verbal.
build.payoff: three purchasable one-shot services (heat -5 once; one impound waived; one fence discount); codex page "The Second Column."
build.seam: barContacts purchase options keyed to heat; service effects via existing law/impound seams

build.title: The Relay Chain
build.trigger: 2 sector-days after any completed rescue (priorOutcome on distress); uniqueOnce per chain
build.sees: A mayday comes in, and the voice is one of the crew you saved last week — different ship, different sector, same luck. "I know. I KNOW. It's not a curse, it's a franchise. Please."
build.payoff: Second rescue earns a permanent crew discount from their employer (a real dock discount), and the radio traffic between rescues starts treating you as their personal roadside service.
build.seam: numbered selfRegistered encounter with gates.requiresCompletedShape on distress outcome 'rescued'; roster memory via state.story.flags

build.title: The Last Shift Witness
build.trigger: after the player has read the Last Shift evidence (doss_ceres_last_shift flag), any Ceres bar regular asks the player directly
build.sees: "You read the shift report. You are one of maybe five living hulls who has. Read it to the yard, out loud, at the bell. The dead worked there. The yard should hear its own name said right." The job: one reading, one bell, no fee, no receipt — the payoff is that the yard's night crew starts leaving one light on for the shift that never clocked out.
build.payoff: flag `last_shift_read_aloud`; the yard's night light becomes permanent dressing; DMC standing +6; codex page "Said Right."
build.seam: doss flag read + bell-window interaction + dressing state + codex overlay

build.title: The Impound Grudge Interview
build.trigger: the player's hull appears on the impound grudge ledger (impoundGrudge system holds a grudge) and the player approaches the shelf
build.sees: the shelf has a slot prepared for the player's hull — labeled, dated, one size too generous. "WE PREPARE FOR EVERYONE. MOST NEVER EARN IT. YOUR SLOT IS THE CORRECT SIZE FOR WHO YOU WILL BE IF YOU KEEP FLYING LIKE THIS. IT IS A COMPLIMENT AND A WARNING AND WE DO NOT DIFFERENTIATE."
build.payoff: clearing the grudge (settling the underlying fine) removes the slot and replaces it with the player's callsign in the "CLEARED" column, which is shorter and prouder; flag `slot_cleared`.
build.seam: impoundGrudge state read (src/systems/impoundGrudge.js) + shelf dressing + flag

build.title: The Courier's Ghost Run
build.trigger: the player accepts any courier contract while their transponder history shows they have flown that exact lane 10+ times (pattern match)
build.sees: the courier job brief appends one personal note from the dispatcher: "You know this lane better than the manifest does. Fly it from memory, not from the plot. If your wake matches the chart exactly, the lane learns nothing. If it doesn't, you are late. Be neither."
build.payoff: flying the lane with any deviation (within tolerance) pays a "memory bonus" — the dispatcher's trust flag unlocks their best contracts permanently; flag `lane_from_memory`.
build.seam: lane-history read + deviation check + contract unlock flag
hones: (a) keyed to courier contracts completed in-sector (deed counter); no lane-history ledger exists
(b) key to courier contracts completed in-sector (A H-28)
(c) Key to courier contracts completed in that sector (deed counter); no lane-history ledger.

build.title: The Beacon That Isn't
build.trigger: proximity — it moves 1 WU per season along a fixed line
build.sees: a navigation light of exactly the standard pattern blinks in open space, catalog-clean, no hull — and it is moving, one world-unit per season along a bearing that (plotted across visits) aims out of the sector. Cartography has flagged it and declined to follow.
build.payoff: plus codex entry; its plotted track is itself a collectible.
build.seam: lamp-finish sprite + position from a season-hash step function; the codex entry draws the track from the same pure function.

build.title: The Debt Collector's Duet
build.trigger: the player carries any unpaid debt while hailing the creditor's own hull (not the station desk — the hull)
build.sees: the creditor's hull hails back, off the record: "The desk wants the number. I want the story. You are one good story from current. Tell it." The player's next three minutes of actual flight — any maneuvering, any assist to anyone, anything the hull can witness — becomes the story; the debt clears on witness alone.
build.payoff: debt cleared for flight rather than credits, once; flag `story_current`; the creditor thereafter greets the player as "the story."
build.seam: debt-state read + witness-window check + economy debt seam
hones: (a) the witnessed story is one assist/scan/dock inside the window; open-ended maneuver watching is not judgeable
(b) the witnessed story is one assist/scan/dock inside the window (A H-29)
(c) The witnessed story = one assist/scan/dock event inside the window; open-ended maneuver watching is not judgeable.

build.title: The Bucket Line
build.trigger: fires during a seeded water-crisis week; all traffic invited on band
build.sees: A colony's reclamation loop is down and the belt improvises: a bucket line of hulls passing water tanks hand to hand up the lane to the colony, day and night, with a chalk tally on the station wall. Nobody's making money. Everyone's counting.
build.payoff: Join the line (each leg is a short real tow) for colony rep and a name on the tally wall; the tally wall persists after the crisis, listing the week's haulers forever.
build.seam: numbered repeatable tow legs + a persistent tally prop (authoredPlaces pattern); rep via d.rep to faction

build.title: Ride the Front
build.trigger: offered at station_io_merc during solar_wind weeks
build.sees: "Stay in the surge for sixty seconds and bring the wick back lit." Sixty seconds inside the visible front — streamers combed past your canopy, the hull crawling with static — then the calm hits like a door closing and the wick's blue flame stands straight up.
build.payoff: plus small bonus + codex entry (storm rider).
build.seam: `src/data/landmarkMissions.js` row with a surge-phase occupancy predicate (pure `seasonalWeatherPhase` read).

build.title: The Fire Watch
build.trigger: seeded station mishap; fires once per sector week; proximity
build.sees: A station module catches fire and the extinguisher drones' sweeps keep missing by meters in the vent wind. The station's solution over the band is dignified and desperate: "Any hull with mass assist. Push the module off the spine. We will owe you the respect of the ledger."
build.payoff: Shove the burning module clear with hull contact or a thrown mass (physics, spectacle); save the module (rep + discount) or let it torch (the station rebuilds, and mentions it).
build.seam: numbered selfRegistered encounter with a burning module prop; shove via massline/bolus force seams (src/data/bolusForces.js)

build.title: The Weathered Buoy Chain
build.trigger: always present; the chain's lamps read the current season
build.sees: five derelict weather buoys strung along the lane edge, one lamp each: amber burns during solar wind, violet during ion storm, dark when clear, all five relighting in sequence at each season turn like a wind gauge changing its mind.
build.payoff: plus codex entry; the chain becomes the sector's forecast you can see.
build.seam: `src/data/worldOneOffs.js` cluster rows + lamp channels keyed by `weatherSeasonAt` (the lamp bus accepts data-driven gain).

build.title: The Last Anvil
build.trigger: always present; hammer strokes on a fixed 9 s period
build.sees: a fully manual forge bolted to a rock: one power hammer arm, one glowing stock, a robot arm that fetches billets. The hammer falls every nine seconds with a spark crown, and has (the plate says) not stopped in thirty-one years. The sparks' light reaches the approach lane.
build.payoff: plus codex entry; a metronome landmark with a story.
build.seam: `src/data/worldOneOffs.js` row (forge donor + articulated hammer) + spark light via `miningContact` family.
hones: (a) rename "The Nine-Second Hammer" - the Anvil is Tethys's named planet (adopted from C)
(b) rename "The Nine-Second Hammer" (C)
(c) Rename “The Nine-Second Hammer” — the Anvil is Tethys’s named planet; thirty-one years at nine seconds is the landmark this is.

build.title: The Helix Invoice Poem
build.trigger: the player pays any Helix fine; every 10th fine thereafter
build.sees: the fine receipt's footer, for the 10th payment only, carries a verse: "THE FINE IS THE PRICE / OF KNOWING THE PRICE / OF THE ROAD." A Helix clerk confirms it is unauthorized and has been unauthorized for years. Removing it is "queued."
build.payoff: pure voice; flag `helix_verse`; codex page "The Queued Verse."
build.seam: fine receipt footer variant keyed to payment counter; codex overlay

build.title: The Bell Ringer's Apprentice
build.trigger: offered by the bell's keeper contact after the player witnesses one unscheduled toll
build.sees: toll the Eighth Bell in the foundry's own sequence (three, rest, one) — each correct toll lights one window row of the foundry in acknowledgment, and the completed sequence leaves the rows lit for the season. Wrong order and the bell answers itself, flat.
build.payoff: plus codex entry + a persistent small light change (the lit rows) that players will recognize.
build.seam: `src/data/landmarkMissions.js` row + lamp rows toggled via the lamp-bus gain path; audio is the existing toll recipe.

build.title: Rime Lightning
build.trigger: sim-time — hash-picked strikes during cold surges
build.sees: a pale-blue arc walks between two rocks — and freezes mid-fork for a full second, a statue of lightning, before crumbling into ice-dust. Frozen bolts persist as faint glassy traces on the rocks for minutes.
build.payoff: plus codex entry; photography moment.
build.seam: pooled arc sprite with an authored hold phase (sprite-batch vocabulary in `src/render/vfx.js`); traces via the seam-marker pipeline already exported there.
hones: (a) persistent ionized glassy traces, not a bolt frozen mid-fork - the physics truth is better than the statue (adopted from C)
(b) persistent ionized glassy traces, not a held bolt (C); you can fly the statue
(c) No bolt freezes mid-fork — the statue is the persistent ionized trace seen from distance; the hold-phase implementation is the honest version, keep the traces.

build.title: The Governor
build.trigger: sim-time — overspeed event once per season, hash-picked watch; spin-down takes 60 s
build.sees: the mining depot's flywheel governor screams over speed, sheds its safety ring (the ring tumbles away, strobing, to be recovered by a scurrying skiff), and spends a full minute visibly slowing while the yard's alarms paint it red. It settles, the ring is re-welded, the season continues.
build.payoff: visual wonder only; a machine failure with a full arc and no casualties.
build.seam: `spawnCauseFragment` (safety-ring shard) + alarm lamp channel via lamp-bus; all pooled.

build.title: The Muster
build.trigger: fires once per seeded sector week at a fixed rock; proximity; cooldownS 86400
build.sees: Forty wasp swarmers drilling in silent formation grids around a dead carrier hull, reliefs cycling through a breach every thirty seconds — a pirate fleet doing PT. Nobody hails you. They are busy.
build.payoff: Pure spectacle; scanning the carrier yields a codex entry on how Reach packs actually work (mostly logistics).
build.seam: numbered ambient encounter (tier 'ambient', deck 'civilian', noCombat) spawning a large cheap wasp grid via d.spawnShips
hones: (a) cap the drill grid at 12-16 drones with a bounded window; forty live hulls breaks the ambient spawn budget
(b) cap 12-16 drones in a bounded window; the PT image survives the cap
(c) Cap the drill grid at 12-16 drones with a bounded window; forty live hulls in formation breaks the ambient spawn budget.

build.title: The Foundry Bell
build.trigger: sim-time — struck once at each shift turn
build.sees: a cast bell the size of a cargo pod hangs from the forge gantry; at each shift turn a robot arm strikes it once — a single deep note that rolls across the yard and (because the yard is full of plates and tanks) returns a two-second echo from three directions.
build.payoff: plus codex entry; the station's heartbeat, audible from the approach.
build.seam: audio:cue with the toll recipe pitched down + spatial echo via two delayed cues (the audio bus supports positioned, ducked cues).

build.title: The Lightning Catcher
build.trigger: sim-time — during ion surges, the named mast draws one bolt every ~45 s
build.sees: the forge's comm mast gathers a crawling glow, then takes the strike — the bolt's light visibly lands on the mast's neighbors and every hull parked on the apron, throwing sharp transient shadows. A safe distance away it is the best show in the sector.
build.payoff: visual wonder only; pairs with the doubled apron lights of SP3-056.
build.seam: event-light pool (`explosionIgnition` row) + mast geometry from the existing everyday-kit (`place_sensor_mast`); all existing parts.

build.title: Market Day Rush
build.trigger: sim-time — each station's market day (already hashed per berth), the 90 s rush windows
build.sees: the apron comes alive: shuttle swarms in lamp-trails queue on the approach, container racks shuffle on their crawlers, and the station's window rows brighten a step. From the lane it reads as one organism breathing faster.
build.payoff: visual wonder only; the economy made visible from outside.
build.seam: `calendar:rushHour` hook (already emitted by worldClock) + traffic thickening + apron streaks (`spawnStationSideEventStreak`).

build.title: The Yard Family Reunion
build.trigger: the player arrives while carrying any hull part/cargo stamped from a Pitborn yard (provenance check)
build.sees: the anchorage's cull channel erupts: the part the player carries was welded by someone's mother. The whole yard turns out, every hull running its work lights, and the crowd (all of them) rates the player's approach — the Cull meter, repurposed as applause. "COUNT 'EM" is sung once, at the player, in the good way.
build.payoff: flag `yard_reunion`; Pitborn standing +8; the part's provenance stamp gains a signature.
build.seam: provenance read + cull-meter crowd cue + flag

build.title: The Echo Bank
build.trigger: proximity at a seeded rotation angle; fires with ≥60min of player comms history in the save
build.sees: A crystalline debris cluster that stores comm traffic in its lattice and replays it — years old, other hulls' arguments, a station's last night shift — and then, once, your own voice, from hours ago, saying something you'd forgotten typing. The bank does not care that it's unsettling. It is a bank.
build.payoff: One replay of the player's own actual past line per visit window (persisted record), plus a codex entry on who built a memory bank and why they needed receipts.
build.seam: numbered anomaly encounter recording comms:popup payloads to story.flags; replay via comms:popup with lag; codex in src/data/codexPages.js
hones: (a) bounded 5-entry comms replay buffer; no full history store exists
(b) bounded 5-line comms replay buffer (A H-09)
(c) Bounded ring buffer — persist the last 5 comms popup payloads for replay, not a full comms history store (none exists).

build.title: The Sails Take the Wind
build.trigger: sim-time — solar_wind weeks; the orchard's sails respond to the gust profile
build.sees: the orchard's farm sails (the gust profile already authored in `ANVIL_ORCHARD_GUST_PROFILE`) visibly billow and yaw through the front, throwing moving shade patterns across the pod rows beneath. In calm they hang slack. The wind is visible because something is rigged to catch it.
build.payoff: visual wonder only; the orchard becomes a weather dial.
build.seam: `src/data/anvilOrchardBody.js` sail articulation + the existing gust profile; presentation only, no sim change.

build.title: The Verge Pilgrims
build.trigger: sim-time — Pale Holiday (dayOfYear 33), one crossing
build.sees: a candle-chain of small ships crosses toward the Veil's deep field — one lamp each, no formation discipline, some old and slow — observing the holiday nobody scheduled. Falling out of the chain is not an insult; rejoining is expected. At the far marker they all flash once and go dark for a minute.
build.payoff: plus codex entry; escorting the full crossing is its own receipt.
build.seam: lane-contact convoy on a festival gate + the lamp floor/dark mechanics of SP3-103/106.

build.title: The Prism Read
build.trigger: proximity to the prism field with running lights on
build.sees: The prism field splits your running lights into a long spectrum fan, and the Vergers read the fan like a mood ring — hull by hull, they'll tell you what your light says ("exhausted, well-fed, recently paid, afraid of checkpoints") and they are right, because it is literally your power budget, refracted.
build.payoff: One honest reading per visit (your real systems, poetically described); adjusting your fit changes the reading, which is how locals check each other's hulls without asking.
build.seam: numbered ambient encounter reading power/fit state; fan vfx via light behavior; readings as barks

build.title: The Storm Riders' Shrine
build.trigger: always present; one ribbon per survived season, seeded from the sector's weather history
build.sees: an antenna mast on the lane-side rock, ribbons tied to it — one per season the lane has survived, color-coded to the season kind, the oldest bleached grey. In wind they all stream one way; new pilots add theirs (a small lamp ignites on the mast).
build.payoff: plus codex entry; a place that remembers the weather.
build.seam: `src/data/worldOneOffs.js` row (`place_memorial_array` donor) + ribbon count read from the seasonal ledger (seeded, deterministic).

build.title: The Crusher Trail
build.trigger: sim-time — after each shift change, proximity 400 WU of the approach lane
build.sees: a yard tug drags a boulder bigger than itself down the refinery approach, its massline drawn bar-taut and singing, rock dust shedding behind. Give way or get swept; cut the line and the boulder rolls free and everyone on the channel has opinions.
build.payoff: visual wonder only; the massline made visible as industry.
build.seam: NPC job runtime (hauler jobs, saveVersion v12) with a massline-attached load; taut-line presentation already exists (`MONOFILAMENT_BLADE_TAUT_RATIO` in `src/render/vfx.js`).

build.title: The Clockwork Yard
build.trigger: always present; every machine on the same 60 s metronome, all out of phase
build.sees: a yard where nothing idles: presses, cranes and turntables all run a visible 60-second metronome, deliberately phase-shifted so at any moment exactly one machine is at its peak stroke. Watch a full minute and you can predict which one fires next. Nobody remembers who set the phase.
build.payoff: plus codex entry; the pleasure of a learnable rhythm.
build.seam: everyday-kit machines with simTime-mod-60 articulation (deterministic phase per machine id hash); no sim cost.

build.title: The Cold Drill Four Broadcast
build.trigger: hold position within 400 WU during the deep-night shift
build.sees: the derelict drill's PA crackles into a shift-change roll call for a crew that has not assembled in years: "COLD FOUR, NIGHT WATCH: REPORT. ... REPORT. ... ALL POSITIONS NOTED AS PRESENT. GOOD WATCH." The roll call is 100% faithful to the original audio, including the pause where the last name should be.
build.payoff: pure ghost-frequency flavor; flag `cold_four_rollcall`; codex page "Good Watch."
build.seam: PA audio row keyed to proximity + shift phase; codex overlay

build.title: The 500th Rock
build.where: any sector (one per sector, seeded position in each rock field)
build.trigger: proximity — mining beam contact
build.sees: one rock in every sector's field carries a small painted "500" and a tally of forty strokes under it. Strike it and it rings (SP3-146's mechanic) with a pitch that is — the codex confirms when you've found all ten — one note of a ten-note scale. The belt is an instrument; the campaign left it tuned.
build.payoff: plus codex entry (collecting all ten completes the scale page).
build.seam: seeded rock flag in the field draw stream (the scatter-salt idiom from `src/data/opticStructures.js`) + strike pitch from sector index; data+glue.
hones: (a) attribute the painted 500s in-world - a survey mark, one person's decade project - and the meta voice becomes a story (adopted from C)
(b) attribute the painted 500s in-world — a survey mark, one person's decade project (C)
(c) Attribute the painted 500s in-world — a survey mark, the Tally, one person’s decade project; “the campaign left it tuned” is a meta voice and one attribution turns the joke into a story.

build.title: The Dione Customs Coin
build.trigger: the player settles a two-lien container dispute (the dione_customs rumor's ropeable bulk container) honestly — both liens paid
build.sees: customs stamps a single physical coin — real inventory item — "ONE (1) HULL SETTLED TWO (2) LIENS. THIS COIN IS LEGAL NOWHERE AND VALID EVERYWHERE." Any future lien dispute the player witnesses can be ended by presenting the coin (one use, then the coin is retired, drilled, and nailed to the customs hall wall with the player's callsign).
build.payoff: a one-use dispute-ender item that becomes a permanent wall fixture; codex page "The Coin"; customs standing +4.
build.seam: cargo/item + lien system interaction + wall-dressing persistence; codex overlay
hones: (a) the coin waives the authored Dione dispute once and becomes wall dressing; no generic lien system exists
(b) scope to the authored Dione dispute once; no generic lien system (A H-26)

build.title: The Gate Sprint
build.trigger: posted during scheduled traffic lulls (seeded); repeatable weekly
build.sees: Two stations, one gate, and an unofficial lunchtime tradition: the gate sprint. Traffic control pretends not to see it and issues a formal advisory about "recreational velocity." The purse is small, the bragging is eternal, and the safety record is, frankly, remarkable.
